The long fibers show reasonably perfect extinction with indices in the range 1.53-1.58. The interference colors are low first-order, and the sign of elongation is positive.

records.microscopy description: In most samples, these transparent, colorless to light yellow fibers will have originated from paper or paper products. Whole tapered fibers are 20-27 µm wide and 0.75-1.14 mm long.
records.Extended description: In most samples, these transparent, colorless to light yellow fibers will have originated from paper or paper products. This sample is distinguished as nonconiferous, or hardwood, by the large baggy cells or vessel elements (001010, 001011) with sometimes as many as ten rows of pits and by Hat, tapering fibers without pits (001010). Mechanical treatment is indicated by the ripped and tomfibers and by the irregular fragments and bundles of ligninrich fibers (011001, 011011). Especially characteristic of mechanical pulping operations are the medullary rays crossing other fibers at right angles. This sample is aspen (Populus tremuloides). Whole tapered fibers are 20-27 µm wide and 0.75-1.14 mm long. The pitting of these vessels is characteristically alternate. The large baggy cells show undulose extinction. The long fibers show reasonably perfect extinction with indices in the range 1.53-1.58. The interference colors are low first-order, and the sign of elongation is positive.

records.microscopy description: In most samples, these transparent, colorless fibers will have originated from paper or paper products. Large, flat, baggy cells with multiple transverse rows of pits, often more readily observed between crossed polars (001011). Long, tapered cells of polygonal cross section showing nodes, polarization colors into low second-order and parallel extinction (001001). The refractive indices vary considerably in the range 1.53-1.58, but all elongated fibers have positive elongation.
records.Extended description: In most samples, these transparent, colorless fibers will have originated from paper or paper products. This sample is distinguished as nonconiferous, or hardwood, by the characteristic cells: 1. Large, flat, baggy cells with multiple transverse rows of pits, often more readily observed between crossed polars (001011). 3. Long, tapered cells of polygonal cross section showing nodes, polarization colors into low second-order and parallel extinction (001001). That the fibers have been separated chemically is indicated by the long, unabraded and unbroken fibers; this also indicates that, if they are paper fibers, they have been beaten only slightly or not at all. The refractive indices vary considerably in the range 1.53-1.58, but all elongated fibers have positive elongation.

records.microscopy description: In most samples, these transparent, colorless to pale yellow fibers will have originated from paper or paper products. The fibers are 15-50 µm wide; the tracheids average 30 µm across. All elongated fibers show refractive indices in the range 1.53-1.58 with a positive sign of elongation.
records.Extended description: In most samples, these transparent, colorless to pale yellow fibers will have originated from paper or paper products. These fibers are distinguished as coniferous by the characteristic cells; see coniferous chemical wood (73). Mechanical treatment is indicated by the ripped and tom fibers and by the irregular fragments and bundles of lignin-rich fibers. Medullary rays crossing other fibers at right angles are especially characteristic of mechanical pulp (see also 70). This sample is balsam fir (Abies balsames), an unbleached groundwood. The fibers are 15-50 µm wide; the tracheids average 30 µm across. The pitted tracheids have incomplete parallel extinction with low first-order interference colors. All elongated fibers show refractive indices in the range 1.53-1.58 with a positive sign of elongation.

records.microscopy description: Longitudinal tracheids-long, tapering, flat, colorless, transparent fibers with one or two rows of pits. others are simply "needle pricks" in the cell walls.
records.Extended description: These fibers are distinguished as coniferous, or softwood, by the characteristic cells: 1. Longitudinal tracheids-long, tapering, flat, colorless, transparent fibers with one or two rows of pits. Some pits are bordered, best seen between crossed polars as a black cross; others are simply "needle pricks" in the cell walls. The interference colors are usually first-order gray (001011). 2. Long, tapering fibers, similar to tracheids but with thicker walls and therefore higher interference colors (into second-order) and good extinction. These show nodes and strikingly resemble ;ute (65) or fiax (63) (001001). 3. Short, brick-shaped cells (ray tracheids) with slanted end walls. The walls are perforated with bordered pits. The interference colors are first-order gray (001001). The extinction is parallel and almost complete. That these fibers were chemically prepared is indicated by the fact that they are separate and undamaged.

The fibers in this product are chemically separated, coniferous wood (001001, 001011). The identifying characteristics are identical to those described under coniferous chemical wood (73). The major difference is that to achieve the desirable property of softness in the product, the fibers here have been more highly treated chemically. The ends of the softwood fibers, especially, show extensive chemical damage, as do the side walls. Some fibers have been destroyed as structural elements by the pulping operation. These have lost their morphological characteristics and consist only of irregularly shaped bits of cellulose (001000).

records.microscopy description: These fibers are transparent, colorless, smooth, thin-walled, hollow cylinders, frequently seen bent over themselves. The fibers, which are sometimes flattened (001011), are unicellular hairs which taper to a rounded point at the free end and are rounded to bulbous at the point of attachment. They resemble kapok (66) but are shorter (1-1.5 cm) and narrower (8-20 µm).
records.Extended description: These fibers are transparent, colorless, smooth, thin-walled, hollow cylinders, frequently seen bent over themselves. The fibers, which are sometimes flattened (001011), are unicellular hairs which taper to a rounded point at the free end and are rounded to bulbous at the point of attachment. They resemble kapok (66) but are shorter (1-1.5 cm) and narrower (8-20 µm). Fibers filled with air appear to have thick black walls. Extinction is parallel, and the interference colors are low first-order; birefringence is about 0.01 (+).

records.microscopy description: These multicellular fibers are colorless, transparent, smooth, hollow cylinders with moderately thin walls. There are 2 (usually) to 4 longitudinal walls per fiber and alternating transverse walls 18-85 µm apart. The fiber is constricted slightly at the transverse walls. The fibers are 6-20 µm (mostly 12-14 µm) wide.
records.Extended description: These multicellular fibers are colorless, transparent, smooth, hollow cylinders with moderately thin walls. There are 2 (usually) to 4 longitudinal walls per fiber and alternating transverse walls 18-85 µm apart. The fiber is constricted slightly at the transverse walls. Air, which may become trapped against these walls, gives the appearance of black nodes. The fibers are 6-20 µm (mostly 12-14 µm) wide. Extinction is parallel but incomplete at the transverse walls. Interference colors are first-order, and the birefringence is about 0.01 (+).

records.microscopy description: These are smooth, thin-walled, hollow, flattened to in­flated cylinders tapering to rounded points at the free end. Most of the transparent, colorless fibers are straight, but many are wavy; The individual fibers average 7.5 µm in width (6-9 µm).
records.Extended description: These are smooth, thin-walled, hollow, flattened to in­flated cylinders tapering to rounded points at the free end. Most of the transparent, colorless fibers are straight, but many are wavy; there is occasional twisting and folding. In a mounting medium, the fibers are likely to contain trapped air. The individual fibers average 7.5 µm in width (6-9 µm). Extinction is parallel and nearly complete. The interference colors are low first-order with a positive sign of elongation, and refractive indices are near 1.54-1.55.

records.microscopy description: These colorless, transparent, hollow fibers are about 6 mm long and vary in width from about 14 µm at the base to 7 µm near the tip. The entire length of the stiff fiber is covered with both opposite and alternate barbs. The sharply pointed, somewhat curved barbs are about 18 µm long and 15-180 µm apart. The fiber tapers to the free end and is terminated with a sharp barb. The general line of the fiber is somewhat undulating from barb to barb rather than straight. The strong contrast is due to air within the fiber.
records.Extended description: These colorless, transparent, hollow fibers are about 6 mm long and vary in width from about 14 µm at the base to 7 µm near the tip. There are numerous heavy longitudinal striations. The entire length of the stiff fiber is covered with both opposite and alternate barbs. The sharply pointed, somewhat curved barbs are about 18 µm long and 15-180 µm apart. The fiber tapers to the free end and is terminated with a sharp barb. The general line of the fiber is somewhat undulating from barb to barb rather than straight. The strong contrast is due to air within the fiber. Extinction is parallel and incomplete. Interference colors are first-order, and the birefringence is about 0.01 (+).

records.microscopy description: The hairs from the fruit of this plant (Platanus sp.) are colorless, transparent, bamboolike segmented cylinders that terminate in a sharp point. The hairs are 5-10 µm long and 20-40 µm in diameter. The bamboolike segments are 100-400 µm long. The fiber diameter varies within each seg­ment -usually decreasing in one or two places-giving thesegment an undulating outline. There may also besharply-pointed, upward-curving, 100 µm long barbs at the nodes.
records.Extended description: The hairs from the fruit of this plant (Platanus sp.) are colorless, transparent, bamboolike segmented cylinders that terminate in a sharp point. The hairs are 5-10 µm long and 20-40 µm in diameter. The bamboolike segments are 100-400 µm long. The fiber diameter varies within each seg­ment -usually decreasing in one or two places-giving thesegment an undulating outline. The thick-walled segments are widened at the nodelike ends. There may also besharply-pointed, upward-curving, 100 µm long barbs at the nodes. The fibers appear dark due to entrapped air. Inter­ference colors are moderate first-order, and the birefrin­gence is about 0.01 (+). The hairs do not show extinction.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless stellate hairs or trichomes are found on plant leaves, stems and grasses. Different species vary greatly in color, shape, number, size and kind of fiber. Most are short (50-200 µm), hollow, tapered, usually cylindrical fibers. The unicellular hairs of Ulmus americana are 100-500+ µm long, hollow, transparent, colorless, smooth-surfaced cylinders that taper to a point at the free end. The base is round to flared and rounded; There are generally one or two curves along the thick-walled fiber.
records.Extended description: Transparent, colorless stellate hairs or trichomes are found on plant leaves, stems and grasses. Different species vary greatly in color, shape, number, size and kind of fiber. Most are short (50-200 µm), hollow, tapered, usually cylindrical fibers. The unicellular hairs of Ulmus americana are 100-500+ µm long, hollow, transparent, colorless, smooth-surfaced cylinders that taper to a point at the free end. The base is round to flared and rounded; the cross section at the point of attachment is round to triangular. There are generally one or two curves along the thick-walled fiber. The central canal is dark when filled with air and accounts for one-third the diameter (up to three-quarters the diameter at the base). Interference colors are moderate first-order. Birefringence is about 0.01 (+). The hairs show almost no extinction.

records.microscopy description: They are truncated to rounded at the free end, without tapering. The transparent fibers are orange to red-orange, but 3-5% are colorless. They have smooth, thin walls and may be round in cross section or collapsed to form a flat ribbon with many bends and curves. There may be a thin, transverse wall at 250-500 µm intervals with some increase in fiber diameter.
records.Extended description: The hairs of Aesculus hippocastanum are about 0.5-1+ mm long and 10-20µm wide. They are truncated to rounded at the free end, without tapering. The transparent fibers are orange to red-orange, but 3-5% are colorless. They have smooth, thin walls and may be round in cross section or collapsed to form a flat ribbon with many bends and curves. There may be a thin, transverse wall at 250-500 µm intervals with some increase in fiber diameter. Extinction is undulose. Moderate first-order interference colors are masked by the orange color. Birefringence is about 0.01 (-).

records.microscopy description: These unicellular, nonglandular hairs are transparent, colorless to dark yellow-orange, hollow, smooth, thin-walled cylinders that taper to a point at the free end. hairs of the lower epidermis are 340-500 µm long, more slender than those above and do not have cystoliths. They are generally straight but may be gently curved to 30-90° at the lower fifth of the fiber.
records.Extended description: These unicellular, nonglandular hairs are transparent, colorless to dark yellow-orange, hollow, smooth, thin-walled cylinders that taper to a point at the free end. Hairs of the upper epidermis are 150-220µm long and usually contain cystoliths of calcium carbonate in the enlarged basal region; hairs of the lower epidermis are 340-500 µm long, more slender than those above and do not have cystoliths. The hairs in this sample are up to 300µm long with diameters ranging from about 3µm near the tip through 12µm near the base and to as much as 45µm at the flared basal end. They are generally straight but may be gently curved to 30-90° at the lower fifth of the fiber. The extinction is parallel and incomplete. The interference colors are low first-order with a birefringence of about 0.01 (+).

records.microscopy description: These are colorless, transparent tubes (001001) which are usually seen collapsed into irregularly twisted ribbons (001011) much like cotton (59) but not so regularly and frequently twisted. The moderately thick to thick-walled fibers are more than 1 mm long and 7-18 µm wide.
records.Extended description: These are colorless, transparent tubes (001001) which are usually seen collapsed into irregularly twisted ribbons (001011) much like cotton (59) but not so regularly and frequently twisted. The moderately thick to thick-walled fibers are more than 1 mm long and 7-18 µm wide. Extinction is parallel and incomplete. The interference colors are moderate to high first-order, and the birefringence is about 0.02 (+).

records.microscopy description: These are transparent, colorless, thin-walled, short and squat hairs of Acer saccharum. They are 20-75 µm long and about 8 µm wide. The hairs taper rather abruptly to a rounded point at the free end; they are rounded to truncated at the attachment end. The hollow fibers have a rugose surface with short, wavy, longitudinal corrugations. The fibers have extremely weak, low first-order interference colors and may appear isotropic.
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless, thin-walled, short and squat hairs of Acer saccharum. They are 20-75 µm long and about 8 µm wide. The hairs taper rather abruptly to a rounded point at the free end; they are rounded to truncated at the attachment end. The hollow fibers have a rugose surface with short, wavy, longitudinal corrugations. The fibers have extremely weak, low first-order interference colors and may appear isotropic. The birefringence is about 0.005 (-) and the extinction is parallel and complete.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless stellate hairs or trichomes occur on tree leaves, stems and grasses. Different species vary greatly in color, shape, number, size and kind of fiber (80-85). Most are short (50-200 µm), hollow, tapered fibers which may be flattened or cylindrical. Three to more than 30 individual trichomes radiate from a central body to form a maple tree leaf stellate hair. In photomicrograph 85, 20 or more fibers radiate from a roughly dimpled central body.
records.Extended description: Transparent, colorless stellate hairs or trichomes occur on tree leaves, stems and grasses. Different species vary greatly in color, shape, number, size and kind of fiber (80-85). Most are short (50-200 µm), hollow, tapered fibers which may be flattened or cylindrical. Three to more than 30 individual trichomes radiate from a central body to form a maple tree leaf stellate hair. In photomicrograph 85, 20 or more fibers radiate from a roughly dimpled central body. The smooth fibers are bulbous at the point of attachment and are joined to each other near the base by weblike tissue.

records.microscopy description: The cause of the continuous striations in these transparent cylinders is evident in the cross section. This shows two to four or more smoothly rounded lobes like those of viscose rayon (102, 103), which appear in larger numbers. One should use optical sectioning to obtain a "slice" of the fiber for observation. The fibers in this sample are 20-30 µm in width. Note that the birefringence and refractive indices are among the lowest for birefringent fibers. Interference colors for 25 µm fibers are very low first-order grays.
records.Extended description: The cause of the continuous striations in these transparent cylinders is evident in the cross section. This shows two to four or more smoothly rounded lobes like those of viscose rayon (102, 103), which appear in larger numbers. One should use optical sectioning to obtain a "slice" of the fiber for observation. The striations may look like a lumen, but there is none. The fibers in this sample are 20-30 µm in width. They are "bright," i.e., they contain no delustering pigments. Extinction is parallel and complete; the indices are 1.478 (lengthwise) and 1.473 (crosswise); (+) 0.005. Note that the birefringence and refractive indices are among the lowest for birefringent fibers. Interference colors for 25 µm fibers are very low first-order grays.

records.microscopy description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders with a smooth surface. the indices may be 1.50-1.53 (length-wise) and 1.50-1.53 (crosswise), but they are usually around 1.520 (lengthwise) and 1.525 (crosswise); Interference colors for 20 µm thick fibers are low first-order gray. The fiber softens at about 240°C and decomposes without melting.
records.Extended description: Acrilan (Chemstrand Corporation) is a synthetic poly-acrylonitrile. These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders with a smooth surface. In cross section, they are round to off-round, but they sometimes show a one-sided indentation like kidney beans, especially in the coarse carpet type. This sample contains a delustering pigment. Extinction is parallel; the indices may be 1.50-1.53 (length-wise) and 1.50-1.53 (crosswise), but they are usually around 1.520 (lengthwise) and 1.525 (crosswise); (-) 0.005. Interference colors for 20 µm thick fibers are low first-order gray. The density is 1.17. The fiber softens at about 240°C and decomposes without melting. It is soluble in dimethyl formamide. The refractive indices, birefringence and sign of elongation of Orlon (88) are similar, but the two are easily distinguished by their different cross sections.

records.microscopy description: These are transparent, smooth, joined cylinder pairs, i.e., in cross section, they are shaped like a short dogbone or dumbbell. The fiber surface appears to have a center longitudinal striation; Note that the crosswise index is greater than the index parallel to the length. The interference colors for the 30 µm wide fibers in this sample are low first-order.
records.Extended description: These are transparent, smooth, joined cylinder pairs, i.e., in cross section, they are shaped like a short dogbone or dumbbell. The cross section may be deduced from the longitudinal view. The fiber surface appears to have a center longitudinal striation; this central portion will go dark, then light, respectively, below and above best focus. It is the thin portion of the cross section. The extinction is parallel and complete; the sign of elongation is negative. The indices are 1.505-1.515 (lengthwise) and 1.507-1.517 (crosswise); (-) 0.002. Note that the crosswise index is greater than the index parallel to the length. The interference colors for the 30 µm wide fibers in this sample are low first-order.

records.microscopy description: These continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders show rather deep longitudinal striations and a convoluted cross section, and, in this respect, they resemble viscose rayon (102). These 15 µm wide fibers show low first-order interference colors. The fiber burns only while kept in a flame and leaves a skeleton of white, fluffy ash.
records.Extended description: These continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders show rather deep longitudinal striations and a convoluted cross section, and, in this respect, they resemble viscose rayon (102). The latter, however, has high birefringence relative to calcium alginate which is low, 0.004 (+), with refractive indices 1.524 (lengthwise) and 1.520 (crosswise). These 15 µm wide fibers show low first-order interference colors. Extinction is parallel and complete. These fibers are metal salts of alginic acid, with a specific gravity of 1.72. The fiber burns only while kept in a flame and leaves a skeleton of white, fluffy ash. It is soluble in dilute alkalis. It is differ~ntiated from other regenerated protein fibers by absence of nitrogen, high ash content and its ready gelatinization and dissolution in sodium carbonate solution.

records.microscopy description: These are black, opaque, continuous cylinders of Pluton a high modulus, virtually pure carbon fiber of great strength made in England by Morganite Research and Development Ltd. They have a mean diameter of 7 µm and a width range of 5-10 µm.
records.Extended description: These are black, opaque, continuous cylinders of Pluton a high modulus, virtually pure carbon fiber of great strength made in England by Morganite Research and Development Ltd. These fibers are round in cross section. They have a mean diameter of 7 µm and a width range of 5-10 µm. The specific gravity is 1.6. They do not melt, but oxidize above about 400°C. In inert atmospheres, the fibers are thermally stable up to 1500°C.

records.microscopy description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders without striations or surface markings of any kind. In cross section, they are round to very slightly oval. The fibers here show numerous flattened sections like the fiber crossings of silk (56). These smoothly contoured, 11 µm wide fibers have high first-order interference colors with indices of 1.548 (lengthwise) and 1.527 (crosswise); (+) 0.034, and show some surface striations.
records.Extended description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders without striations or surface markings of any kind. In cross section, they are round to very slightly oval. The fibers here show numerous flattened sections like the fiber crossings of silk (56). These smoothly contoured, 11 µm wide fibers have high first-order interference colors with indices of 1.548 (lengthwise) and 1.527 (crosswise); (+) 0.021. Extinction is parallel and complete. Fibers of other manufacturers may have indices of 1.553 (lengthwise) and 1.519 (crosswise); (+) 0.034, and show some surface striations. Specific gravity is 1.53. Decomposes on heating; chars about 185-20D°C; burns without melting.

records.microscopy description: the surface is smooth and unmarked. These fibers are thick (300 µm), however, and show interference colors up to the fourth order. The fiber is optically negative.
records.Extended description: These are colorless, transparent, continuous cylinders of polyvinylidene chloride. In cross section, they are uniformly round; the surface is smooth and unmarked. The refractive indices both lengthwise and crosswise are 1.60-1.63 and may be very close so that the birefringence is low. These fibers are thick (300 µm), however, and show interference colors up to the fourth order. The extinction is parallel and complete. The fiber is optically negative. The unusually high specific gravity of 1.68-1.75 causes Saran to sink in carbon tetrachloride. Burns very slowly with melting; self-extinguishing leaving a hard, black, irregular bead. Shrinks at about 90°C; softens at about 115°C; melts at about 168°C.

records.microscopy description: The surface is marked by fine, short, longitudinal corrugations. These 15-18 µm wide fibers show moderate first-order interference colors, masked in this sample by the brown color.
records.Extended description: These are translucent, brown, continuous cylinders of duPont polytetrafluorethylene (PTFE). In cross section, they are round. The surface is marked by fine, short, longitudinal corrugations. The specific gravity is 2.1. The indices are very low, 1.34-1.38. These 15-18 µm wide fibers show moderate first-order interference colors, masked in this sample by the brown color. Extinction is parallel and complete. The fibers are stable to 250°C; they do not burn or melt, but char at very high temperatures. Outstanding chemical inertness; not affected by common reagents and solvents.

records.microscopy description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders with a deeply fluted surface. interference colors for 50 µm thick fibers are low first-order grays. The fiber contracts at 135-155°C, has no softening range and melts at 160°C.
records.Extended description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders with a deeply fluted surface. In cross section, they are dog-bone, peanut and three-lobed shapes. Extinction is parallel and complete; the indices are 1.535 (lengthwise) and 1.533 (crosswise); (+) 0.002. Note that the birefringence is barely evident with slightly uncrossed polars; interference colors for 50 µm thick fibers are low first-order grays. The density is 1.31. The fiber contracts at 135-155°C, has no softening range and melts at 160°C. Dynel is a modacrylic fiber (polyvinyl chloride and acrylonitrile) soluble in butyrolactone, nitromethane and acetone with warming. Orlon (88) is similar in birefringence and morphology, but the two are easily distinguished by their opposite signs of elongation.

records.microscopy description: These polypropylene fibers are colorless, transparent, smooth-walled cylinders with a diameter of 32 µm (28-38 µm) and a specific gravity of 0.90-0.92.
records.Extended description: These polypropylene fibers are colorless, transparent, smooth-walled cylinders with a diameter of 32 µm (28-38 µm) and a specific gravity of 0.90-0.92. Interference colors are high second-order and third-order with refractive indices of 1.530 (lengthwise) and 1.496 (crosswise); (+) 0.034. Extinction is parallel and complete. The fibers soften at 145-150°C and melt at 165°C; they burn with a luminous, smoky flame and leave a round, hard bead. Note the low density-less than water. It is soluble in hot, chlorinated hydrocarbons, e.g., trichlorethylene, boiling xylene and high boiling hydrocarbons.

records.microscopy description: A readily identified fiber because both refractive indices are higher than Aroclor®, > 1.8 (lengthwise) and 1.664 (cross-wise). 18-22 µm fibers show medium and high second-order colors. Other duPont Nomex fibers have indices of 1.680 (crosswise) and 1.747 (length-wise).
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless, continuous cylinders of a high temperature resistant nylon-duPont's nylon HT-1. The smooth-surfaced fibers are round in cross section. A readily identified fiber because both refractive indices are higher than Aroclor®, > 1.8 (lengthwise) and 1.664 (cross-wise). Birefringence is about 0.036 (+) or higher; 18-22 µm fibers show medium and high second-order colors. Extinction is parallel and complete. Other duPont Nomex fibers have indices of 1.680 (crosswise) and 1.747 (length-wise). Specific gravity is 1.38. Does not melt; decomposes above 370°C.

records.microscopy description: These smooth, continuous, transparent cylinders are round in cross section. The fibers in this sample average 25 µm in width (20-30 µm). Interference colors for 25 µm fibers are third-order blue through fourth-order red-mostly light greens and rose. With higher magnification, say 400X, bands of lower-order interference colors running parallel to the length of the fiber can be seen. Nylon fibers themselves are colorless, but they may be dyed a variety of colors.
records.Extended description: These smooth, continuous, transparent cylinders are round in cross section. The fibers in this sample average 25 µm in width (20-30 µm). Extinction is parallel and complete. The refractive indices are 1.580 (lengthwise) and 1.520 (crosswise); (+) 0.060. Interference colors for 25 µm fibers are third-order blue through fourth-order red-mostly light greens and rose. With higher magnification, say 400X, bands of lower-order interference colors running parallel to the length of the fiber can be seen. Nylon fibers themselves are colorless, but they may be dyed a variety of colors.

records.microscopy description: These fibers average 15 µm in diameter. The pigments make the fiber appear white in reflected light.
records.Extended description: In bulk, this material lacks shine because so much delustering pigment usually TiO2) has been added. Surfaces are pitted where pigment particles have broken through. These fibers average 15 µm in diameter. Like bright nylon (97), they are continuous, translucent cylinders, round in cross section, with complete parallel extinction. The refractive indices are 1.580 (lengthwise) and 1.520 (crosswise); (+) 0.060. Interference colors for 15 µm fibers are high second-order red, difficult to see due to light scattering by pigment. The pigments make the fiber appear white in reflected light.

Like bright nylon (97) and especially like semidull nylon (98) with the addition of even more delustering pigment (usually TiO2). The bulk material has almost no shine. The optical properties are more difficult to determine because of delustering pigment, but are like 97 and 98.

records.microscopy description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders. The birefringence is extremely high for a fiber. The fibers in this sample are 12 µm wide (10-15 µm);
records.Extended description: These are continuous, transparent, colorless cylinders. The surface is smooth except where delustering pigment particles have broken through and caused pitting. Extinction is complete; the refractive indices are 1. 710 (lengthwise) and 1.535 (crosswise) ; (+) 0.175. The birefringence is extremely high for a fiber. The fibers in this sample are 12 µm wide (10-15 µm); their interference colors are high fourth- and fifth-order light green and rose. Note that one refractive index is above and the other below Aroclor® (1.66).

records.microscopy description: Parallel striations run along the length of these transparent, colorless, smooth, continuous cylinders. these cause the surface striations. the fiber darkens at 230°C and melts at 293°C;
records.Extended description: Parallel striations run along the length of these transparent, colorless, smooth, continuous cylinders. In cross section, the fibers resemble a clover leaf, with four or more lobes, not too deeply cut; these cause the surface striations. The indices, both lengthwise and crosswise, are close to 1.469; the birefringence is therefore less than (+) 0.001. Actually, with white light and a first-order red compensator, exceedingly faint birefringence may be detected with a positive sign of elongation. The density is 1.30; the fiber darkens at 230°C and melts at 293°C; it is soluble in glacial acetic acid. Amel and Tricel are typical triacetate fibers. They are similar morphologically to bright acetate,(86) but are even less birefringent.

records.microscopy description: These continuous, transparent, colorless, striated cylinders show highly convoluted cross sections, as many as 6-20 rounded lobes around the circumference. Optical sectioning can be used to establish the cross-sectional shape. These fibers are 25 µm wide, but their width may vary from 10 to 50 µm. The interference colors for 25 µm fibers are high first- and low second-order.
records.Extended description: These continuous, transparent, colorless, striated cylinders show highly convoluted cross sections, as many as 6-20 rounded lobes around the circumference. Optical sectioning can be used to establish the cross-sectional shape. These fibers are 25 µm wide, but their width may vary from 10 to 50 µm. Extinction is parallel and complete; the refractive indices are 1.535-1.555 (lengthwise) and 1.515-1.535 (crosswise); (+) 0.020. The interference colors for 25 µm fibers are high first- and low second-order.

records.microscopy description: These fibers are like bright viscose rayon (102), but they are introduced here because they show the appearance and effect of both a dyed fiber (011001) and a fiber dust or "flock" (001001). Ordinarily for a fiber of this average diameter (20 µm), the interference colors would be high first-order. But because the fiber has been dyed red, all "interference colors" shown are shades of pink, red and orange. Dusts or flocks are characterized by their short fiber length 675 µm in this sample (640-700 µm).
records.Extended description: These fibers are like bright viscose rayon (102), but they are introduced here because they show the appearance and effect of both a dyed fiber (011001) and a fiber dust or "flock" (001001). The dye masks the interference colors. Ordinarily for a fiber of this average diameter (20 µm), the interference colors would be high first-order. But because the fiber has been dyed red, all "interference colors" shown are shades of pink, red and orange. Dusts or flocks are characterized by their short fiber length 675 µm in this sample (640-700 µm). Extinction of the fibers is complete; the refractive indices are 1.535-1.555 (lengthwise) and 1.515-1.535 (crosswise); (+) 0.020.

records.microscopy description: Tiny fragments of this rock wool product are transparent, colorless, isotropic, smooth threads, rods, "knees" and U's. a few are spheres.
records.Extended description: Tiny fragments of this rock wool product are transparent, colorless, isotropic, smooth threads, rods, "knees" and U's. Many are bulbous and contain air bubbles; a few are spheres. The index is about 1.57 (000001, 000000).

records.microscopy description: These are transparent, colorless, isotropic glass fibers (see 106) of uniform diameter (10 µm) ; Many of the rods are coated with, or cemented into bundles by, a transparent, yellow, amorphous, birefringent (strained) plastic binder; The bundles in this sample are 30-190 µm wide. Particle length ranges from 10 to 770 µm. Very small broken pieces of the rod without the binder are indistinguishable from ground glass (000000).
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless, isotropic glass fibers (see 106) of uniform diameter (10 µm) ; their refractive index is about 1.52. Many of the rods are coated with, or cemented into bundles by, a transparent, yellow, amorphous, birefringent (strained) plastic binder; its indices are around 1.53 (000001). The bundles in this sample are 30-190 µm wide. Particle length ranges from 10 to 770 µm. Very small broken pieces of the rod without the binder are indistinguishable from ground glass (000000).

records.microscopy description: These are transparent, colorless, continuous, isotropic cylinders, almost always smooth and regular. The cross sections of the fibers are perfectly round, 8 µm in diameter.
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless, continuous, isotropic cylinders, almost always smooth and regular. The ends usually show a clean transverse or diagonal break, but they are sometimes chipped, just like the broken ends of macroscopic glass rods. The cross sections of the fibers are perfectly round, 8 µm in diameter. The index is usually around 1.55 although it varies widely, normally about 1.47 for borosilicate and above 1.52 for soft glass.

records.microscopy description: Ninety-five percent of the sample is glass wool: transparent, colorless, isotropic rods, commas, dumbbells, U's, T's and completely amorphous globs of glass. The globs are all rounded; the rods are both uniform in diameter and tapering (both regularly and nonuniformly). The straight and "blobular" rods average 10 µm (3-15 µm) wide and 25 µm (5-1000 µm) long.
records.Extended description: This is a settled dust sample from an area in which fine glass wool is applied as insulation between the outer jacket and inner container of water-heater tanks. Ninety-five percent of the sample is glass wool: transparent, colorless, isotropic rods, commas, dumbbells, U's, T's and completely amorphous globs of glass. The globs are all rounded; the rods are both uniform in diameter and tapering (both regularly and nonuniformly). The straight and "blobular" rods average 10 µm (3-15 µm) wide and 25 µm (5-1000 µm) long. The index is about 1. 51 (000001, 000000). Other particles in this settled-dust sample include cotton (59) and paper fibers (70-74), as well as quartz (183), calcite (133) and combustion products (551-579).

records.microscopy description: Transparent; colorless, straight and curved, isotropic rods, circular in cross section (000001). some chips and irregular forms have broken off. The isotropic rods in this sample are 10 µm (5-35 µm) wide and 100 µm (15-1280 µm) long; These forms comprise about 85% of the sample. See fiber glass (106).
records.Extended description: 1. Transparent; colorless, straight and curved, isotropic rods, circular in cross section (000001). The broken ends are clean or jagged; some chips and irregular forms have broken off. The isotropic rods in this sample are 10 µm (5-35 µm) wide and 100 µm (15-1280 µm) long; the index is about 1.52. These forms comprise about 85% of the sample. See fiber glass (106). 2. Transparent, yellow, amorphous resin adhering to many of the glass rods. The resin shows very slight strain birefringence but is almost completely isotropic (010010) with an index of about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: Transparent to translucent, colorless to yellow to yellow-brown, isotropic cylinders of both uniform and varying diameters are seen here. Spheres also occur (000000, 010000). The distorted, fiberlike particles, many with enclosed air bubbles, range in diameter from 8 to 200 µm and may be several millimeters long. The spheres are 20 to more than 200 µm across. The particles have a generally smooth surface;
records.Extended description: Transparent to translucent, colorless to yellow to yellow-brown, isotropic cylinders of both uniform and varying diameters are seen here. Some have bumps and bulbous ends (000001, 010001). Spheres also occur (000000, 010000). The distorted, fiberlike particles, many with enclosed air bubbles, range in diameter from 8 to 200 µm and may be several millimeters long. The spheres are 20 to more than 200 µm across. The particles have a generally smooth surface; their refractive index is about 1.62.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless to brown, isotropic, smooth cylinders, straight or gently curved. some spheres also occur (000000, 010000). Transparent, colorless, isotropic, amorphous, plastic binder "cementing" masses of the fibers together. Its index is about 1.53, but it contains many birefringent 1 µm particles.
records.Extended description: This particular mineral wool is typical of the product used to manufacture insulating mats for use up to 550°C. It contains: 1. Transparent, colorless to brown, isotropic, smooth cylinders, straight or gently curved. Their refractive index is about 1.57 (000001, 010001). Many of the fibers are thickened and bulbous; some spheres also occur (000000, 010000). 2. Transparent, colorless, isotropic, amorphous, plastic binder "cementing" masses of the fibers together. Its index is about 1.53, but it contains many birefringent 1 µm particles.

records.microscopy description: These are transparent, colorless, isotropic, fine glassy fibers of mineral wool used as insulation. broken fragments are equant (000000). Diameters are <1-30+ µm.
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless, isotropic, fine glassy fibers of mineral wool used as insulation. The smooth cylinders are straight, gently curved and sharply bent (000001) ; broken fragments are equant (000000). The refractive index is about 1.51. Diameters are <1-30+ µm. Deformed fibers-doublets, knotted, thickened-are common.

records.microscopy description: Most of this sample consists of transparent to translucent, yellow spheres, dumbbells and clubs; The particle indices are about 1.57. Most of these particles have strain birefringence and show a black cross under crossed polars, much like that of starch (010000). Some show small, skeletal, birefringent crystals dispersed within the mass and on the surface. The sample also contains smooth, transparent, colorless, isotropic, glassy rods of both uniform and nonuniform diameter;
records.Extended description: Most of this sample consists of transparent to translucent, yellow spheres, dumbbells and clubs; many contain air bubbles. The particle indices are about 1.57. Most of these particles have strain birefringence and show a black cross under crossed polars, much like that of starch (010000). Some show small, skeletal, birefringent crystals dispersed within the mass and on the surface. These are evidence of incipient devitrification. Small fragments show no birefringence (010000). The sample also contains smooth, transparent, colorless, isotropic, glassy rods of both uniform and nonuniform diameter; many curve gently or

records.microscopy description: These colorless, angular crystals are equant (001000), tabular (001010), or pyramidal. Albite is triclinic and forms a solid solution series (the plagioclases) in which calcium replaces sodium;
records.Extended description: These colorless, angular crystals are equant (001000), tabular (001010), or pyramidal. Albite has good cleavage in two directions [001] and [010], making the crystal faces appear terraced; fracture is conchoidal. About 5% of the crushed crystals show "albite twinning"-lamellar bright and dark bands which appear when the crystal is at extinction. The specific gravity and hardness are, respectively, 2.60-2.62 and 6-6.5. Albite is triclinic and forms a solid solution series (the plagioclases) in which calcium replaces sodium; its refractive indices are 1.528-1.533 (alpha), 1.532-1.537 (beta), 1.538-1.542 (gamma); (+) 0.009; 2V=70°.

records.microscopy description: In the massive variety shown here, the texture is fibrous. High magnification reveals transparent, colorless rods and agglomerates of rods with a splintery fracture; Individual splinters are less than 2 µm wide, 6-15 µm long; the agglomerates average 20 µm across. The specific gravity of these particles is 2.6-2.8; Associated with the alunite are opaque, brownish-black, jagged chips and rounded, foamy, perforated particles of volcanic ash.
records.Extended description: Alunite is a naturally occurring basic potassium aluminum sulfate usually found with volcanic and other igneous rocks. In the massive variety shown here, the texture is fibrous. High magnification reveals transparent, colorless rods and agglomerates of rods with a splintery fracture; the indices are 1.572 (omega) to 1.592 (epsilon); (+) 0.020. Individual splinters are less than 2 µm wide, 6-15 µm long; the agglomerates average 20 µm across. The specific gravity of these particles is 2.6-2.8; their hardness is 4 (001001). Associated with the alunite are opaque, brownish-black, jagged chips and rounded, foamy, perforated particles of volcanic ash. Sometimes an extremely thin edge appears translucent dark brown (100010, 010000). Also present are transparent, colorless, rounded hexagonal plates and tablets with indices of about 1.73 and very low birefringence. This is very possibly an aluminum spinel from the firebricks of the furnace in which the alunite was roasted to produce water-soluble alum (000110).

records.microscopy description: Colorless, equant (001000), softly angular fragments of amblygonite show orange dispersion staining colors in Aroclor®.
records.Extended description: Colorless, equant (001000), softly angular fragments of amblygonite show orange dispersion staining colors in Aroclor®. Ninety-five percent of the fragments include squares, rectangles and tubes of liquid. These are randomly oriented, and most contain an internal gas bubble. The smooth to uneven faces occasionally show conchoidal fracture. The specific gravity ranges from 2.98 to 3.11, hardness from 5.5 to 6. This triclinic mineral has indices of 1.578 (alpha), 1.595 (beta), 1.598 (gamma); (-) 0.020; 2V = 50°.

records.microscopy description: Most of these colorless, sharply angular, translucent fragments are equant (001000) with smooth to uneven faces.
records.Extended description: Most of these colorless, sharply angular, translucent fragments are equant (001000) with smooth to uneven faces. Cleaved faces are occasionally seen though fractures predominate. The specific gravity range is 2.89-2.99; hardness is 3-3.5. The orthorhombic crystals have indices of 1.571 (alpha), 1.576 (beta), 1.614 (gamma); (+) 0.043; 2V=42°. Anhydrite rapidly changes to gypsum (151) in the presence of water so that it is seldom found without the hydrated mineral.

records.microscopy description: Serpentine consists of colorless (though sometimes faintly tan due to light scatter), equant, rough chips with splintery edges (001000); colorless, angular plates with uneven faces and edges (001010); The equant chips have mottled gray interference colors; Extinction is incomplete and fanlike for the equant fragments, while the blades and needles show parallel extinction.
records.Extended description: Serpentine consists of colorless (though sometimes faintly tan due to light scatter), equant, rough chips with splintery edges (001000); colorless, angular plates with uneven faces and edges (001010); and short, narrow blades and needles (001001). The equant chips have mottled gray interference colors; the plates, blades and needles show extremely weak interference colors. All of the longer fragments have positive elongation. Extinction is incomplete and fanlike for the equant fragments, while the blades and needles show parallel extinction. Monoclinic serpentine has indices of 1.555-1.567 (a), 1.560-1.573 (beta), 1.560-1.573 (gamma); (-) 0.004-0.009; 2V=20-50°. The hardness range is 2.5-4; the specific gravity range is 2.5-2.65. This sample also contains opaque to deep brown, isotropic particles of chromite (100000) and highly birefringent calcite (133) (001000).

records.microscopy description: Crushed apatite particles are colorless, transparent chips and flakes with sharp edges and smooth faces showing a trace of conchoidal fracture. The commonest form of apatite is fluorapatite.
records.Extended description: Crushed apatite particles are colorless, transparent chips and flakes with sharp edges and smooth faces showing a trace of conchoidal fracture. The chips taper to a very thin edge which, along with the refractive indices, gives the crystals very low contrast in Aroclor®. The specific gravity is 3.2; hardness is 5. These uniaxial crystals belong to the hexagonal system and have indices of 1. 630-1. 643 (epsilon) and 1.632-1.648 (w); (-) 0.002-0.005. The commonest form of apatite is fluorapatite. Calcite (133) is usually associated with apatite but can be easily distinguished by its very high birefringence. With an annular stop and Aroclor®, the dispersion staining colors for apatite are red-orange; with a central stop, blue-green.

records.microscopy description: triangular plates with rough to sharp angular edges;
records.Extended description: Bits of aragonite, a less common form of CaCO3 , have many shapes: elongated prisms (001101) which terminate in slightly oblique faces; subcircular plates (001110) with edges saw-toothed due to cleavage; triangular plates with rough to sharp angular edges; striated rhombs (001100) strongly resembling calcite (133) except that these striations bisect the obtuse rhomb angle. The striations, due to twinning, are thin crystal bands rather than grooves; they can be seen, between crossed polars, to penetrate the entire crystal. Aragonite is orthorhombic with indices of 1.530 (alpha), 1.682 (beta), 1.686 (gamma); (-) 0.156; 2V=18-19°. The specific gravity is 2.94; hardness is 4. The dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® for the high index direction are yellow with an annular stop, blue with a central stop. Without a dispersion staining objective, blue and orange Becke lines are observed.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless, straight, long fibers of orthorhombic asbestos from Transvaal, South Africa, may be gray, yellowish or brownish in thick bundles, due principally to light scattering by the fine fibrils. The fibrils that make up the 50+ µm bundles in this sample are much less than 1 µm wide. Refractive indices are variable depending on the amount of iron present: -y parallel to the fiber length is about 1.695 and a is about 1.700. Distinguished from chrysotile by the straight fiber and higher index.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless, straight, long fibers of orthorhombic asbestos from Transvaal, South Africa, may be gray, yellowish or brownish in thick bundles, due principally to light scattering by the fine fibrils. The fibrils that make up the 50+ µm bundles in this sample are much less than 1 µm wide. In composition, amosite is between anthophyllite (121), q.v., and gedrite (iron present in much larger amounts). Refractive indices are variable depending on the amount of iron present: -y parallel to the fiber length is about 1.695 and a is about 1.700. Interference colors here are low first-order. Optically positive (but negative for gedrite). Extinction is parallel and complete. Specific gravity 2.6-3.0. Distinguished from chrysotile by the straight fiber and higher index.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless, straight orthorhombic fibers may also be lamellar. The fibrils that make up the 70+ µm bundles in this sample are much less than 1 µm wide. The refractive indices vary with composition: gamma, parallel to the length, varies from about 1.62-1.64, alpha from about 1.60-1.62.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless, straight orthorhombic fibers may also be lamellar. The fibrils that make up the 70+ µm bundles in this sample are much less than 1 µm wide. The refractive indices vary with composition: gamma, parallel to the length, varies from about 1.62-1.64, alpha from about 1.60-1.62. Magnesium lowers the indices; aluminum may also be present in considerable amounts. 2V very nearly 90°. Interference colors here are low first-order. Positive optical character is negative for gedrite (iron present in much larger amounts). Extinction is parallel, but may be inclined to about 15°. Specific gravity is 2.85-3.4 (inreasing with iron). Cf. amosite (120).

records.microscopy description: The colorless, transparent, cylindrical fibrils (the bands are translucent) are less than 1 µm in diameter and have smooth surfaces. its indices are 1.529-1.559 (alpha) , 1.530-1.564 (beta), 1.537-1.567 (gamma parallel to fiber length); The low a index distinguishes chrysotile from other asbestos forms such as crocidolite (123) and anthophyllite (121).
records.Extended description: This sample includes bands of straight, parallel fibrils with nonperiodic crimps, wavy bands of fibrils and single, randomly twisted fibrils. The colorless, transparent, cylindrical fibrils (the bands are translucent) are less than 1 µm in diameter and have smooth surfaces. Chrysotile is monoclinic; its indices are 1.529-1.559 (alpha) , 1.530-1.564 (beta), 1.537-1.567 (gamma parallel to fiber length); (+) 0.004-0.016; 2V cannot be observed. The fibers show parallel extinction and have a positive sign of elongation. The low a index distinguishes chrysotile from other asbestos forms such as crocidolite (123) and anthophyllite (121). Probably the best key to the identification of chrysotile is its low refractive index. The specific gravity is 2.2; the hardness ranges from 2.5 to 4.

records.microscopy description: This "blue asbestos" is an asbestiform of riebeckite consisting of bundles of easily separable, long, delicate, blue-green fibers elongated parallel to the c axis. The cylindrical fibrils show their blue color even when less than 1 µm in diameter. The indices of this monoclinic, biaxial mineral are 1.680-1.698 (alpha parallel to fiber length) , 1.683-1.700 (beta), 1.685-1.
records.Extended description: This "blue asbestos" is an asbestiform of riebeckite consisting of bundles of easily separable, long, delicate, blue-green fibers elongated parallel to the c axis. The cylindrical fibrils show their blue color even when less than 1 µm in diameter. The indices of this monoclinic, biaxial mineral are 1.680-1.698 (alpha parallel to fiber length) , 1.683-1.700 (beta), 1.685-1. 706 (gamma); (-) 0.003-0.009; 2V is large. The indices decrease and the birefringence increases as magnesium replaces ferrous iron. At Fe:Mg of 2:1, the birefringence is 0.018-0.022. First-order interference colors are normally masked by the mineral's blue color. The needles are strongly pleochroic with alpha green-blue to yellow, beta gray-blue to blue, gamma yellow-brown to yellow-green. Crocidolite is the only asbestos with a negative sign of elongation. The maximum extinction angle varies with composition from 3 to 15°. Specific gravity is 3.2 to 3.3; hardness is 4. This sample also contains bits of albite (113), kyanite (156), goethite (162) , other iron oxides and fine-grained quartz (183).

records.microscopy description: Asbestos: individual fibers and small bundles (to 40 µm X 160 µm) of chrysotile asbestos (122), q.v. Filler: agglomerates of 1 µm, black, opaque, equant particles that appear medium to dark gray in top light (100000); Binder: transparent, isotropic, yellow to orange, amorphous, organic binder cementing the other components into equant (to 100 µm) aggregates (010000);
records.Extended description: Three major components make up this sample: 1. Asbestos: individual fibers and small bundles (to 40 µm X 160 µm) of chrysotile asbestos (122), q.v. (001001). 2. Filler: agglomerates of 1 µm, black, opaque, equant particles that appear medium to dark gray in top light (100000); usually carbon black. 3. Binder: transparent, isotropic, yellow to orange, amorphous, organic binder cementing the other components into equant (to 100 µm) aggregates (010000); usually phenolic resin. In addition, there are small amounts (< 1 %) of brass, steel and hematite.

records.microscopy description: Some chrysotile asbestos is still present, but most of the particles are mineral species removed by the cleaning procedure.
records.Extended description: This sample is typical of asbestos cleaning. Some chrysotile asbestos is still present, but most of the particles are mineral species removed by the cleaning procedure. They include quartz (183), calcite (133), a variety of feldspars and mica as well as a few particles of rutile (186), an unusual associate of chrysotile.

records.microscopy description: The transparent, colorless, generally flaky particles may be lying sideways in the medium and look like needles. The mostly 3-6 µm (<1-45 µm) particles show low to moderate gray interference colors.
records.Extended description: This clay is the mineral attapulgite (named from its occurrence at Attapulgus, Georgia), a variable type amphilbole (double silica-chain) with the ideal formula of 5(MgAl)O·8SiO2·4H2O. It is used as an absorbent material, an anticaking agent and an extender in paint, plaster and ink. The transparent, colorless, generally flaky particles may be lying sideways in the medium and look like needles. The mostly 3-6 µm (<1-45 µm) particles show low to moderate gray interference colors. Specific gravity is about 2.4.

records.microscopy description: These fragments are subrectangular to square plates and tablets (011110) with sharp and rough angular edges. Pale green and gray-green particles predominate (even 5 µm particles are green) ; less than 1 % are pleochroic, showing blue-green in one direction and gray-green when the particles, illuminated by polarized light, are rotated 90°. The interference colors are not seriously affected, at least on small particles, by the absorption colors.
records.Extended description: These fragments are subrectangular to square plates and tablets (011110) with sharp and rough angular edges. No cleavage is evident. The faces are uneven, showing non-parallel but aligned striations and conchoidal fracture. Pale green and gray-green particles predominate (even 5 µm particles are green) ; less than 1 % are pleochroic, showing blue-green in one direction and gray-green when the particles, illuminated by polarized light, are rotated 90°. About 5% of the samples are covered with orange-brown particles of Fe2O3. The specific gravity range is 3.25-3.55; hardness is 6. The indices of this monoclinic mineral range from 1.680-1.703 (alpha) through 1.684-1.711 (beta) to 1.706-1.729 (gamma); (+) 0.025; 2V = 39-63°. The indices increase with iron content. The interference colors are not seriously affected, at least on small particles, by the absorption colors.

records.microscopy description: The "azure" blue to pale blue-green of these translucent, sharply angular chips (011100, 001100) is a chief identifying characteristic of azurite. They do not show significant pleochroism, but the interference colors are affected, especially in particles more than about 5 µm in diameter.
records.Extended description: The "azure" blue to pale blue-green of these translucent, sharply angular chips (011100, 001100) is a chief identifying characteristic of azurite. The absence of easily detectable color in very fine crystals, however, does not preclude the possibility of azurite being present. "Green azurite," or malachite (166), has a green absorption color. The indices of these monoclinic crystals are 1.730 (alpha), 1.758 (beta), 1.838 (gamma); (+) 0.108; 2V=68°. They do not show significant pleochroism, but the interference colors are affected, especially in particles more than about 5 µm in diameter.

records.microscopy description: Particles of crushed barite are colorless, transparent plates (001010), chips and pseudocubes (001000) with jagged, sharp edges. At least 70% of these particles have liquid-gas inclusions (up to 30% by volume) which would affect the microdensity determination.
records.Extended description: Particles of crushed barite are colorless, transparent plates (001010), chips and pseudocubes (001000) with jagged, sharp edges. The fragments have smooth to uneven faces, occasionally with conchoidal fracture. At least 70% of these particles have liquid-gas inclusions (up to 30% by volume) which would affect the microdensity determination. Cleavage is seen as two edges at right angles on the plates. The specific gravity is 4.3-4.6, the hardness 2.5-3.5. Barite is orthorhombic, with indices of 1.636 (alpha), 1.637 (beta), 1.648 (gamma); (+) 0.012; 2V=37°. The dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® are orange with an annular stop and blue, with a slightly green-blue Becke line, with a central stop.

records.microscopy description: These particles appear to be a glassy matrix (010000) with occluded birefringent crystals (011000). Most of the color is, however, structural and due to the fine grain size of the innumerable occlusions in each particle.
records.Extended description: These particles appear to be a glassy matrix (010000) with occluded birefringent crystals (011000). It is, in reality, a gel of hydrous oxides of aluminum [diaspore, HA1O2; gibbsite, Al(OH)g; boehmite, AlO(OH) and some lepidocrocite, FeO (OH)] which contributes a brown color. Most of the color is, however, structural and due to the fine grain size of the innumerable occlusions in each particle. The cleavage is conchoidal, and the refractive indices are usually less than 1.50. It is a cloudy white by reflected light except for some areas of a rosy red due to iron.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless, apparently rounded, equant (001000) particles and agglomerates of clay appear here. The ultimate clay particle cannot be resolved with the light microscope. Because the particles are so small, their agglomerates look hazy-almost fibrous. This sample from the Dakotas is actually the sodium form of a clay mineral rock.
records.Extended description: Transparent, colorless, apparently rounded, equant (001000) particles and agglomerates of clay appear here. Their birefringence is low; the indices are about 1.52. The ultimate clay particle cannot be resolved with the light microscope. Because the particles are so small, their agglomerates look hazy-almost fibrous. Natural deposits of good molding sand for foundries are almost exhausted. Sand containing little or no clay is therefore mixed with clay or claylike material such as bentonite to make "synthetic" sands. This sample from the Dakotas is actually the sodium form of a clay mineral rock. It absorbs large quantities of water so that it swells into jellylike masses which are permanent suspensions. Besides being a bonding agent for foundry sands, bentonite is used to seal dams, as a drilling mud, in concrete and portland cements, in paper manufacture, in ceramics, paints and soaps, and to bond asbestos and mineral wool.

records.microscopy description: The fragments are colorless, transparent, sharply angular chips (001000); liquid-gas inclusions are spherical, tubular and randomly oriented, though not so numerous as in barite.
records.Extended description: Beryl resembles barite (129) except that beryl has higher contrast and lacks cleavage. The fragments are colorless, transparent, sharply angular chips (001000); some of the edges end in points. The faces are uneven and usually have conchoidal fracture; liquid-gas inclusions are spherical, tubular and randomly oriented, though not so numerous as in barite. This hexagonal mineral has indices of 1.564-1.595 (E) and 1.582-1.602 (omega); (-) 0.004-0.008. Quartz (183) is distinguished by its lower indices.

records.microscopy description: The colorless, transparent, crushed fragments are frequently seen as rhombohedra.
records.Extended description: Calcite, along with quartz (183), is a common constituent of dust samples. The colorless, transparent, crushed fragments are frequently seen as rhombohedra. These are plates (001010) or tablets (001000) commonly showing twinning striations that bisect the acute rhomb angle. The specific gravity is 2. 7; hardness is 3. The refractive indices of calcite are 1.486 (epsilon) and 1.658 (omega); (-) 0.172. The crystal, oriented to show omega, though nearly invisible, shows faint yellow dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® (epsilon = 1.566 if the rhomb plane is parallel to the stage). The birefringence of the calcite group is so extreme that even 5 µm particles show second-order interference colors. The dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® for omega are red-orange with the annular stop and blue-green with the central stop. Calcite is isomorphous with rhodochrosite, MnCO3, which generally can be distinguished by its higher indices. Dolomite, CaMg (C03) 2, siderite, FeCO3, and magnesite, MgCO3, also strongly resemble calcite but can be distinguished by their indices, by microchemical tests or by microprobe.

records.microscopy description: Thin particles are colorless; The fragments are sharp, angular chips (011100, 001100) with jagged, fine edges; elongated particles are generally pick-shaped and terminate in sharp points. simply rotate the crystal to that extinction position in which it is nearly colorless. Epsilon, or more probably epsilon-prime, denotes the extinction position in which the crystal is salmon to deep red, depending on its size and orientation. Although rutile (186) resembles cassiterite in shape and color, it has much higher indices and consequently shows greater contrast.
records.Extended description: Thin particles are colorless; as the thickness increases, the color changes through salmon to deep orange-red. The fragments are sharp, angular chips (011100, 001100) with jagged, fine edges; elongated particles are generally pick-shaped and terminate in sharp points. All faces are strongly marked with conchoidal fracture; no cleavage is evident. The specific gravity is 7.0, and the hardness is 6.5. This tetragonal crystal has indices of 2. 093 (epsilon) and 1.997 (omega) ; (+) 0.096. Its strong pleochroism can be used to locate omega; simply rotate the crystal to that extinction position in which it is nearly colorless. Epsilon, or more probably epsilon-prime, denotes the extinction position in which the crystal is salmon to deep red, depending on its size and orientation. Although rutile (186) resembles cassiterite in shape and color, it has much higher indices and consequently shows greater contrast.

records.microscopy description: These colorless, transparent, sharply angular chips are a fibrous form of Si02 . The truly fibrous fragments are cryptocrystalline and do not show regular extinction;
records.Extended description: These colorless, transparent, sharply angular chips are a fibrous form of Si02 . The truly fibrous fragments are cryptocrystalline and do not show regular extinction; fragments not truly fibrous resemble quartz (183). Fracture more or less conchoidal; no cleavage. The indices of hexagonal chalcedony are variously reported: 1.530-1.553 (epsilon) and 1.531-1.544 (omega); birefringence is about 0.007, and the sign is usually (+). The specific gravity range is 2.55-2.64, and the hardness is 7. Red and brown varieties are called jasper; banded and variegated varieties are called agate.

records.microscopy description: The amorphous particles are isotropic, with a refractive index of 1.57-1.63 (000000), but may show low first-order colors due to strain birefringence (001000).
records.Extended description: These irregular, colorless to brown, transparent to translucent particles are cryptocrystalline carbonate-hydroxy-fluorapatite, a variety of apatite (118), q.v. The amorphous particles are isotropic, with a refractive index of 1.57-1.63 (000000), but may show low first-order colors due to strain birefringence (001000). Hardness is 3-5; specific gravity is 2.6-2.9 (both depending on purity and porosity). This mineral is a replacement for bone (fossil bone) and may actually show bony structure (brown coloration due to organic pigment, 010000). Organic matter, iron, aluminum and calcite are usually found associated. May be weakly radioactive. White to yellow (due to small amounts of ematite) in top light.

records.microscopy description: The amorphous particles are isotropic, with a refractive index of 1.57-1.63 (000000), but may show low first-order colors due to strain birefringence (001000).
records.Extended description: These irregular, colorless to brown, transparent to translucent particles are cryptocrystalline carbonate-hydroxy-fluorapatite, a variety of apatite (118), q.v. The amorphous particles are isotropic, with a refractive index of 1.57-1.63 (000000), but may show low first-order colors due to strain birefringence (001000). Hardness is 3-5; specific gravity is 2.6-2.9 (both depending on purity and porosity). This mineral is a replacement for bone (fossil bone) and may actually show bony structure (brown coloration due to organic pigment, 010000). Organic matter, iron, aluminum and calcite are usually found associated. May be weakly radioactive. White to yellow (due to small amounts of ematite) in top light.

records.microscopy description: The shape of the broken particles is influenced by the good to perfect basal parting, often resulting in a single flat face. if visibly colored, they will be dichroic when viewed along or near the optic normal.
records.Extended description: Aluminum oxide occurs naturally in irregular, transparent, colorless (001100) to pale pinkish-tan, sharp-edged fragments and chips (011100). The shape of the broken particles is influenced by the good to perfect basal parting, often resulting in a single flat face. Minute "opaque" occlusions are hematite (390). Next to diamond (272), this is the hardest natural abrasive. Other samples of natural corundum may well be dull gray to brown, red, blue or yellow; if visibly colored, they will be dichroic when viewed along or near the optic normal. The refractive indices range from 1.7676-1.7682 (epsilon) to 1.7594-1.7598 (omega); birefringence is low, about (-) 0.008.

records.microscopy description: These colorless, transparent to translucent, irregular to generally rounded particles occur in two varieties in nature: (1) a high temperature, isotropic form (alpha) with a refractive index of 1.485-1.487 (000000), and (2) a low temperature, anisotropic (tetragonal) form (beta) with refractive indices of 1.482-1.484 (epsilon) and 1.486-1.488 (omega); The beta form inverts to the a form between 200 and 275°C. In this sample, minute (1 µm) gas bubbles cause the translucent, almost opaque, appearance. Here the particles also contain hairlike crystallites (trichites).
records.Extended description: These colorless, transparent to translucent, irregular to generally rounded particles occur in two varieties in nature: (1) a high temperature, isotropic form (alpha) with a refractive index of 1.485-1.487 (000000), and (2) a low temperature, anisotropic (tetragonal) form (beta) with refractive indices of 1.482-1.484 (epsilon) and 1.486-1.488 (omega); (-) 0.002-0.006 (001000) (for synthetic: Epsilon is 1.484 and omega is 1.487). The beta form inverts to the a form between 200 and 275°C. Hardness is 6-7; specific gravity is 2.27-2.35. Cristobalite occurs in volcanic igneous rocks and is formed by hot gases. In this sample, minute (1 µm) gas bubbles cause the translucent, almost opaque, appearance. Here the particles also contain hairlike crystallites (trichites). Frosty white in top light.

records.microscopy description: These colorless, transparent to translucent, irregular to generally rounded particles occur in two varieties in nature: (1) a high temperature, isotropic form (alpha) with a refractive index of 1.485-1.487 (000000), and (2) a low temperature, anisotropic (tetragonal) form (beta) with refractive indices of 1.482-1.484 (epsilon) and 1.486-1.488 (omega); The beta form inverts to the a form between 200 and 275°C. In this sample, minute (1 µm) gas bubbles cause the translucent, almost opaque, appearance. Here the particles also contain hairlike crystallites (trichites).

records.microscopy description: Many of these transparent, colorless fragments are "cubes" or show one or more "cube" faces. The faces are smooth, and the edges and corners may be either sharp or rounded. Most of the particles less than 10 µm in diameter are actually rounded and equant rather than cubic. Note that the birefringence is very low, making small particles appear isotropic.
records.Extended description: Many of these transparent, colorless fragments are "cubes" or show one or more "cube" faces. The faces are smooth, and the edges and corners may be either sharp or rounded. Most of the particles less than 10 µm in diameter are actually rounded and equant rather than cubic. The indices are 1.3385 (alpha), 1.3389 (beta), 1.3396 (gamma); (+) 0.0011. Note that the birefringence is very low, making small particles appear isotropic. Excellent parting rather than cleavage is responsible for the regular shapes obtained on grinding. Hardness is 2.5; density is 2.97.

These transparent, colorless, generally equant particles are a double salt of CaCO3 and MgCO3. They are rhombohedra, often curved or saddle-shaped. Cleavage perfect. Extinction symmetrical. The refractive indices of hexagonal dolomite are 1.5026 (1:) and 1.6817 (omega); (-) 0.179. The extremely high birefringence yields high-order white interference colors even on small crystals. Forms a solid solution series with CaFe (CO3) 2 and CaMn (CO3) 2; indices increase with Fe to 1.526 (epsilon) and 1.716 (omega) for ankerite. Hardness is 3.5-4; specific gravity is 2.83-3 (increasing with Fe). Can be confused with calcite (133), q.v., but twinning not as abundant as in calcite. Also, twinning here shows up as striations on the cleavage faces parallel to both the long and short diagonal of the rhomb (unlike

records.microscopy description: Crushed fragments of epidote are pale yellow-green, equant (011100) with rough to uneven edges and faces. The particles are weakly pleochroic; Particles less than 20 µm across exhibit the pleochroic effect as a change in absorbed light intensity rather than color.
records.Extended description: Crushed fragments of epidote are pale yellow-green, equant (011100) with rough to uneven edges and faces. Some cleaved faces are present; fracture is uneven to subconchoidal. There are minor inclusions of magnetite (165) and gases. The hardness range is 6-7; specific gravity is 3.3-3.5. Epidote is monoclinic with indices of 1.723-1.751 (alpha), 1.730-1.784 (beta) , 1.736-1.797 (gamma); (-) 0.013-0.46 2V = 64.89°. The particles are weakly pleochroic; in plane polarized light they are pale yellow in one direction, yellow-green in the perpendicular direction. Particles less than 20 µm across exhibit the pleochroic effect as a change in absorbed light intensity rather than color. Epidote is distinguished from hornblende (152) and augite (127) by both color and refractive index.

records.microscopy description: Crushed fluorite consists of colorless, transparent, sharply angular, equant chips (000000). Some are elongated. All show smooth to uneven, sharp edges and faces with conchoidal fracture. Fluorite and cryolite (139) look very similar except that cryolite is very weakly birefringent (sometimes this is evident only in large particles) and has lower indices (1.339).
records.Extended description: Crushed fluorite consists of colorless, transparent, sharply angular, equant chips (000000). Some are elongated. Approximately 25% of the crushed crystals are triangular or pyramidal due to octahedral cleavage. All show smooth to uneven, sharp edges and faces with conchoidal fracture. Rough traces of parallel cleavage can also be seen on most of the faces. The specific gravity range is 3.01-3.25; hardness is 4. Fluorite belongs to the cubic system as glass and obsidian, can be distinguished from it by their higher indices. Fluorite and cryolite (139) look very similar except that cryolite is very weakly birefringent (sometimes this is evident only in large particles) and has lower indices (1.339). Some of these fluorite particles (less than 5%) have calcite (133) inclusions.

records.microscopy description: most are about 15 µm.
records.Extended description: This sample, from near Paris, contains quartz (183) sand and calcite (133). Some crystals from this material have been reported to have the form of calcite, but contain 60% or more quartz. The smaller amount of calcite is said to have impressed its own crystallizing characteristics on the sand. This sample consists of about 80% quartz in particle sizes < 1-60+ µm; most are about 15 µm. The remainder of the sample consists of calcite, <1-3 µm. An occasional quartz grain does seem to have one or more rather straight fractures, suggestive of cleavage planes. A few are almost rhombs.

records.microscopy description: The sample in 144A consists of transparent to translucent, light tan to dark brown, rounded 300+ µm agglomerates (011000) of <l µm transparent, colorless particles (001000) that have been stained brown through use as a refining company catalyst carrier. Some are so dark brown they are opaque (100000). Some fragments are so small (to 6 µm) as to appear colorless (001000, 001010). The sample in 144B consists of transparent to translucent, colorless to yellow, 500+ µm, softly rounded agglomerates of <l µm, birefringent particles (001000, 011000). Small (3-15 µm) pieces may be flakes (001010).
records.Extended description: This is a naturally occurring, porous, highly absorptive claylike material. It is essentially a hydrated aluminum silicate containing some magnesium and a little iron. It is composed largely of attapulgite (126) with some montmorillonite. Varieties differ in specific gravity (1. 7-2.4) and absorptive and catalytic properties.
