records.microscopy description: Almandite particles are transparent, colorless to salmon-tinged, irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges; the surfaces are semiconchoidal with curved fracture; Many grains are etched; The 5-350 µm particles in this sample are colorless (000100) to pale salmon, but because this is an iron-aluminum garnet, larger particles may be red, brown or black. Crystals less than 5-10 µm thick are essentially colorless.
records.Extended description: Almandite particles are transparent, colorless to salmon-tinged, irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges; the surfaces are semiconchoidal with curved fracture; some are stepped and wavy. Many grains are etched; some show grooves and pits. The isotropic particles may contain small birefringent occlusions, such as quartz (183), feldspar and muscovite (168). The 5-350 µm particles in this sample are colorless (000100) to pale salmon, but because this is an iron-aluminum garnet, larger particles may be red, brown or black. Crystals less than 5-10 µm thick are essentially colorless. The indices are 1.770-1.830, depending on the actual composition of the crystals. The almandite variety of garnet is also called almandine.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless (to light brown and dark brown for grains), irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges have curved, semiconchoidal fracture. Surfaces may be etched; The particles are isotropic (000100) generally, but twinning is common with weak birefringence (001100) and large optic angle.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless (to light brown and dark brown for grains), irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges have curved, semiconchoidal fracture. Surfaces may be etched; some show grooves, pits or parallel striations. No cleavage but may show parting. The particles are isotropic (000100) generally, but twinning is common with weak birefringence (001100) and large optic angle. The refractive index is 1.857-1.895 (1.895 for synthetic). Hardness is 6.5-7; specific gravity is 3. 75 (3.83 for synthetic). Cf. grossularite (147).

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless (to yellow and brown for grains) , irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges have curved, semiconchoidal fracture. Surfaces may be etched; The particles are isotropic (000100) generally, but birefringence is not uncommon (001100). also rounded and elongated gas bubbles.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless (to yellow and brown for grains) , irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges have curved, semiconchoidal fracture. Surfaces may be etched; some show grooves, pits or parallel striations. No cleavage. The particles are isotropic (000100) generally, but birefringence is not uncommon (001100). The refractive index is 1.735-1.763 (1.735 for synthetic). Forms a continuous series with Ca3Fe2Si3O12, andradite (146), q.v., and Ca3Cr2Si3O12 (index is 1.86; specific gravity is 3. 78). The hardness is 6.5-7; the specific gravity is 3.53. In this sample, there are small, birefringent occlusions of quartz and other materials; also rounded and elongated gas bubbles.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless to salmon pink, irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges have curved, semiconchoidal fracture. Surfaces may be etched; The particles are isotropic (000100, 010100) generally, but some may show weak birefringence in parts or be distinctly anisotropic (010100, 011100).
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless to salmon pink, irregular chips and fragments with sharp to rounded edges have curved, semiconchoidal fracture. Surfaces may be etched; some show grooves or pits. No cleavage. The particles are isotropic (000100, 010100) generally, but some may show weak birefringence in parts or be distinctly anisotropic (010100, 011100). The refractive index is 1.792-1.820 (1.80 for synthetic). Hardness is 7-7.5; specific gravity is 4.18. May contain yttrium; forms solid solution series with Yt3Al2Si3O12 (refractive index 1.823). The particles in this sample contain birefringent occlusions of quartz and other materials.

records.microscopy description: It consists of minute, overlapping, transparent platelets; some single crystal grains are roughly hexagonal in outline. particles less than 2 µm in diameter are colorless (001010). The yellowish and brown particles in the photomicrograph are limonite (162) and goethite (see 162) , alteration products of glauconite.
records.Extended description: The rounded, fine-grained aggregates of this hydrous silicate of iron and potassium constitute a sedimentary marine deposit usually associated with clays and sand. It consists of minute, overlapping, transparent platelets; some single crystal grains are roughly hexagonal in outline. The fine laminae show a distinct micaceous cleavage. The color is green, olive green or blackish green (011010) ; particles less than 2 µm in diameter are colorless (001010). Higher iron content causes a shift toward red and higher refractive indices. The indices of this monoclinic, biaxial mineral are 1.590-1.612 (alpha) , 1.609-1.643 (f3), 1.610-1.644 (gamma); (-) 0.014-0.032; 2V = 0-20°, but usually greater than 10°. Specific gravity ranges from 2.4 to 2.95; hardness is 2. Individual crystals are strongly pleochroic with a pale to straw yellow, f3 and gamma green, dark green, bluish green or olive green. The yellowish and brown particles in the photomicrograph are limonite (162) and goethite (see 162) , alteration products of glauconite.

This sample, a plutonic rock dust from a granite works, consists of three major components: 1. Quartz (183) , q.v., here comminuted to a range of 5-10 µm, with sharp, irregular edges (001000) ; about 75% of the sample. 2. Feldspar (aluminum silicates with sodium, potassium or calcium): see albite (113), labradorite (157), microcline (169) and orthoclase (176). All are 001000, 001010. 3. Dark ferromagnesian minerals such as pyroxene, hornblende (152) (011110) , biotite (167) (011010, 011110) or olivine (174) (001110) in small amounts.

records.microscopy description: Gypsum particles are colorless, transparent, equant chips (001000) which are sometimes elongated. the particles are soft (Moh 1.5-2.0).
records.Extended description: Gypsum particles are colorless, transparent, equant chips (001000) which are sometimes elongated. The faces appear very rough due to smaller adhering crystals. The edges are uneven and slightly rough. Cleavage fragments (less than 5% of this sample) are rhomb-shaped with striations parallel to an edge. Heavy striations also follow the gentle arc of curved crystals. The specific gravity is 2.3; the particles are soft (Moh 1.5-2.0). Gypsum is a monoclinic crystal with indices of 1.520 (alpha) , 1.523 (f3), 1.530 (gamma); (+) 0.010; 2V = 58°. The cleavage fragments generally show a flash figure. Gypsum is the most common sulfate; it alters to plaster of paris (532) with sufficient heat (> 100°C). The irregular fragments resemble quartz (183), but gypsum has lower birefringence and indices.

records.microscopy description: Hornblende particles are pale blue and green, rarely colorless, translucent, angular, platy chips and blades.
records.Extended description: Hornblende particles are pale blue and green, rarely colorless, translucent, angular, platy chips and blades. Fine tan particles of iron oxide, a hornblende alteration product, coat some of the smooth to uneven faces which may show cleavage striations parallel to the long edge. The specific gravity range is 3.05-3.47; the hardness is 5-6. Monoclinic hornblende has index ranges of 1.646-1.665 a), 1.656-1.675 (beta), 1.661-1.685 (gamma); (-) 0.015-0.020; 2V= 66-85°. In plane polarized light, larger crystals show moderate green-blue at one extinction position; a yellow-green is seen by rotating the crystal 90° to its next extinction position. The green-blue direction corresponds to an index slightly higher than or equal to that of Aroclor® (1.66); the index in the yellow-green direction is always lower than, but close to, that of the medium. The green-blue direction is parallel to the long edge of the blades, which therefore have positive elongation. Because horn-blende is a very common rock-former, it is found associated with many minerals. Quartz (183) can be recognized in this sample by its high contrast (001000).

records.microscopy description: These transparent, yellow to deep red-orange and reddish-brown, pleochroic particles have perfect cleavage in one direction, resulting in large, equant fragments which are stepped and terraced aggregates of blades (011100); small particles are elongated plates and blades (011110, 011111).
records.Extended description: These transparent, yellow to deep red-orange and reddish-brown, pleochroic particles have perfect cleavage in one direction, resulting in large, equant fragments which are stepped and terraced aggregates of blades (011100); small particles are elongated plates and blades (011110, 011111). The indices (Li) of monoclinic huebnerite are 2.17 (alpha), 2.22 (beta), 2.32 (gamma); (+) 0.15; 2V = 73° [for the synthetic: 2.150 (alpha), 2.195 (beta), 2.283 (gamma); (+) 0.133; 2V = 75°]. The hardness is 5; specific gravity is 7.0-7.1. Note high birefringence and high specific gravity.

Only about 2% of this sample consists of ilmenite; the remainder is the gangue dust consisting mostly, in this case, of feldspar (aluminum silicates with sodium, potas-sium or calcium) (001000, 001010) and dark ferromagnesian minerals in very small amounts, e.g., hornblende (152) (011110). The ilmenite itself, FeTiO3, consists of black or reddish-brown tablets or plates (100010) or equant particles (100000). They are rhombohedral and slightly magnetic. The hardness is 5-6; specific gravity is 4. 7. Ilmenite alters to leucoxene, the whitish, amorphous titanium dioxide.

records.microscopy description: Interference colors are low first-order gray, even for 1 µm particles. Individual particles are colorless, but the aggregates may be white to gray or yellow to brownish.
records.Extended description: 1.565 (alpha), 1.559-1.569 (beta), 1.560-1.570 (;-); (-) 0.005. Interference colors are low first-order gray, even for 1 µm particles. The hardness ranges from 2.0 to 2.5; the specific gravity is 2.6Â±. Individual particles are colorless, but the aggregates may be white to gray or yellow to brownish.

records.microscopy description: Kyanite fragments are colorless and transparent (though the edges show a light blue dispersion staining color in Aroclor®); they are often blades, laths (001101) or tablets (001110) but are sometimes equant (001100); the edges are rough, sharp or saw-toothed. The specific gravity ranges from 3.56 to 3.67, the anisotropic hardness from 5.0 to 7.3.
records.Extended description: Kyanite fragments are colorless and transparent (though the edges show a light blue dispersion staining color in Aroclor®); they are often blades, laths (001101) or tablets (001110) but are sometimes equant (001100); some curve in gentle C's or S's. The fragments show transverse cracks and parallel cleavage traces; the edges are rough, sharp or saw-toothed. The specific gravity ranges from 3.56 to 3.67, the anisotropic hardness from 5.0 to 7.3. The indices of this triclinic crystal are 1.712-1.718 (alpha), 1.720-1.725 (beta), 1.727-1.734 (;-); (-) 0.012; 2V=82°. The wider blades usually lie on [001], which is nearly the optic normal; on these cleavage plates, an acute biaxial interference figure can be obtained. Other plates or blades lie on [010] and give an obtuse interference figure. The sign of elongation is positive for [ 100] cleavage and negative for [010] cleavage. The extinction angle (28°) is oblique for the edge formed by [010] and [100].

records.microscopy description: The colorless, transparent plates (001010) , chips and rhombs (001000) show good cleavage in two nearly perpendicular directions. the edges are moderately sharp and uneven or rough.
records.Extended description: The composition of this plagioclase feldspar is intermediate between albite (113) and anorthite; 30-50% is NaAlSi3O5 and the balance is CaAl3Si2O8. The colorless, transparent plates (001010) , chips and rhombs (001000) show good cleavage in two nearly perpendicular directions. The faces are uneven to rough, occasionally with conchoidal fracture; the edges are moderately sharp and uneven or rough. "Albite twinning" (alternate bright and dark bands visible as the crystals are rotated between crossed polars) is seen in less than 5% of the fragments; the extinction angle between the bands is 18 °. Labradorite can have many crystalline inclusions, or microlites, two of which are represented here: magnetite (165) and augite (127). The specific gravity range is 2.60-2.75; the hardness is 5-6. The indices of this triclinic mineral are 1.554-1.563 (alpha), 1.558-1.568 (beta), 1.562-1.573 (;-); (+) 0.008-0.010; 2V = 76-86°. Although labradorite strongly resembles the other plagioclase feldspars, all of them can be differentiated by their indices.

records.microscopy description: Langbeinite is colorless, transparent and equant. The ground material is in the form of chips and sharply jagged fragments with conchoidal fracture. The surface texture is smooth to slightly pitted. Langbeinite is isotropic (1.535).
records.Extended description: Langbeinite is colorless, transparent and equant. The ground material is in the form of chips and sharply jagged fragments with conchoidal fracture. The surface texture is smooth to slightly pitted. Langbeinite is isotropic (1.535). The appearance is morphologically and optically similar to ground glass. It is, of course, soluble in water in contrast with glass. The specific gravity is 2.829; the melting point is 927°C.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless, equant, irregular, embedded crystals are isotropic with a refractive index of 1.50 or, especially in larger particles, slight retardation, 1.508-1.511 (alpha), 1.509-1.511 (gamma); The first-order red plate is helpful in detecting the birefringence. The particles may show surface sculpturing due to multiple, lamellar twinning.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless, equant, irregular, embedded crystals are isotropic with a refractive index of 1.50 or, especially in larger particles, slight retardation, 1.508-1.511 (alpha), 1.509-1.511 (gamma); 0.001. The first-order red plate is helpful in detecting the birefringence. The hard-ness is 5.5-6; the specific gravity is 2.5. The particles may show surface sculpturing due to multiple, lamellar twinning. Inclusions are common; here the inclusions are magnetite, and particles bearing these inclusions respond strongly to the magnet. This sample also contains some feldspar (001000, 001010) with which leucite occurs.

records.microscopy description: The rounded, roughly six-sided plates and sheets of monoclinic lepidolite are colorless and transparent. Some of the larger particles show pseudohexagonal cleavage lines. The birefringence (-) 0.018-0.038, is moderate, but since the optic plane is perpendicular to the dominant cleavage direction, the maximum birefringence observed on the usual plate view is 0.003.
records.Extended description: The rounded, roughly six-sided plates and sheets of monoclinic lepidolite are colorless and transparent. These plates are composed of thin layers which can be cleaved or sheared, though with more difficulty than those of the other micas. The faces are uneven to rough, and many show cleavage traces. Some of the larger particles show pseudohexagonal cleavage lines. The interference colors are a mottled gray due to the disorientations and varying thickness of the lamellae. The indices of lepidolite, 1.525-1.548 (alpha), 1.551-1.580 (beta), 1.554-1.586 (gamma), are lower than those of the other micas. The birefringence (-) 0.018-0.038, is moderate, but since the optic plane is perpendicular to the dominant cleavage direction, the maximum birefringence observed on the usual plate view is 0.003. This sample also contains large quartz particles which have second-order interference colors.

Limestone is a sedimentary rock that contains 95% or more calcite (133), q.v. There are many kinds of limestone, some with up to 50% dolomite (140), q.v. Rhodochrosite (184) , siderite (193) and magnesite (164) strongly resemble calcite and dolomite morphologically but can generally be distinguished by their indices or by microchemical tests. Constituents in limestone may be quartz (183), chalcedony (135) or clay minerals (illite etc.). Aragonite (119) from shell organisms, opal (175) and collophane (136) may also be present.

records.microscopy description: Actually, only about 15% of this sample is limonite which consists of transparent to translucent, yellow to orange and brown, compact, porous, earthy masses of small particles. The isotropic mineraloid has a refractive index of 2.0-2.1 (010100); it may also be weakly birefringent (011100). It is, however, ortho-rhombic, occurring as small acicular crystals, bladed aggregates (011110) and as masses (011100) with a fibrous structure. The transparent to translucent particles are bi-axial, with 2.260 (alpha), 2.393 (beta), 2.398 (gamma);
records.Extended description: Actually, only about 15% of this sample is limonite which consists of transparent to translucent, yellow to orange and brown, compact, porous, earthy masses of small particles. They are amorphous, with a hardness of 5.5 and a specific gravity of 3.8. The isotropic mineraloid has a refractive index of 2.0-2.1 (010100); it may also be weakly birefringent (011100). Clay and organic matter may be intermixed. Goethite, HFeO2, the remainder of the sample, also is yellow to orange and orange-brown. It is, however, ortho-rhombic, occurring as small acicular crystals, bladed aggregates (011110) and as masses (011100) with a fibrous structure. The transparent to translucent particles are bi-axial, with 2.260 (alpha), 2.393 (beta), 2.398 (gamma); (-) 0.138; 2V small to 30°. Pleochroic. Hardness is 5.5; specific gravity is 4.28. Extreme dispersion, and for 610-620 nm uniaxial (-). Limonite and goethite are associated with each other and with lepidocrocite (2V = 83°).

records.microscopy description: In large fragments, these equant particles are opaque, dark green (110000) or black (100000) in top light, and show a striated surface. These are actually fibrous masses. Thin splinters (011111) and other small, broken fragments (011100) are transparent to translucent, dark green, and pleochroic, with X and Y directions bottle green and Z red-brown.
records.Extended description: In large fragments, these equant particles are opaque, dark green (110000) or black (100000) in top light, and show a striated surface. These are actually fibrous masses. Thin splinters (011111) and other small, broken fragments (011100) are transparent to translucent, dark green, and pleochroic, with X and Y directions bottle green and Z red-brown. The orthorhombic crystals have indices of 1.83 (alpha), 1.83 (beta) , 1.97 (gamma); (+) 0.14; 2V small for low iron samples, to 1.85 (alpha), 1.85 (beta), 2.02 (gamma); (+) 0.17; 2V very small for low magnesium samples. Strong dispersion; r > v. Fusible. The hardness is 5; the specific gravity is 3.6-4.7 with increasing iron.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless particles (1-5 µm in this sample) sometimes show prominent rhombohedral cleavage, and may form cleavable or compact porcelainlike masses.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless particles (1-5 µm in this sample) sometimes show prominent rhombohedral cleavage, and may form cleavable or compact porcelainlike masses. The hexagonal crystals have refractive indices of 1.515 (e) and 1.717 (omega) ; (-) 0.202 [for the synthetic 1.509 (e) and 1.700 (omega); (-) 0.191]. High-order whites are common interference colors because of the high birefringence; extinction is symmetrical. The hardness is 4-5.5; specific gravity is 3.0-3.3. Miscible with FeCO3, but limited with CaCO3 and MnCO3. Where Fe and Mg are present in equal amounts, 1.570 (e) and 1.788 (omega); (-) 0.218. Effervesces in HCL Microchemical test for Mg may be necessary. Cf. calcite (133), dolomite (140) and rhodochrosite (184).

records.microscopy description: All particles of this isometric mineral are opaque (100000), even those less than 1 µm across;
records.Extended description: Magnetite, Fe3O4, is the commonest spinel. All particles of this isometric mineral are opaque (100000), even those less than 1 µm across; the reflectivity of crushed fragments is moderately high. The crystals fracture unevenly and rarely show cleavage. Magnetite alters to red iron oxides (391), which can be seen occasionally coating the surface. The crushed fragments will be attracted to one another and cohere in a fluid mount because they are magnetized. They can also be observed to move freely in a mobile liquid mount, e.g., warmed Aroclor®, in response to a magnet moved near the objective.

records.microscopy description: Among these crushed fragments, the elongated prisms (011101) and rhombs (011110) show good cleavage; the chips (011100) and flakes have rounded, rough edges. The faces are rough and uneven due to fine adhering particles and dense cleavage traces which make the larger particles appear fibrous. Some of the elongated prisms show parallel extinction (/3 _J_ 010), but most are oblique. The fibrous, larger pieces do not extinguish.
records.Extended description: Malachite is translucent and pale green (alpha) to deep emerald green (gamma). Among these crushed fragments, the elongated prisms (011101) and rhombs (011110) show good cleavage; the chips (011100) and flakes have rounded, rough edges. The faces are rough and uneven due to fine adhering particles and dense cleavage traces which make the larger particles appear fibrous. Some of the elongated prisms show parallel extinction (/3 _J_ 010), but most are oblique. The fibrous, larger pieces do not extinguish. The indices are 1.655 (alpha), 1.875 (beta), 1. 909 (gamma); (-) 0.254; 2V = 43°. When the crystal is rotated to the extinction position in which it is pale green, contrast is very low and the index is just higher than Aroclor®. The absorption color masks the interference colors and may affect the dispersion staining colors except at thin edges. The specific gravity ranges from 3.9 to 4.03, the hardness from 3.5 to 4.

records.microscopy description: The sample consists of very thin, transparent to translucent flakes and lamellar masses. The rounded, pseudohexagonal flakes have uneven to jagged edges, like muscovite (168). Small pieces are colorless, but larger fragments are shades of brown, green, blue-green or greenish-brown; Per-fect [001] cleavage influences orientation of flakes. The edges of the flakes may be curly.
records.Extended description: The sample consists of very thin, transparent to translucent flakes and lamellar masses. The rounded, pseudohexagonal flakes have uneven to jagged edges, like muscovite (168). Small pieces are colorless, but larger fragments are shades of brown, green, blue-green or greenish-brown; they are pleochroic. Manganese may replace iron, lithium may replace aluminum, and magnesium may be absent. The indices will, therefore, vary: 1.565-1.625 (alpha), 1.605-1.675 (gamma); (-) 0.040- 0.060; 2V=0 to 25, usually <10°. Per-fect [001] cleavage influences orientation of flakes. Hardness is 2.5-3; specific gravity is about 2.90. Inclusions, especially zircon, are common. The edges of the flakes may be curly. The extinction in bent plates is wavy. Basal sections show a centered Bxa figure, but little or no pleochroism.

records.microscopy description: This sample consists of very thin sheets (001010 and flakes (less than 5 µm thick) which have extremely low contrast even though their refractive index is 0.08 index units below Aroclor®. The rounded, rectangular plates have uneven, continuous edges. The surfaces show some cleavage traces and are uneven because the particles are made of smaller, randomly stacked plates. Flat flakes show a faint acute bisectrix interference figure due to their thinness and low birefringence.
records.Extended description: This sample consists of very thin sheets (001010 and flakes (less than 5 µm thick) which have extremely low contrast even though their refractive index is 0.08 index units below Aroclor®. The rounded, rectangular plates have uneven, continuous edges. The surfaces show some cleavage traces and are uneven because the particles are made of smaller, randomly stacked plates. This stacking imparts a mottled gray color between crossed polars. The birefringence (0.006) is low for cleavage fragments. The edge view of the plates shows much higher birefringence (-0.036). In this position, they look like fine needles or, if they are slightly tilted, thin chips. The indices of mono-clinic muscovite are 1.552 (alpha), 1.582 (beta), 1.588 (gamma); 2V = 40°. Flat flakes show a faint acute bisectrix interference figure due to their thinness and low birefringence. The specific gravity range is 2. 73-3, the hardness 2-2.5. Like many other mineral samples, this one contains quartz (183).

records.microscopy description: These are colorless, transparent to translucent chips (001000) and plates (001010), some elongated, with occasional rhombs and triangular fragments.
records.Extended description: These are colorless, transparent to translucent chips (001000) and plates (001010), some elongated, with occasional rhombs and triangular fragments. Almost all show good cleavage for one plane, some for two; the faces are uneven to rough with infrequent conchoidal fracture. Crossed polars reveal the most distinctive characteristic two perpendicular sets of twin bands that look like cross-hatching. One set of parallel lamellae consists of fine, "albite-twinned," alternately dark and light bands; the bands of the other set, at right angles to the first, are broader. The indices, which must be determined on fragments not showing this twinning, are 1.518 (alpha), 1.522 (beta), 1.525 (gamma); (-) 0.007; 2V = 83 °. Microcline is triclinic. Its specific gravity is 2.5; the hardness is 6.

records.microscopy description: Commercially mined monazite sand is composed of ellip-soidal, spherical (011100) or potato-shaped, salmon-colored, translucent grains. The surfaces are cracked and finely pitted, appearing veined; The grains are not noticeably pleochroic, and their color does not affect the interference color. Most grains yield an optic normal figure.
records.Extended description: Commercially mined monazite sand is composed of ellip-soidal, spherical (011100) or potato-shaped, salmon-colored, translucent grains. The surfaces are cracked and finely pitted, appearing veined; some bear dark orange deposits of alteration product. Dark red-brown inclusions of zircon (212) and rutile (186) occur frequently. The grains are not noticeably pleochroic, and their color does not affect the interference color. Monazite is monoclinic and has indices of 1.785-1.800 (alpha), 1.787-1.801 (beta), 1.837-1.849 (gamma); (+) 0.045-0.055; 2V=6-19°. Most grains yield an optic normal figure.

records.microscopy description: elongated prisms with fibrous-looking surfaces-all of these characterize natrolite. Some of the particles are cleaved transversely into equant fragments (001000). All are transparent to translucent and colorless.
records.Extended description: Very fine rods (001001) with rough edges; rough, heavily striated columns; elongated prisms with fibrous-looking surfaces-all of these characterize natrolite. Some of the particles are cleaved transversely into equant fragments (001000). All are transparent to translucent and colorless. Natrolite is orthorhombic and has indices of 1.473-1.489 (alpha), 1.476-1.491 (beta), 1.485-1.502 (gamma); (+) 0.011-0.014; 2V = 60-63°. Extinction is parallel and complete; the sign of elongation is positive. All of the fragments show an optic normal or obtuse bisectrix interference figure. The crystals have a specific gravity of 2.2 and a hardness of 5.

records.microscopy description: Nephelite fragments are sharply angular, equant chips (001000); some elongated pieces are prismatic and show poor cleavage. The fragments are colorless and transparent to translucent.
records.Extended description: Nephelite resembles quartz (183) so closely that the two can be distinguished microscopically only by their optical properties. Nephelite fragments are sharply angular, equant chips (001000); some elongated pieces are prismatic and show poor cleavage. The edges are uneven to rough, and the faces are generally uneven with conchoidal fracture. The fragments are colorless and transparent to translucent. Indices range from 1.528-1.544 (E) to 1.531-1.519 (omega); (-) 0.003-0.005. The specific gravity is 2.6, the hardness 6. Quartz never occurs with nephelite, but feldspars, such as the microcline (169) in this sample, are usually associated with it.

records.microscopy description: The transparent to translucent, compact, fibrous particles in this sample are an amphibole of variable composition ranging from tremolite (205) (white in mass) to actinolite (green in mass, due to iron). Breaks with splintery fracture (001111) or as equant fragments (001100). The fibrous masses here show undulose extinction. The colorless to green, monoclinic crystals have indices of 1.654-1.673 (alpha), 1.659-1.679 (beta), 1.667-1.693 (gamma);
records.Extended description: The transparent to translucent, compact, fibrous particles in this sample are an amphibole of variable composition ranging from tremolite (205) (white in mass) to actinolite (green in mass, due to iron). Breaks with splintery fracture (001111) or as equant fragments (001100). The hardness is 6-6.5; specific gravity is 2.96-3.1. The fibrous masses here show undulose extinction. Nephrite is one of the two species properly included in the general term "jade"-the other being jadeite of the pyroxene group. Jadeite grades from (Na,Ca) (Al,Mg) (Si,Al) 2O6 to (Ca,Na) (Mg,Fe,Al) (Si,AlhO6. The colorless to green, monoclinic crystals have indices of 1.654-1.673 (alpha), 1.659-1.679 (beta), 1.667-1.693 (gamma); 0.012-0.027; 2V = 70-80°. It is distinguished from nephrite by having higher indices and a larger extinction angle (35°).

records.microscopy description: Olivine fragments are colorless, transparent, sharply angular, platy chips (001110). Two other components in this sample are spinel-translucent to opaque, deep greenish-brown, isotropic chips with an index significantly higher than Aroclor®; and garnet (145-148)-pale green, isotropic, rough tablets with an index much lower than Aroclor®. The garnet fragments contain opaque dendrites.
records.Extended description: Olivine fragments are colorless, transparent, sharply angular, platy chips (001110). The edges show blue to orange annular stop dispersion colors, indicating that the crystals are close in index and have a dispersion significantly different from Aroclor®. The faces are smooth to uneven, with conchoidal fracture; no cleavage planes are evident. The indices of orthorhombic olivine are 1.635-1.655 (alpha), 1.65-1.67 (beta), 1.67-1.69 (gamma); (+) 0.034-0.037; 2V = 70-90°. The specific gravity is 3.3, and the hardness is 7. The dispersion staining colors in plane polarized light in Aroclor® with a central stop are golden magenta for one extinction position and bluish magenta for the perpendicular position. Two other components in this sample are spinel-translucent to opaque, deep greenish-brown, isotropic chips with an index significantly higher than Aroclor®; and garnet (145-148)-pale green, isotropic, rough tablets with an index much lower than Aroclor®. The garnet fragments contain opaque dendrites.

records.microscopy description: These are colorless, translucent, very rough, sharp-edged chips (000000). They contain many cavities, and the faces of broken grains appear heavily pitted or pocked. bits of pumice less than 10 µm across look like glass powder with perhaps some evidence of "fire-polishing."
records.Extended description: These are colorless, translucent, very rough, sharp-edged chips (000000). They contain many cavities, and the faces of broken grains appear heavily pitted or pocked. The refractive index of this amorphous substance varies from 1.406 to 1.460 as the amount of water decreases. The specific gravity range is 1.9-2.3; the hardness range is 5.5-6.5. Pumice (226) strongly resembles opal, but it is usually porous with conchoidal fracture and it appears heavily twisted; bits of pumice less than 10 µm across look like glass powder with perhaps some evidence of "fire-polishing."

records.microscopy description: Fragments of orthoclase, one of the commonest silicates, are colorless, transparent to translucent and equant (001000), prismatic or tabular (001010). The edges are unevenly angular, and the faces are uneven to rough, mostly due to conchoidal fracture.
records.Extended description: Fragments of orthoclase, one of the commonest silicates, are colorless, transparent to translucent and equant (001000), prismatic or tabular (001010). The edges are unevenly angular, and the faces are uneven to rough, mostly due to conchoidal fracture. The cleavage prisms of this monoclinic mineral have a negative sign of elongation. The specific gravity is 2.6, and the hardness is 6. The indices, 1.519 (alpha), 1.523 (beta), 1.525 (gamma), are all less than those of quartz (183). The birefringence is (-) 0.006; 2V = 70°. The lack of lamellar twin bands differentiates orthoclase from microcline (169) and labradorite (157).

records.microscopy description: The transparent, isotropic fragments have a conchoidal fracture and vitreous luster. They are amorphous and structureless but usually with sharp edges, resembling ground glass. Very large pieces may be colorless, gray, black, and even green, brown and red, but in microscopic sizes they are all colorless. The fragments contain inclusions of elongated gas bubbles, almost rounded rectangular, like those that appear in furnace slags. They take the form of radiating and/ or twisting hairlike structures.
records.Extended description: This is one of the principal varieties of volcanic glass, along with pumice (226) and perlite (529). The transparent, isotropic fragments have a conchoidal fracture and vitreous luster. They are amorphous and structureless but usually with sharp edges, resembling ground glass. The composition is variable but is primarily a mixture of silicon dioxide and aluminium oxide, with oxides of iron, magnesium, calcium, sodium and potassium also present. The refractive index range is 1.48-1.51, with most samples about 1.495. Very large pieces may be colorless, gray, black, and even green, brown and red, but in microscopic sizes they are all colorless. The hardness is 5-7, and the specific gravity is 2.2-2.7, depending on composition. The fragments contain inclusions of elongated gas bubbles, almost rounded rectangular, like those that appear in furnace slags. There are crystallites, especially trichites, which are very common in obsidian. These are inclusions which are between amorphous matter and true crystals. They take the form of radiating and/ or twisting hairlike structures. Very minute fragments of obsidian without inclusions are very difficult to distinguish from ground glass. Obsidian fuses to a vesicular enamel.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless (001000) to pale green (011000) particles of an aluminum amphibole are monoclinic and show cleavage in two directions; The crystals are pleochroic when colored with iron. Most of the particles in this sample show longitudinal striations from the cleavage, and narrow, elongated air bubbles.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless (001000) to pale green (011000) particles of an aluminum amphibole are monoclinic and show cleavage in two directions; some small pieces may be blades (001011). The high refractive index Z direction is inclined to the c axis by about 26°; optically (+), with 2V ~ 60°, r > v. The crystals are pleochroic when colored with iron. Pargasite grades into edenite with decreased iron: 1.606--1.649 (alpha),1.617-1.660 (beta), 1.631-1.672 (gamma) ; (+) 0.016--0.023 (increases with iron; decreases as F replaces OH). Both edenite and pargasite grade into hornblende (152), q.v. The specific gravity is 3.05-3.47. Most of the particles in this sample show longitudinal striations from the cleavage, and narrow, elongated air bubbles.

records.microscopy description: Pectolite particles are very fine needles, either single or in bundles or sheaves. Individual needles (some are very thin rods) are colorless and transparent (001001), while the bundles are light brown and translucent (011001).
records.Extended description: Pectolite particles are very fine needles, either single or in bundles or sheaves. Individual needles (some are very thin rods) are colorless and transparent (001001), while the bundles are light brown and translucent (011001). The smaller bundles appear splintery. All of the fragments have a positive sign of elongation. The specific gravity is 2.8, the hardness 5. Indices of 1.594-1.610 (alpha), 1.603-1.614 (beta) and 1.631-1.642 (y) distinguish this triclinic mineral from natrolite (171) and steatite (199). The dispersion staining colors in plane polarized light, parallel to the long axis, are central stop-very pale blue with blue-white Becke line; and annular stop-dark orange-red. Some

records.microscopy description: Pectolite particles are very fine needles, either single or in bundles or sheaves. Individual needles (some are very thin rods) are colorless and transparent (001001), while the bundles are light brown and translucent (011001).
records.Extended description: Pectolite particles are very fine needles, either single or in bundles or sheaves. Individual needles (some are very thin rods) are colorless and transparent (001001), while the bundles are light brown and translucent (011001). The smaller bundles appear splintery. All of the fragments have a positive sign of elongation. The specific gravity is 2.8, the hardness 5. Indices of 1.594-1.610 (alpha), 1.603-1.614 (beta) and 1.631-1.642 (y) distinguish this triclinic mineral from natrolite (171) and steatite (199). The dispersion staining colors in plane polarized light, parallel to the long axis, are central stop-very pale blue with blue-white Becke line; and annular stop-dark orange-red. Some calcite (133), and probably nephelite (172), fragments

records.microscopy description: Individual grains of periclase are polygonal but rounded. The larger, very rough fragments are slightly rounded and elongated or equant. The surface roughness is due to the intergranular fracture. The grains look as if much smaller grains had been plucked out of their surface. The fragments are translucent and colorless with a faint blue edge (dispersion staining) in Aroclor®. This sample contains many birefringent inclusions of pseudomorphic magnesite (164)
records.Extended description: Individual grains of periclase are polygonal but rounded. The larger, very rough fragments are slightly rounded and elongated or equant. The surface roughness is due to the intergranular fracture. The grains look as if much smaller grains had been plucked out of their surface. The fragments are translucent and colorless with a faint blue edge (dispersion staining) in Aroclor®. The hardness is 6, and the specific gravity is 3.8. The refractive index ranges from 1.736 to 1.745. This sample contains many birefringent inclusions of pseudomorphic magnesite (164)

records.microscopy description: Prehnite particles are colorless, transparent to translucent, and equant (001000), tabular (001010) or somewhat elongated. The edges are angular and rough to uneven. Prismatic fragments with lengthwise striations have a negative sign of elongation.
records.Extended description: Prehnite particles are colorless, transparent to translucent, and equant (001000), tabular (001010) or somewhat elongated. The edges are angular and rough to uneven. The faces have two sets of moderately faint, fine striations, each nearly perpendicular to the other; in some, one dominant set of striations looks like icicles. These crystals do not extinguish between crossed polars as the stage is rotated but show a very deep blue at the extinction position, changing to dirty orange and then to first-order white. This is due to internal disorientation of crystallites. Other twinning striation pairs appear oblique to an edge, like feathers on an arrow. Prismatic fragments with lengthwise striations have a negative sign of elongation. The indices of orthorhombic prehnite are 1.610-1.637 (alpha), 1.615-1.647 (beta), 1.632-1.670 (gamma); (+) 0.020-0.035; 2V=64-70°. The specific gravity is 2.9, and the hardness is 6.5.

records.microscopy description: Crystals may usually be colorless except in bulk when they may be pale yellow, green, blue or brownish green. Individual crystals may be as large as 100 µm but are usually smaller.
records.Extended description: A talclike mineral made up grossly of radially grouped foliated masses consisting of cleavable biaxial crystals. The monoclinic crystals have refractive indices 1.534-1.556 (alpha), 1.586-1.589 (beta) and 1.596-1.601 (gamma); (-) ~0.050; extinction may be slightly undulose. The density is 2.65-2.90 with a hardness on the Moh scale of 1-2. Cleavage is perfect parallel to [001]. Crystals may usually be colorless except in bulk when they may be pale yellow, green, blue or brownish green. Individual crystals may be as large as 100 µm but are usually smaller. It is differentiated from talc by its larger optic axial angle-53-62 ° compared with ~30° for talc. Pyrophyllite is also an aluminum silicate, whereas talc is a magnesium silicate.

records.microscopy description: The fragments are colorless, transparent to translucent, sharply angular chips (001000).
records.Extended description: One of the commonest minerals, quartz occurs in nearly every dust sample. The fragments are colorless, transparent to translucent, sharply angular chips (001000). Faces often show marked conchoidal fracture; rarely cleavage. Large crystals often have gas-liquid inclusions. Quartz is hexagonal with indices of 1.553 (epsilon) and 1.544 (omega); (+) 0.009. The specific gravity is 2.7, and the hardness is 7. See also quartz molding sand (411).

records.microscopy description: The transparent to translucent, crushed fragments, because of their perfect rhombohedral [1011] cleavage, are frequently seen as rhombohedra. This mineral is usually colorless (001100) but may also be pink, red or brownish red (011100) in larger fragments.
records.Extended description: The transparent to translucent, crushed fragments, because of their perfect rhombohedral [1011] cleavage, are frequently seen as rhombohedra. The refractive indices are 1.597 (1:) and 1.816 (omega); (-) 0.219. Note the extreme birefringence of this uniaxial mineral. It is completely isomorphous with calcite (133) and siderite (193). Calcium and iron are usually present as replacing elements. The indices decrease with increasing calcium, and increase with increasing iron. Cleavage fragments give an off-center uniaxial interference figure with many color rings. This mineral is usually colorless (001100) but may also be pink, red or brownish red (011100) in larger fragments. The hardness is 4; the specific gravity is 3.5Â±. Extinction is symmetrical. The mineral alters readily to pyrolusite. Rhodonite (185) and quartz (183) are common associates. The addition of hot ammonium paramolybdate gives reddish-orange pleochroic crystals with rhodochrosite.

records.microscopy description: Fragments of rhodonite are faintly salmon-colored, transparent to translucent, elongated prisms (011101), rhombs (011110) and equant (011100) particles. the faces, also uneven, are faintly striated with cleavage traces parallel to the prism length.
records.Extended description: Fragments of rhodonite are faintly salmon-colored, transparent to translucent, elongated prisms (011101), rhombs (011110) and equant (011100) particles. The uneven to rough edges show a blue Becke line in Aroclor®; the faces, also uneven, are faintly striated with cleavage traces parallel to the prism length. Extinction is oblique, and the sign of elongation is positive. An off-center optic axis figure is seen on most prisms. The specific gravity is 3.6, and the hardness is 6. Rhodonite is triclinic and has indices of 1.711-1.738 (alpha), 1.714-1.741 (beta), 1.724-1.751 (y); (+) 0.011-0.014; 2V = 61-76°. The dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® are: annular stop-blue-gray with some black edges; central stop-golden white with white Becke line. Rhodonite is distinguished from kyanite (156) by its cleavage plates, which give nearly centered, obtuse or acute, biaxial interference figures.

records.microscopy description: Rutile fragments are light gold to bright amber, translucent to nearly opaque and very sharply angular (011100). These equant chips show unusually high contrast due to the extremely high indices: 2.9 (1:) and 2.6 (omega); Although rutile resembles sphalerite (196), the two are easily distinguished because sphalerite is isotropic and shows cleavage fragments.
records.Extended description: Rutile fragments are light gold to bright amber, translucent to nearly opaque and very sharply angular (011100). These equant chips show unusually high contrast due to the extremely high indices: 2.9 (1:) and 2.6 (omega); (+) 0.3. The edges are uneven, and the faces have well-marked conchoidal fractures; no cleavage is evident in this sample. Some fragments are banded with irregular red-orange areas. The interference colors are somewhat masked by the absorption color. Although rutile resembles sphalerite (196), the two are easily distinguished because sphalerite is isotropic and shows cleavage fragments.

records.microscopy description: The particles in this sample are optically and chemically identical to rutile (186) above. The high degree of rounding of these particles is due to water attrition. There are several particles of zircon (212) in this sample also.
records.Extended description: The particles in this sample are optically and chemically identical to rutile (186) above. The high degree of rounding of these particles is due to water attrition. This sample comes from Australia, where many rutile sand beaches are located. There are several particles of zircon (212) in this sample also.

records.microscopy description: The individual sand grains are cemented together to form the sedimentary rock, sandstone. The surfaces of the grains are etched and pitted where the cement adhered.
records.Extended description: Optically and chemically, these particles are identical to quartz (183), q.v. The individual quartz sand grains are rounded, indicating attrition in the geological past. The individual sand grains are cemented together to form the sedimentary rock, sandstone. The surfaces of the grains are etched and pitted where the cement adhered. Sand-stones are cemented with a variety of substances such as clay minerals, muscovite and calcite, but in this sample the interstitial cement seen adhering to the grains is siliceous, detrital quartz in particle size much less than 1 µm. The cement is brownish due to iron oxide.

records.microscopy description: Whether individual grains come from a desert (wind-worn sand, 190) or from water (river, ocean etc.) may be impossible to tell, but a number of observations on differences may be made: (alpha) water-worn sand shows glossy and highly polished grains even in indentations and crevices, due to chemical action in water; (b) careful focus on the grain profile and surface shows no angularity even in the smallest indentations; (c) there are no adhering small particles on the grains; (d) rivers size-separate their sediment more selectively than wind so that grains of similar size are apt to be deposited close together.
records.Extended description: The chemical and optical properties of these particles are identical to those of quartz (183), q.v. Sand originate from the chemical and mechanical disintegration of gneiss and granite (150). Whether individual grains come from a desert (wind-worn sand, 190) or from water (river, ocean etc.) may be impossible to tell, but a number of observations on differences may be made: (alpha) water-worn sand shows glossy and highly polished grains even in indentations and crevices, due to chemical action in water; (b) careful focus on the grain profile and surface shows no angularity even in the smallest indentations; (c) there are no adhering small particles on the grains; (d) rivers size-separate their sediment more selectively than wind so that grains of similar size are apt to be deposited close together. Cf. wind-worn sand (190), rutile beach sand (187) and zircon (212).

records.microscopy description: It may not be possible to distinguish between wind-worn (desert) and water-worn grains, but a number of observa-tions on wind-worn sand may be made: (alpha) unmounted desert sand grains have a frosted surface due to the chemical action attending the wetting by dew and drying by the sun; (b) careful focus on the grain profile and surface shows angularity remaining in the indentations and crevices; (c) small particles adhere to the surface of the grains; (d) desert sands tend to have a wide assortment of grain sizes; (e) the surface shows spalling caused by grain-to-grain collisions. There may also be 5-20 µm, polygonal shrinkage cracks attributed to the shrinkage of an altered silica layer due to the daily variations of humidity and temperature in the desert climate.
records.Extended description: The chemical and optical properties of these particles of quartz sand are identical to those of quartz (183), q.v. It may not be possible to distinguish between wind-worn (desert) and water-worn grains, but a number of observa-tions on wind-worn sand may be made: (alpha) unmounted desert sand grains have a frosted surface due to the chemical action attending the wetting by dew and drying by the sun; (b) careful focus on the grain profile and surface shows angularity remaining in the indentations and crevices; (c) small particles adhere to the surface of the grains; (d) desert sands tend to have a wide assortment of grain sizes; (e) the surface shows spalling caused by grain-to-grain collisions. There may also be 5-20 µm, polygonal shrinkage cracks attributed to the shrinkage of an altered silica layer due to the daily variations of humidity and temperature in the desert climate. Cf. water-worn sand (189).

records.microscopy description: Approximately 80% of these particles are scheelite; the remainder are opaque particles of wolframite (100000), with which scheelite is often associated. Scheelite fragments are sharp, angular, colorless and transparent to translucent. The chips are equant (001100) with no evident cleavage; Some grains show orange inclusions which are probably rutile (186).
records.Extended description: Approximately 80% of these particles are scheelite; the remainder are opaque particles of wolframite (100000), with which scheelite is often associated. Scheelite fragments are sharp, angular, colorless and transparent to translucent. The chips are equant (001100) with no evident cleavage; the edges and faces are uneven to rough, exhibiting conchoidal fracture. Some grains show orange inclusions which are probably rutile (186). The refractive indices of this tetragonal mineral are 1.934 (e) and 1.918 (omega); (+) 0.016. The specific gravity is 6; the hardness is 5.

records.microscopy description: Shale is a fine-grained, thinly bedded rock formed largely by the hardening of clay-size and/ or silt-size particles.
records.Extended description: Shale is a fine-grained, thinly bedded rock formed largely by the hardening of clay-size and/ or silt-size particles. The exact mineral composition may not be easily determined microscopically. Coarse particles of, e.g., quartz (183), feldspar (113, 157, 169, 176), muscovite (168), horn-blende (152), magnetite (165), zircon (212) are set in a microcrystalline to cryptocrystalline matrix of clay minerals such as montmorillonite and kaolinite (155); quartz (183), limonite (162), sericite, carbonaceous material etc. Glauconite (149), collophane (136) and carbonates (133, 140) are other constituents. This sample shows a quartzose (001000) variety with calcareous (limestone) (001000), carbonaceous (100000) and pyritic (100000) material in the matrix. Other varieties may be feldspars, micas, chlorites or carbonaceous.

records.microscopy description: Shale is a fine-grained, thinly bedded rock formed largely by the hardening of clay-size and/ or silt-size particles.
records.Extended description: Shale is a fine-grained, thinly bedded rock formed largely by the hardening of clay-size and/ or silt-size particles. The exact mineral composition may not be easily determined microscopically. Coarse particles of, e.g., quartz (183), feldspar (113, 157, 169, 176), muscovite (168), horn-blende (152), magnetite (165), zircon (212) are set in a microcrystalline to cryptocrystalline matrix of clay minerals such as montmorillonite and kaolinite (155); quartz (183), limonite (162), sericite, carbonaceous material etc. Glauconite (149), collophane (136) and carbonates (133, 140) are other constituents. This sample shows a quartzose (001000) variety with calcareous (limestone) (001000), carbonaceous (100000) and pyritic (100000) material in the matrix. Other varieties may be feldspars, micas, chlorites or carbonaceous.

records.microscopy description: Siderite particles are almost exclusively colorless (001110) to pale amber (011110) rhombohedra. Some of the rhombs are elongated, appearing prismatic.
records.Extended description: Siderite particles are almost exclusively colorless (001110) to pale amber (011110) rhombohedra. Some of the rhombs are elongated, appearing prismatic. The faces and edges of most fragments are even, but some show wide, irregular cracks in two directions, paralleling the edges of the rhombohedra. All of the cleavage rhombo-hedra have indices greater than Aroclor®. The acute rhomb angle is bisected by Â£', the obtuse angle by eu. The refrac-tive indices of hexagonal siderite are 1. 788-1.875 (omega), 1.570-1.633 (epsilon), 1.673-1.748 (epsilon-prime); (-) 0.218-0.242. An off-center uniaxial interference figure can be obtained on all of the rhombs. Siderite has much higher indices than calcite (133), with which it might be confused. Hematite is seen here in a deep gray to red pseudomorph of siderite which is nearly opaque; some of the partially altered rhombs are bright red. Siderite has a specific gravity of 3.8-3.9; the hardness is 3.5-4.

Slate is a hard, fine-grained rock with highly developed foliation (slaty cleavage) in large pieces, formed by metamorphism of shale (192). The minerals of slates are not all identified microscopically; unresolved fractions of the matrix material require x-ray diffraction. The coarser constituents include quartz (183), sericite, chlorite, magnetite (165) , biotite (167) , hematite (390) , calcite (133) , dolomite (140) and organic material. The cryptocrystalline matrix consists (by x-ray) of illite and chloritic type clay minerals. In this sample, quartz (183) (001000), limestone (161) (001000) and organic material (100000) are identifiable.

records.microscopy description: Crushed fragments of sodalite are colorless, transparent, equant (000000) to elongated plates and chips. Cleavage planes can be seen on several particles, but most are fractured (conchoidal) with uneven faces. Some rounded particles are very rough and at high magnifications can be seen to be composed of single crystals.
records.Extended description: Crushed fragments of sodalite are colorless, transparent, equant (000000) to elongated plates and chips. Cleavage planes can be seen on several particles, but most are fractured (conchoidal) with uneven faces. Some rounded particles are very rough and at high magnifications can be seen to be composed of single crystals. The roughness is due to the voids left by removal of individual crystals. Minute, subspherical bits and well-formed rhombohedra of calcite (133) (001000) are occluded in sodalite. Magnetite (165) (100000) is also associated with this sample. Sodalite is isometric, with an index range of 1.483-1.487. It is similar to periclase (180) (which has a much higher index) and almandite garnet (145) (which has poor cleavage as well as a higher index). The specific gravity is 2.3, and the hardness is 5.5-6.

records.microscopy description: Crushed sphalerite consists of translucent, colorless to pale yellow to greenish yellow, equant chips (010100) showing dodecahedral cleavage and fragments that are rhomb-shaped or tetrahedral.
records.Extended description: Crushed sphalerite consists of translucent, colorless to pale yellow to greenish yellow, equant chips (010100) showing dodecahedral cleavage and fragments that are rhomb-shaped or tetrahedral. The contrast is very high, the refractive index range is 2.370-2.428 and the faces are scarred with cleavage lines and conchoidal fracture. Some of the crystals show extremely weak, abnormal birefringence (sphalerite is isometric) with incomplete fanlike extinction. The specific gravity ranges from 3.9 to 4.1, hardness from 3.5 to 4.

records.microscopy description: The colorless, transparent fragments of spodumene are laths or blades with uneven, irregularly protruding ends. Some of the fragments show birefringent occlusions which are probably albite (113).
records.Extended description: The colorless, transparent fragments of spodumene are laths or blades with uneven, irregularly protruding ends. All the crystals show thin, rodlike furrows parallel to the long edge. The blades and laths have positive elongation and oblique extinction (12-18°). The refractive indices of monoclinic spodumene are 1.618-1.661 (alpha), 1.655-1.670 (beta), 1.662-1.679 (gamma); (+) 0.014-0.027; 2V = 54-69°. Some of the fragments show birefringent occlusions which are probably albite (113). The specific gravity is 3.2, and and the hardness is 6. The dispersion colors (in Aroclor®) parallel to the long axis are greenish blue with an annular stop, magenta-gold with a central stop. The dispersion staining colors parallel to the short axis are yellow-green with an annular stop, bluish magenta with a central stop.

records.microscopy description: These are colorless, translucent, fibrous (001001) and platy (001010) aggregates.
records.Extended description: These are colorless, translucent, fibrous (001001) and platy (001010) aggregates. Turned on edge, the thin plates look like fine, uneven needles (001001). Talc is otherwise similar to steatite (199) but smaller.

records.microscopy description: Steatite particles are larger than those of talc (116), but the two are chemically similar. Colorless, transparent to translucent blades (001010). Somewhat rounded (001000) to elongated, fibrous, colorless, translucent aggregates of much smaller blades (001001). These fibrous aggregates have incomplete undulose extinction.
records.Extended description: Steatite particles are larger than those of talc (116), but the two are chemically similar. This sample contains two kinds of talc cleavage fragments: 1. Colorless, transparent to translucent blades (001010). 2. Somewhat rounded (001000) to elongated, fibrous, colorless, translucent aggregates of much smaller blades (001001). Many of the blades are separated and can be instinctly seen. These fibrous aggregates have incomplete undulose extinction. All of the fragments have positive elongation. The individual blades normally show oblique extinction. The refractive indices of monoclinic steatite talc are 1.539 (alpha), 1.589 (beta), 1.589 (gamma); (-) 0.050; 2V = 0.60°. The specific gravity is 2.7, and the hardness range is 1-1.5.

records.microscopy description: taconite ore dust | The particle size range is <1-200 µm.
records.Extended description: Taconite ore is a low grade iron ore consisting essentially of a mixture of hematite and silica (also magnetite and hydrous iron silicates) and containing about 25% iron. Specifically, this sample from Minnesota consists of about 65% hematite (390) (011100), 20% magnetite (165) (100000) and 15% quartz (183)(001000). The particle size range is <1-200 µm.

records.microscopy description: Thaumasite particles are transparent, colorless, hexagonal, elongated prisms (001001) with jagged to plane ends.
records.Extended description: Thaumasite particles are transparent, colorless, hexagonal, elongated prisms (001001) with jagged to plane ends. Some of the smaller prisms are stubby, occasionally tapering (001000). The prisms have negative elongation and parallel extinction. This hexagonal mineral has indices of 1.468 (Â£) and 1.507 (omega); (-) 0.039. The specific gravity is 1.88; the hardness is 3.5.

records.microscopy description: Titanite resembles rutile (186) (which has a much higher index) and sphalerite (196) (which is isotropic). It is colorless to moderate amber. The crushed crystals are equant (011100) to elongated, sharply angular chips.
records.Extended description: Titanite resembles rutile (186) (which has a much higher index) and sphalerite (196) (which is isotropic). It is colorless to moderate amber. The crushed crystals are equant (011100) to elongated, sharply angular chips. The uneven to rough faces are heavily marked with conchoidal striations but show no cleavage. Monoclinic titanite has indices of 1.840-1.950 (alpha) , 1.870-2.034 (beta), 1.943-2.110 (gamma); (+) 0.100-0.192; 2V=20-56°. The larger, darker fragments are pleochroic, changing from amber to pale amber. The specific gravity is 3.5, the hardness 5.5. This sample includes some bits of opaque magnetite (165) (100000).

records.microscopy description: Tourmaline fragments are colorless, transparent, sharply angular plates (001010) and chips (001000) with no cleavage.
records.Extended description: Tourmaline fragments are colorless, transparent, sharply angular plates (001010) and chips (001000) with no cleavage. The faces are uneven (because of faint conchoidal fracture) to rough (due to numerous gaseous inclusions) with even to ragged edges. Tourmaline is hexagonal with indices of 1.622 (Â£) and 1.637 (omega); (-) 0.02. The specific gravity is 3.1; the hardness is 7. The positive birefringence of topaz (204) distinguishes it from this mineral. Tourmaline shows dispersion staining colors in Aroclor®: red-orange with an annular stop, and blue with a blue-green Becke line with a central stop.

records.microscopy description: Crushed topaz consists of transparent, sharply angular flakes and chips (001000) devoid of color.
records.Extended description: Crushed topaz consists of transparent, sharply angular flakes and chips (001000) devoid of color. The edges and faces are uneven due to conchoidal fracture. Topaz is orthorhombic and has indices of 1.606-1.629 (alpha), 1.609-1.631 (beta), 1.616-1.638 (gamma); (+) 0.009-0.0ll. It resembles quartz (183) but has much lower contrast in Aroclor®. Its dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® are blue with a blue-green Becke line when a central stop is used, orange-yellow when an annular stop is used. The specific gravity is 3.5, and the hardness is 8.

records.microscopy description: These are colorless, transparent, elongated prisms (001001) (some furrowed parallel to their length), rhomb-shaped fragments (001010) and irregular chips (001000).
records.Extended description: These are colorless, transparent, elongated prisms (001001) (some furrowed parallel to their length), rhomb-shaped fragments (001010) and irregular chips (001000). The ends of the prisms are uneven to jagged; the faces are smooth to uneven except for the occasional furrows. Extinction is oblique, and the elongation is positive. Tremolite is monoclinic, with indices of 1.599-1.612 (alpha), 1.613-1.626 (beta), 1.625-1.637 (,1); (-) 0.022-0.027; 2V=80-88°. The dispersion staining colors are faint reddish yellow with an annular stop and faint reddish blue with a central stop when the cleavage fragments are parallel to the polar vibration direction. The specific gravity is 3.1, and the hardness is 5.5. Approximately 2% of this sample is quartz (183) (001000).

records.microscopy description: This ore has been ground to a maximum size of 150 µm and roasted at 425°C. The uranium bearing portion constitutes less than 5% of the sample and consists of transparent, light yellow, small, equant particles with an index >1.66 (0lll00).
records.Extended description: This ore has been ground to a maximum size of 150 µm and roasted at 425°C. The sample here consists of 70% limestone (161) (001000); 15% feldspars (113, 157, 169, 176) (001000, 001010); and 10% quartz (183) (001000). The uranium bearing portion constitutes less than 5% of the sample and consists of transparent, light yellow, small, equant particles with an index >1.66 (0lll00).

records.microscopy description: These are irregular, transparent to opaque, colorless to yellow and golden flakes and plates (001000, 001010 and 011010) of layered mica. Particles in this sample average 250 µm across (10-1500 µm). Under top lighting, the surface is colorless to milky white, and shades of yellow and orange; many particles are iridescent red, green and white and sparkle markedly. This biaxial, negative monoclinic mineral is pleochroic-colorless or pale green perpendicular to the plate and pale brown, yellow-green and brownish-green parallel to the plate. This sample has been heated and the thin parallel layers produce a form of iridescence.
records.Extended description: These are irregular, transparent to opaque, colorless to yellow and golden flakes and plates (001000, 001010 and 011010) of layered mica. Particles in this sample average 250 µm across (10-1500 µm). Under top lighting, the surface is colorless to milky white, and shades of yellow and orange; many particles are iridescent red, green and white and sparkle markedly. This biaxial, negative monoclinic mineral is pleochroic-colorless or pale green perpendicular to the plate and pale brown, yellow-green and brownish-green parallel to the plate. Its indices are 1.525-1.561 (alpha) to 1.545-1.581 (gamma); (-) 0.020-0.031; 2V = 0-8°. This sample has been heated and the thin parallel layers produce a form of iridescence. Other samples of vermiculite may not show so much color.

records.microscopy description: Crushed fragments of vesuvianite are rough and equant (001100). Vesuvianite strongly resembles periclase (180), which is usually isotropic with birefringent inclusions.
records.Extended description: Crushed fragments of vesuvianite are rough and equant (001100). They are translucent with blue edges. Large pieces show cleavage traces. This mineral has a specific gravity of 3.4 and a hardness of 6.5. The refractive indices of tetragonal vesuvianite are 1.698-1. 736 (1:) and 1. 702-1.742 (omega); (-) 0.001-0.012. The interference colors are mottled grays, whites and occasional yellows with incomplete undulose extinction for the larger fragments. Smaller, individual crystals show complete extinction. Vesuvianite strongly resembles periclase (180), which is usually isotropic with birefringent inclusions. The dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® are blue or light blue with an annular stop, golden magenta with a central stop.

These transparent, colorless particles of hydrous basic aluminum phosphate occur as prismatic fragments either equant (001000) in a radiated fibrous structure or as rectangular fragments (001001, 001011) showing good cleavage. Orthorhombic wavellite has refractive indices of 1.525 (alpha), 1.534 (beta), 1.552 (gamma); (+) 0.027; 2V is 72°. c = gamma, parallel to elongation. The hardness is 3.5-4; the specific gravity is 2.31-2.36. Some of the particles in this sample are covered with hematite (390, 391).

records.microscopy description: Willemite is a hexagonal mineral which can be crushed into colorless, transparent, equant, angular chips.
records.Extended description: Willemite is a hexagonal mineral which can be crushed into colorless, transparent, equant, angular chips. The edges are rough and the faces are uneven due to conchoidal fracture and gaseous inclusions; no cleavage is evident. The indices are l. 719 (e) andl.691 (omega); (+) 0.028. The specific gravity is 4, the hardness 5.5. Dispersion staining colors in Aroclor® are faint blue with an annular stop and golden white with a central stop.

records.microscopy description: Zincite fragments are yellow to orange to deep red, translucent, equant, angular chips. The particles are not noticeably pleochroic, but interference colors are abnormal mostly greens and reds.
records.Extended description: Zincite fragments are yellow to orange to deep red, translucent, equant, angular chips. The faces bear the marks of conchoidal fracture combined with triangular and trapezoidal gaseous occlusions. The particles are not noticeably pleochroic, but interference colors are abnormal mostly greens and reds. The indices of hexagonal zincite are 2.029 (e) and 2.013 (omega); (+) 0.016. Associated with the sample are willemite (210) and franklinite (100000). The specific gravity is 5.4, the hardness 4.5.

records.microscopy description: The zircon in this sample is a beach sand, as indicated by the rounding of the particles. These grains, when coated with resins, may be used for casting metals -see molding sand, zircon (416).
records.Extended description: The zircon in this sample is a beach sand, as indicated by the rounding of the particles. These grains, when coated with resins, may be used for casting metals -see molding sand, zircon (416). These tetragonal crystals have refractive indices of 1.96-2.02 (epsilon) and 1.91-1.96 (omega); (+) 0.07. The hardness is 7.5; the specific gravity is 4. 7 (4.2-4.86). Fracture is conchoidal. This sample also contains a few rounded grains of quartz (183) and hematite (391).

records.microscopy description: abrasive dust | Transparent, colorless to pale blue chips and equant fragments of sharp-edged, birefringent silicon carbide (Carborundum®, 215) with indices over 2.6 (001100, 011100). These particles make up about 50% of the sample. Transparent, colorless, sharp-edged, irregular fragments of corundum (128, 218-220). Transparent to translucent, orange particles of isotropic resin. They are equant or appear as Hakes; the edges are sharp or rounded, or completely lack a regular outline (010000, 010010).
records.Extended description: This sample, evidently intended for bonding into a grinding wheel, has four distinct components: 1. Transparent, colorless to pale blue chips and equant fragments of sharp-edged, birefringent silicon carbide (Carborundum®, 215) with indices over 2.6 (001100, 011100). These particles make up about 50% of the sample. 2. Transparent, colorless, sharp-edged, irregular fragments of corundum (128, 218-220). They have low birefringence with indices of about 1.76 (001100). These fragments constitute 25-30% of the sample. 3. Black, opaque, rounded particles of magnetite (165) (100000). They account for about 15% of the sample. 4. Transparent to translucent, orange particles of isotropic resin. They are equant or appear as Hakes; the edges are sharp or rounded, or completely lack a regular outline (010000, 010010). The refractive indices are below 1.66. These particles comprise about 5% of the sample.

records.microscopy description: The transparent to translucent, very pale yellow to orange-brown, earthy looking particles are rounded to polygonal agglomerates <1-30 µm. The particles are weakly birefringent to isotropic with a refractive index greater than 1.66.
records.Extended description: Bamesite® (Kerr-McGee Chemical Corporation) is a lens polishing compound consisting of rare earth oxides, in which the rare earths are present in their natural ratio of abundance. The transparent to translucent, very pale yellow to orange-brown, earthy looking particles are rounded to polygonal agglomerates <1-30 µm. These agglomerates are, in tum, composed of small (< 1µm) crystallites. The particles are weakly birefringent to isotropic with a refractive index greater than 1.66. The specific gravity is 6.1.

records.microscopy description: These irregular, sharp-edged chips and equant fragments of silicon carbide (011100) are blue and green, but they may also be gray or black (001100). Very small particles are almost colorless, and many particles of all sizes appear opaque due to high internal reflection and refraction caused by the very high refractive index. In top light, they may show iridescence due to a surface film of silica.
records.Extended description: These irregular, sharp-edged chips and equant fragments of silicon carbide (011100) are blue and green, but they may also be gray or black (001100). Very small particles are almost colorless, and many particles of all sizes appear opaque due to high internal reflection and refraction caused by the very high refractive index. The faces of this most widely used artificial abrasive are smooth or striated. In top light, they may show iridescence due to a surface film of silica. The refractive indices are 2.648 (omega) to 2.691 (epsilon); (+) 0.043.

records.microscopy description: Blue to green, sharp-edged, birefringent, equant fragments of high index (about 2.6). These are amorphous, compact masses of isotropic material (000000). Their surfaces show rounded irregularities characteristic of vitreous substances. Internal optical discontinuities, due to composition variations such as fine cracks, make the particles cloudy by reflected light and gray by transmitted light.
records.Extended description: This sample, from a grinding operation on unglazed porcelain, has two major components: 1. Blue to green, sharp-edged, birefringent, equant fragments of high index (about 2.6). These are Carborundum® (215) (011100). 2. Unglazed porcelain fragments. These are amorphous, compact masses of isotropic material (000000). Their surfaces show rounded irregularities characteristic of vitreous substances. Internal optical discontinuities, due to composition variations such as fine cracks, make the particles cloudy by reflected light and gray by transmitted light. The photomicrograph was taken without top lighting. The translucent clumps contain birefringent quartz (183) (001000); feldspars (113,157,169,176) (001000) may also be present. The index of the porcelain is about 1.55.

records.microscopy description: It is an electric furnace product which can be cast in sand molds to form these products. The acute, angular, equant particles of corundum are most evident with dendritic crystal inclusions of, perhaps, rutile and opaque, magnetic iron.
records.Extended description: The Carhart Company makes an abrasion resistant material (Corguard®) for pipe, bins, conveyor skirts, chutes etc. It is an electric furnace product which can be cast in sand molds to form these products. To be abrasion resistant, the material must be itself very hard, hence we find this dust from the cast material to be mainly corundum, q.v., but with other refractory substances like zircon (212) and hornblende (152). The optical properties of these substances are described under each title. The acute, angular, equant particles of corundum are most evident with dendritic crystal inclusions of, perhaps, rutile and opaque, magnetic iron. The Moh hardness of this material is 9.

records.microscopy description: Irregular to slightly rounded fragments appear here (011100, 001100); most have rounded, opaque occlusions (100000). The particles are colorless or blue, some tinged with green and brown; the colored ones show pleochroism when they are properly oriented (birefringent views).
records.Extended description: Irregular to slightly rounded fragments appear here (011100, 001100); most have rounded, opaque occlusions (100000). Emery is an intimate mixture of transparent, granular corundum (128, 218-220) , magnetite (165) and often hematite (390) or limonite (162). Small quantities of other minerals, such as diaspore, gibbsite and sillimanite, may be present. The particles are colorless or blue, some tinged with green and brown; the colored ones show pleochroism when they are properly oriented (birefringent views). The rounded, opaque occlusions are magnetite (165). A magnet moved around the objective will draw the opaque magnetite and magnetite-containing particles around with it. The indices are 1.7676-1.7682 (omega) to 1.7594-1.7598 (epsilon) for corundum, and the birefringence is low, about (- ) 0.008. The blue color shows up best in ordinary or plane polarized transmitted light. It is washed out by the prominent interference colors observed between slightly uncrossed or crossed polars. Top lighting enhances the red and brown patches of iron oxide on some of the particles.

records.microscopy description: Irregular to slightly rounded fragments appear here (011100, 001100); most have rounded, opaque occlusions (100000). The particles are colorless or blue, some tinged with green and brown; the colored ones show pleochroism when they are properly oriented (birefringent views).
