records.microscopy description: The opaque particles are magnetic; in this sample, they average 40 µm across (10-390 µm). Corundum particles often show a single Hat face.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless to light yellow and dark brown, equant, sharp fragments of artificial a-Al2O3 (011100, 001100) contain some opaque iron compounds (100000), both free and occluded. This is suggestive of natural corundum, variety emery (137, 218), but the intimate association does not occur here to the same extent. Also, the artificial product lacks the wide color range often found in the natural abrasive. The opaque particles are magnetic; in this sample, they average 40 µm across (10-390 µm). Corundum particles often show a single Hat face. It is uniaxial negative; the indices range from 1. 7686 (omega) to 1.7604 (epsilon), with low birefringence, (-) 0.0082.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless to brown, jagged, equant fragments of corundum (128, 218-220) (001100, 011100) make up about 95% of this sample; opaque, magnetic particles, both free and included (100000) , constitute the other 5%. The particles in this sample, averaging 50 µm across (10-250 µm), are colorless to reddish in reflected light.
records.Extended description: Transparent, colorless to brown, jagged, equant fragments of corundum (128, 218-220) (001100, 011100) make up about 95% of this sample; opaque, magnetic particles, both free and included (100000) , constitute the other 5%. The particles in this sample, averaging 50 µm across (10-250 µm), are colorless to reddish in reflected light. They are uniaxial negative, with indices ranging from 1.7686 (omega) to 1.7604 (epsilon); (-) 0.0082.

records.microscopy description: Colorless, transparent, sharp crystal fragments of corundum (128, 218-220). These average 20 µm across (10-50 µm); The rubber particles themselves are colorless and transparent, with a refractive index of about 1.54. They are very small (<l µm) and appear to be opaque except at high magnification. The true nature of the agglomerate can be seen on thin particles at high magnification.
records.Extended description: This sample consists of two major components: 1. Colorless, transparent, sharp crystal fragments of corundum (128, 218-220). They have low birefringence, with indices around 1.76 (001100). 2. Translucent, brick-red, loose, spongy clumps of rubber. These average 20 µm across (10-50 µm); they are made up of granules in which individual pigment particles, less than 1 ,-im in diameter, have been dispersed. The rubber particles themselves are colorless and transparent, with a refractive index of about 1.54. The pigment particles, iron oxide (223, 391), are also transparent but deep red and with very high refractive indices (2. 7 4-2.95). They are very small (<l µm) and appear to be opaque except at high magnification. Particles of rubber-pigment are opaque by transmitted light at low magnification but red by reflected light. The true nature of the agglomerate can be seen on thin particles at high magnification.

records.microscopy description: Transparent crystal fragments with a refractive index of 2.419, sharp, jagged edges, conchoidal fracture and smooth, perfect octahedral cleavage are diamond particles. Small particles are almost always colorless, even in varieties which, in larger particles, show pale shades of yellow, red, orange, green, blue or brown; they are rarely deeply colored except for the black and opaque carbonado diamond. Many of the faces are rounded and/or striated; occasionally triangular depressions mark the surfaces. Diamond is isotropic but often shows abnormal birefringence which may be visible in particles larger than about 10 ,-im.
records.Extended description: Transparent crystal fragments with a refractive index of 2.419, sharp, jagged edges, conchoidal fracture and smooth, perfect octahedral cleavage are diamond particles. Small particles are almost always colorless, even in varieties which, in larger particles, show pale shades of yellow, red, orange, green, blue or brown; they are rarely deeply colored except for the black and opaque carbonado diamond. Many of the faces are rounded and/or striated; occasionally triangular depressions mark the surfaces. Inclusions and flaws are common. Diamond is isotropic but often shows abnormal birefringence which may be visible in particles larger than about 10 ,-im. Diamond looks almost exactly like -fl,uorite (142), but the refractive index readily distinguishes between them; the index for fluorite is only 1.433.

records.microscopy description: Most of the particles are less than 1 µm across, and agglomerates are common although occasionally single fragments up to 10 µm in diameter are found. If the particles had come from the cake form of the polish, bits of clay would also be present.
records.Extended description: Jewelers' rouge is made up of transparent, deep red, rounded to sharp-edged grains of iron oxide (391 ). Most of the particles are less than 1 µm across, and agglomerates are common although occasionally single fragments up to 10 µm in diameter are found. The indices are 2. 95 (omega) to 2.74 (epsilon); (-) 0.21 (Li). The hardness is 5, and the density is 5.2. The compound is used as a polishing agent for glass and some metals. If the particles had come from the cake form of the polish, bits of clay would also be present.

records.microscopy description: matchbox striker dust | The birefringent particles average 20 µm across (1-220 µm); This dust is from the manufacture of striker surfaces for kitchen matches. Also present are small, transparent, yellow, isotropic, rounded, amorphous bits of glue with a refractive index around 1.53 (010000).
records.Extended description: Most evident here are transparent, colorless, irregular, sharp fragments and bits of quartz (183) (001000). The birefringent particles average 20 µm across (1-220 µm); indices are 1.544 (omega) to 1.553 (epsilon). This dust is from the manufacture of striker surfaces for kitchen matches. Also present are small, transparent, yellow, isotropic, rounded, amorphous bits of glue with a refractive index around 1.53 (010000).

records.microscopy description: grinding dust | Transparent, blue and green, sharp-edged, equant particles of Carborundum® (215) showing high refractive indices, 2.648 (omega) to 2.691 (epsilon); These particles comprise about 15% of the sample. Most look opaque due to the very high indices. Transparent, colorless, equant particles of corundum (128, 218-220) with opaque inclusions. Transparent to translucent, isotropic, orange to red-brown, amorphous masses of resinous binder (about 20% of the sample). The resin may appear anisotropic due to the associated corundum.
records.Extended description: Three major components make up this sample: 1. Transparent, blue and green, sharp-edged, equant particles of Carborundum® (215) showing high refractive indices, 2.648 (omega) to 2.691 (epsilon); (+) 0.043 (011100). These particles comprise about 15% of the sample. Most look opaque due to the very high indices. 2. Transparent, colorless, equant particles of corundum (128, 218-220) with opaque inclusions. The birefringence is low, (-) 0.0082; the indices are 1. 7686 (omega) to 1. 7604 (epsilon)(001100). About 65% of the sample is accounted for here. 3. Transparent to translucent, isotropic, orange to red-brown, amorphous masses of resinous binder (about 20% of the sample). The resin may appear anisotropic due to the associated corundum. The indices are below 1.66 (010000).

records.microscopy description: These irregular, transparent, colorless, sharp-edged, isotropic fragments of foamy volcanic glass have been perforated and channeled by trapped and escaping gases. Very small pieces may lack perforations so that they resemble ground glass, but even these show some "fire-polished" surfaces (000000). There are two kinds of markings: parallel grooves due to elongated gas bubbles (226A) and nearly spherical cavities due to round bubbles (226B).
records.Extended description: These irregular, transparent, colorless, sharp-edged, isotropic fragments of foamy volcanic glass have been perforated and channeled by trapped and escaping gases. Very small pieces may lack perforations so that they resemble ground glass, but even these show some "fire-polished" surfaces (000000). The index is about 1.45. There are two kinds of markings: parallel grooves due to elongated gas bubbles (226A) and nearly spherical cavities due to round bubbles (226B).

records.microscopy description: roto-blast steel shot dust | These are more or less rounded bits of partly fused steel dust from a Roto-blast. The black, opaque particles average 65 µm across (1-190 µm) and are strongly magnetic.
records.Extended description: These are more or less rounded bits of partly fused steel dust from a Roto-blast. The black, opaque particles average 65 µm across (1-190 µm) and are strongly magnetic. Steel shot is gray to black and highly reflective under top light.

records.microscopy description: and 15% transparent to translucent, isotropic, brownish organic debris (010000). Aggregates to 50 µm are common.
records.Extended description: This is an abrasive polish consisting of dustlike, friable, siliceous material that is the residue of siliceous limestone from which the carbonates have been removed by natural water action. This sample consists of about 70% silicasee quartz (183) (001000)-many in the form of minute flakes (001010); 10% clay; 5% iron oxides-see limonite (162) (010100) and hematite (391) (011100); and 15% transparent to translucent, isotropic, brownish organic debris (010000). The particles are < 1-3 µm, except for some of the quartz which goes to 15 µm. Aggregates to 50 µm are common. Cf. tripoli powder (230).

records.microscopy description: The particle size here is 1-150 µm.
records.Extended description: This sample was collected as an abrasive used to clean masonry. It consists entirely of comminuted quartz. The chemical and optical characteristics are identical to those described under quartz (183), q. v. The particle size here is 1-150 µm.

records.microscopy description: The mineral form is tripolite, which includes infusorial earth (6) resembling a brownish chalk or clay. The ultimate clay particles are beyond the resolution of the light microscope, but larger particles are transparent to translucent, colorless to light brown, porous, rough aggregates consisting chiefly of fine-grained silica. Individual particles are apparently rounded equant. Interference colors are low-order grays, even for 10 µm particles.
records.Extended description: Tripoli is an earth consisting of very friable, dustlike silica not of diatomaceous origin [although friable schistose deposits of silica including diatomite (4) and kieselguhr are also called tripoli]. The mineral form is tripolite, which includes infusorial earth (6) resembling a brownish chalk or clay. Its hardness is sufficient to scratch glass. The ultimate clay particles are beyond the resolution of the light microscope, but larger particles are transparent to translucent, colorless to light brown, porous, rough aggregates consisting chiefly of fine-grained silica. Individual particles are apparently rounded equant. Interference colors are low-order grays, even for 10 µm particles. Refractive indices are around 1.54.

records.microscopy description: electrostatic precipitator dust | This electrostatic precipitator dust from a cat-cracker consists of 20 µm (5-40 µm) particles of semisynthetic catalyst [cf.fresh semisynthetic catalyst (237) ]. Many of the transparent, colorless and isotropic (000000) to gray-brown (010000) to opaque (100000) particles still show the birefringent occlusions (001000) of the fresh material (237).
records.Extended description: This electrostatic precipitator dust from a cat-cracker consists of 20 µm (5-40 µm) particles of semisynthetic catalyst [cf.fresh semisynthetic catalyst (237) ]. These are not as spent as those shown in spent semisynthetic catalyst (238). Many of the transparent, colorless and isotropic (000000) to gray-brown (010000) to opaque (100000) particles still show the birefringent occlusions (001000) of the fresh material (237).

Many of the transparent, colorless and isotropic (000000) to gray-brown (010000) to opaque (100000) particles still show the birefringent occlusions (001000) of the fresh material (237).

Many of the transparent, colorless and isotropic (000000) to gray-brown (010000) to opaque (100000) particles still show the birefringent occlusions (001000) of the fresh material (237).

records.microscopy description: high-alumina catalyst, fresh. The colorless, isotropic particles closely resemble those in 241 and 243 although these are smoother and more transparent. No smaller, isotropic particles are dispersed in these "potatoes," although a few angular, moderately birefringent (less than 0.01) crystals are present some occluded, some free. The particles are harder than the zeolite catalyst particles but can be crushed by pressure on the cover slip.
records.Extended description: This is one of the commonest cracking catalysts. The colorless, isotropic particles closely resemble those in 241 and 243 although these are smoother and more transparent. Their refractive index is about 1.54. No smaller, isotropic particles are dispersed in these "potatoes," although a few angular, moderately birefringent (less than 0.01) crystals are present some occluded, some free. Their indices are about 1.60. The particles are harder than the zeolite catalyst particles but can be crushed by pressure on the cover slip. They fracture conchoidally.

records.microscopy description: high-alumina catalyst, spent. Particles of spent high-alumina catalyst are opaque (100000). In this sample, one finds some fresh catalyst (colorless and transparent) (000000) , some spent (opaque)(100000) and some in 'intermediate stages (brown or gray) (010000). The particles are potato-shaped to subspherical with smooth surfaces. Some show internal markings, but there are few occluded particles.
records.Extended description: Particles of spent high-alumina catalyst are opaque (100000). In this sample, one finds some fresh catalyst (colorless and transparent) (000000) , some spent (opaque)(100000) and some in 'intermediate stages (brown or gray) (010000). The particles are potato-shaped to subspherical with smooth surfaces. Some show internal markings, but there are few occluded particles. The refractive indices are all less than 1.54, the index of the corresponding fresh catalyst.

records.microscopy description: low-alumina catalyst, fresh. Particles of fresh low-alumina catalyst are difficult to distinguish from zeolite catalyst (241, 243). They are colorless and isotropic, but more transparent than zeolite, with a slightly lower average refractive index of about 1.525 (000000). The particles tend to be snowball shapes with irregular, porous surfaces (like an orange skin). Dispersed throughout, though not as thickly as in zeolite, are transparent, almost spherical, isotropic occlusions (000000).
records.Extended description: Particles of fresh low-alumina catalyst are difficult to distinguish from zeolite catalyst (241, 243). They are colorless and isotropic, but more transparent than zeolite, with a slightly lower average refractive index of about 1.525 (000000). The particles tend to be snowball shapes with irregular, porous surfaces (like an orange skin). Dispersed throughout, though not as thickly as in zeolite, are transparent, almost spherical, isotropic occlusions (000000). The refractive index of these subspheres is about 1.56.

records.microscopy description: low-alumina catalyst, spent. Most are opaque (100000). Particles less spent have a lower refractive index but stronger absorption than the fresh catalyst. Tumbling the particles in a fluidized bed rounds off rough edges admirably. The colors range from colorless (000000) to light brown (010000) , dark brown and black (100000).
records.Extended description: The morphological characteristics of spent low-alumina catalyst are similar to those of spent zeolite catalyst (242, 244). Most are opaque (100000). Particles less spent have a lower refractive index but stronger absorption than the fresh catalyst. Another general characteristic shown by all used catalysts, and one that shows up particularly well here, is increased smoothness. Tumbling the particles in a fluidized bed rounds off rough edges admirably. The colors range from colorless (000000) to light brown (010000) , dark brown and black (100000).

records.microscopy description: raw natural catalyst. Most of the particles are very irregular-from angular to subspherical. The shapes of the raw materials are still apparent, and there are many birefringent rods (001001) showing first-order interference colors, positive elongation and refractive indices from about 1.54 (lengthwise) to about 1.62 (crosswise).
records.Extended description: This granulated zeolite catalyst differs from samples 241-244 in having been sintered at a low temperature. Most of the particles are very irregular-from angular to subspherical. The shapes of the raw materials are still apparent, and there are many birefringent rods (001001) showing first-order interference colors, positive elongation and refractive indices from about 1.54 (lengthwise) to about 1.62 (crosswise). These crystals and another glassy phase are clumped into aggregates. The refractive index of the glass is about 1.530.

records.microscopy description: semisynthetic catalyst, fresh. Particles of fresh semisynthetic catalyst (000000, 010000) are transparent, light brown (> 5 µm thick) and isotropic, with an average refractive index of about 1.525. The particles tend to be very irregular, porous "snowballs." Dispersed throughout are transparent, colorless occlusions (001000). The rounded, isotropic occlusions have an index below 1.525; the angular occlusions have low birefringence and indices greater than 1.525. The presence of birefringent material distinguishes this catalyst from zeolite catalyst (241,243).
records.Extended description: Particles of fresh semisynthetic catalyst (000000, 010000) are transparent, light brown (> 5 µm thick) and isotropic, with an average refractive index of about 1.525. The particles tend to be very irregular, porous "snowballs." Dispersed throughout are transparent, colorless occlusions (001000). The rounded, isotropic occlusions have an index below 1.525; the angular occlusions have low birefringence and indices greater than 1.525. The presence of birefringent material distinguishes this catalyst from zeolite catalyst (241,243).

records.microscopy description: semisynthetic catalyst, spent. Particles of spent semisynthetic catalyst are transparent, colorless and isotropic (000000) to opaque (100000). The more strongly absorbing particles have the lower indices. The nearly spherical particles are very smooth as a consequence of their use in a fluidized bed.
records.Extended description: Particles of spent semisynthetic catalyst are transparent, colorless and isotropic (000000) to opaque (100000). Some intermediate types are gray-brown (010000). The refractive indices are slightly lower than 1.526, the index of the corresponding fresh catalyst. The more strongly absorbing particles have the lower indices. The nearly spherical particles are very smooth as a consequence of their use in a fluidized bed.

records.microscopy description: synthetic catalyst, fresh. These are transparent, colorless and isotropic chips. Their smooth, angular surfaces show conchoidal fracture (000000). The particle slowly soaks up the liquid, causing the apparent refractive index to change. A rounded outline of the low-index "dry" portion slowly contracts and, in a few minutes, disappears. The index of the final "wetted" particle is only slightly less than 1.50.
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless and isotropic chips. Their smooth, angular surfaces show conchoidal fracture (000000). The refractive index varies from about 1.51 to about 1.54. Some of the low-index chips show a most unusual behavior when mounted in Cargille index liquids near 1.50. The particle slowly soaks up the liquid, causing the apparent refractive index to change. A rounded outline of the low-index "dry" portion slowly contracts and, in a few minutes, disappears. The index of the final "wetted" particle is only slightly less than 1.50.

records.microscopy description: synthetic catalyst, spent. Collected from the kiln stack of a cat-cracker, these isotropic chips are transparent to opaque, and colorless (000000) to amber (010000) to black (100000) by transmitted light. Their smooth, angular surfaces show conchoidal fracture. The refractive indices vary between 1.50 and, for the more strongly absorbing particles, about 1.55.
records.Extended description: Collected from the kiln stack of a cat-cracker, these isotropic chips are transparent to opaque, and colorless (000000) to amber (010000) to black (100000) by transmitted light. Their smooth, angular surfaces show conchoidal fracture. The refractive indices vary between 1.50 and, for the more strongly absorbing particles, about 1.55.

records.microscopy description: zeolite catalyst, fresh. These are nearly colorless, isotropic, potato-shaped particles with a refractive index of ~ 1.53. Very small, rounded, isotropic particles are dispersed throughout the "potatoes"; The "potatoes" average 60 µm in diameter, the "warts" 2-3 µm. The large particles crumble easily when the cover slip is pressed, and show conchoidal fracture.
records.Extended description: These are nearly colorless, isotropic, potato-shaped particles with a refractive index of ~ 1.53. They show a slight brownish tint due to light scatter by fine internal pores. Very small, rounded, isotropic particles are dispersed throughout the "potatoes"; some protrude in "warts." These have a lower refractive index (about 1.45). The "potatoes" average 60 µm in diameter, the "warts" 2-3 µm. The large particles crumble easily when the cover slip is pressed, and show conchoidal fracture.

records.microscopy description: zeolite catalyst, spent. The spent particles have become completely opaque due to the presence of carbon and other resinous decomposition products (100000). Many of these are not totally spent, however, and appear to be somewhere between fresh, colorless transparency and spent opacity (000000, 010000). Curiously enough, the refractive indices of all of the particles in this sample are considerably lower than that of the fresh catalyst, 1.53. The "warts" apparent in 241 have been worn off in the fluidized bed, where the particles have abraded each other into very smooth, nearly spherical shapes.
records.Extended description: Originally, this catalyst was identical with the fresh zeolite catalyst (241). The spent particles have become completely opaque due to the presence of carbon and other resinous decomposition products (100000). Many of these are not totally spent, however, and appear to be somewhere between fresh, colorless transparency and spent opacity (000000, 010000). Curiously enough, the refractive indices of all of the particles in this sample are considerably lower than that of the fresh catalyst, 1.53. The "warts" apparent in 241 have been worn off in the fluidized bed, where the particles have abraded each other into very smooth, nearly spherical shapes.

records.microscopy description: zeolite catalyst, fresh. Besides the isotropic "warts," however, other, somewhat larger (5-10 µm) particles are occluded, which have a higher index than the matrix;
records.Extended description: This catalyst is very similar to that shown in 241 (000000). Besides the isotropic "warts," however, other, somewhat larger (5-10 µm) particles are occluded, which have a higher index than the matrix; these show moderate birefringence (less than 0.01) and are often square or rectangular (001000).

records.microscopy description: zeolite catalyst, spent. These are used catalyst particles, originally the same as those in sample 243. Now they are more nearly spherical, and completely spent particles are black (100000). Like samples in 241-243, these particles crumble readily when the cover slip is pressed with a needle.
records.Extended description: These are used catalyst particles, originally the same as those in sample 243. Now they are more nearly spherical, and completely spent particles are black (100000). Some, showing intermediate degrees of use, are gray-brown (010000) and have refractive indices lower than 1.54, the index of the fresh catalyst. Like samples in 241-243, these particles crumble readily when the cover slip is pressed with a needle.

records.microscopy description: The cement here, however, is a transparent, colorless, isotropic, amorphous, organic binder (000000).
records.Extended description: This sample consists of two major components: 1. Asbestos: individual fibers and bundles of chrysotile asbestos (122), q.v. (001001). 2. Binder: a true mortar would consist of a mixture of cement of lime and sand. The cement here, however, is a transparent, colorless, isotropic, amorphous, organic binder (000000). There are also small amounts of limestone (133, 161), iron or steel and hematite (223, 390).

This synthetic silicate, one of the principal components of portland cement, is monoclinic, forming colorless, rounded angular, equant crystals. The refractive indices are 1.707 (alpha), 1.715 (beta), 1.730 (gamma); (+) 0.023. The specific gravity is 3.27. The birefringence for C2S is greater (by a factor of about 7) than that for C3S (249) and the indices are slightly lower. Thus C3S crystals show slightly greater contrast in Aroclor® than crystals of C2S.

records.microscopy description: This is the only important colored compound found in portland cement. It is orthorhombic, forming yellow to orange to brown crystals, depending on the size. Most are equant with moderate birefringence.
records.Extended description: This is the only important colored compound found in portland cement. It is orthorhombic, forming yellow to orange to brown crystals, depending on the size. Most are equant with moderate birefringence. The specific gravity is 3.73, much higher than the specific gravities of other components of cement, which are all about 3. The refractive indices (Li) are 1.96 (alpha), 2.01 (beta), 2.04 (gamma); (-) 0.08.

records.microscopy description: This specially synthesized sample is cubic, forming aggregates of rounded, equant, 5-10 µm crystals. Each particle shows many occluded gas bubbles, and some aggregates show very low strain birefringence;
records.Extended description: C3A is another principal compound in portland cement. This specially synthesized sample is cubic, forming aggregates of rounded, equant, 5-10 µm crystals. Each particle shows many occluded gas bubbles, and some aggregates show very low strain birefringence; fracture is conchoidal. The specific gravity is 3.04, and the refractive index is 1.701.

records.microscopy description: Between completely crossed polars, the crystals appear very slightly birefringent, showing light gray interference colors.
records.Extended description: A principal component of portland cement, this synthetic silicate is triclinic, forming colorless, rounded-angular, equant grains. The refractive indices range from 1.7139 (alpha) to 1.7172 (gamma); (+) 0.0033. The specific gravity is about 3.13. Between completely crossed polars, the crystals appear very slightly birefringent, showing light gray interference colors.

records.microscopy description: individual grains are held together by a fine-grained eutectic (251).
records.Extended description: Type I cement, illustrated by this standard PCA sample, is the most commonly used cement type. It is about 25% C2S (246) (001100), 50% C3S (249) (001100), 10% C3A (248) (000100) and 10% C4AF (247) (011100). A few extraneous substances, such as gypsum (151), quartz (183), limestone (161 ) and other silicates and aluminates, usually are also present. Individual crystals of each component can be seen although the yellow C4AF tends to grow on the surfaces of the other components as a fine-grained dendrite, probably because of its lower melting point. The large aggregate in the upper left center of the figure is typical; individual grains are held together by a fine-grained eutectic (251).

records.microscopy description: cement, type ii
records.Extended description: Type II cement differs from Type I only in the relative proportions of its major components: about 33% C2S (246) (001100) , 42% C3S (249) (001100), 5% C3A (248) (000100) and 13% C4AF (247) (011100). C4AF crystallizes as fine-grained needles between and on grains of the other components. This sample is a PCA standard. The aggregates shown are typical of a well-fired cement. Unfortunately, finished cement is usually ground so fine that these aggregates are destroyed (see especially 253).

records.microscopy description: cement, type iii
records.Extended description: A high-strength cement, Type III differs from the other types only in the relative percentages of its principal components and in its particle size. It is supplied as finer crystals than the other types although the difference is not significant from a morphological viewpoint. This PCA standard consists of approximately 13% C2S (246) (001100), 60% C3S (249) (001100), 9% C3A (248) (000100) and 8% C4AF (247) (011100). As usual, fine yellow needles of C4AF coat the other components.

records.microscopy description: cement, type iv
records.Extended description: Type IV cement sets at relatively low temperatures because it is only about 26% C3S (249) (001100). The average percentages of the other components are 50% C2S (246) (001100), 5% C3A (248) (000100) and 12% C4AF (247) (011100). The additional C4AF is particularly evident and seems to "cement" individual, equant, colorless grains into aggregates resembling bunches of grapes. Fine-grained, yellow needles of C4AF also are evident on and between the other grains, as if it had crystallized last as a low-melting eutectic.

records.microscopy description: cement, type v
records.Extended description: Type V cement is intended for use with water having a high sulfate content. It is made up of approximately 40% each of C2S (246) (001100) and C3S (249) (001100) 4% C3A (248) (000100) and 9% C4AF (247) (011100). Individual grains of C2S, C3S and C3A are sometimes partly coated, or even cemented together, with yellow needles of C4AF.
A commercial dry-process cement taken from the final product line, this differs little from the standard types above and appears to be a Type I cement (250).
This is a commercial Type I cement dust (250). C3S (249) and C2S (246) particles are larger here and, though rounded, much better formed than in the PCA standards (250-254).

records.microscopy description: Most of the effluent is colorless to yellow or reddish, glassy spheres with indices around 1.60.
records.Extended description: Among these particles from the dust collector on a rotary kiln making portland cement, little crystalline C3S (246). C2S (249), C3A (248) or C4AF (247) can be found. Most of the effluent is colorless to yellow or reddish, glassy spheres with indices around 1.60.

Besides particles of C2S (246), C3S (249) and C3A (248) in this sample from the kiln stack of a dry-process cement plant, many limestone particles (001010, 001000) and other raw material components (001000) are present.

records.microscopy description: This sample is predominantly portland cement and small, highly birefringent particles of limestone (001010, 001000).
records.Extended description: Mortar mix is made up of a Type III portland cement high in C3S (249) content (001100, 000100, 011100) and considerable amounts of a so-called plasticizer such as limestone, hydrated lime or diatomaceous earth (4-7). This sample is predominantly portland cement and small, highly birefringent particles of limestone (001010, 001000).

records.microscopy description: These are colorless, birefringent, somewhat tabular, monoclinic prisms soluble in water and glycerin, very slightly soluble in alcohol and insoluble in acid. Cleavage is distinct and ground crystals are conchoidally fractured, equant fragments. This sample shows the crystals rounded as a result of partial solution in water.
records.Extended description: These are colorless, birefringent, somewhat tabular, monoclinic prisms soluble in water and glycerin, very slightly soluble in alcohol and insoluble in acid. Cleavage is distinct and ground crystals are conchoidally fractured, equant fragments. The soft crystals (Moh 2.0-2.5) effloresce in dry air and have a specific gravity of about 1.70. Heat releases water of crystallization-two molecules at 72°C and the remaining eight molecules at 123°C. The refractive indices of borax are 1.4467 (alpha), 1.4694 (beta), 1.4724 (gamma); (-) 0.0257. This sample shows the crystals rounded as a result of partial solution in water.

records.microscopy description: cleaner dust | This sample illustrates very well the necessity for polarized light microscopy for particle identification.
records.Extended description: This cleaner dust is made up of isotropic particles of pumice (226) (000010), low birefringent crushed quartz (183) (001000), high birefringent anhydrous sodium carbonate (339) (001010) and polycrystalline surfactant (270) (001000). This sample illustrates very well the necessity for polarized light microscopy for particle identification.
This kitchen cleanser is made up of conchoidal particles of quartz (183) (001000), chlorinated trisodium phosphate (271) (001001) and surfactant (270) (001000).

records.microscopy description: laundry detergent dust | These spray-dried particles representative of such products as "Bold," "Tide," "Surf" etc. are bubbly aggregates sometimes broken into small flakes with traces of bubble walls. Each particle consists of small, low birefringent crystals (001000) in an isotropic matrix; larger particles contain air bubbles. This is evidence of a "bluing" constituent and confirms the detergent source for the particle aggregate. They are transparent, colorless and birefringent with refractive indices of 1.439 (alpha), 1.473 (beta) and 1.484 (gamma);
records.Extended description: These spray-dried particles representative of such products as "Bold," "Tide," "Surf" etc. are bubbly aggregates sometimes broken into small flakes with traces of bubble walls. Each particle consists of small, low birefringent crystals (001000) in an isotropic matrix; larger particles contain air bubbles. Some of the aggregates show a deep blue coloration. This is evidence of a "bluing" constituent and confirms the detergent source for the particle aggregate. Occasionally, square tablets will be seen. These are crystals of sodium perborate (001010). They are transparent, colorless and birefringent with refractive indices of 1.439 (alpha), 1.473 (beta) and 1.484 (gamma); (-) 0.045. Sodium perborate has a melting point of 130°C and a specific gravity of 1.90.

records.microscopy description: The particles of this spray-dried product are mostly transparent, colorless, isotropic, angular grains (000000), with some irregular, birefringent flakes (001010). The particle size range is <1-25 µm.
records.Extended description: Nacconol® (Allied Chemical Corporation, National Aniline Division) is a line of technical grade biodegradable, linear alkyl sulfonate detergents used in industrial and household cleaners, in textile scouring agents, and as a detergent intermediate. The particles of this spray-dried product are mostly transparent, colorless, isotropic, angular grains (000000), with some irregular, birefringent flakes (001010). The particle size range is <1-25 µm.

records.microscopy description: The latter are translucent, colorless agglomerates of microcrystals.
records.Extended description: This scouring powder is made up of particles of crushed quartz (183) (001000), surfactant (270) (001000) and anhydrous trisodium phosphate (001000). The latter are translucent, colorless agglomerates of microcrystals. They are monoclinic with a specific gravity of 2.54 and refractive indices with blue light (476 nm) of 1.455 (alpha), 1.504 (beta) and 1.505 (gamma); (-) 0.50.

records.microscopy description: soap dust | Particles of soap dust are transparent, colorless, equant and have rounded edges. Soap dust is weakly birefringent having refractive indices around 1.50. These soap dust particles behave like parallel aggregates of fibrous crystallites.
records.Extended description: Particles of soap dust are transparent, colorless, equant and have rounded edges. Soap dust is weakly birefringent having refractive indices around 1.50. These soap dust particles behave like parallel aggregates of fibrous crystallites. They show low birefringence and undulose extinction especially when squeezed into thin layers by pressure on the cover slip. They soften but do not darken on heating to 150°C. The refractive indices are about 1.50.

records.microscopy description: These particles of powdered soap have been spray dried and show a bubbled flake appearance. They are aggregates of small, low birefringent crystals (001000) and have indices near 1.50.
records.Extended description: These particles of powdered soap have been spray dried and show a bubbled flake appearance. They are aggregates of small, low birefringent crystals (001000) and have indices near 1.50. They are soft and can be pressed into coherent "pancakes" by pressure on the cover slip.

records.microscopy description: It is biaxial and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, equant crystals, usually in large agglomerates. Agglomerates of very small particles appear to be opaque;
records.Extended description: Tetrasodium pyrophosphate is soluble in water and insoluble in alcohol. It is biaxial and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, equant crystals, usually in large agglomerates. Cleavage is imperfect, and the fracture is uneven. The crystals have a specific gravity of 2.534. The refractive indices are 1.475 (alpha), 1.477 (beta), 1.496 (gamma); (+) 0.021. Agglomerates of very small particles appear to be opaque; large single crystals show birefringence.

records.microscopy description: Sodium tripolyphosphate is biaxial and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, equant agglomerates.
records.Extended description: Sodium tripolyphosphate is biaxial and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, equant agglomerates. It is soluble in water, insoluble in alcohol. The individual crystals have imperfect cleavage and uneven fracture. The refractive indices are: alpha-phase-1.477 (alpha), 1.478 (beta), 1.504 (gamma); (+) 0.027; beta-phase-1.470 (alpha), 1.477 (beta), 1.502 (gamma); (+) 0.032.

records.microscopy description: Particles of surfactant are more or less rounded, colorless polycrystalline aggregates. They are composed of birefringent crystallites aligned more or less parallel. If heated to about 150°C in Aroclor®, the aggregates darken slightly and crumble into separate small birefringent crystals.
records.Extended description: This surfactant is one of the wetting agents used in dry, mechanically mixed, heavy duty cleaners. Particles of surfactant are more or less rounded, colorless polycrystalline aggregates. They are composed of birefringent crystallites aligned more or less parallel. Surfactant aggregates soften at temperatures below 100°C and can be deformed easily by pressure on the cover slip into pancakelike masses of irregularly oriented soft crystals; at room temperature, the aggregates tend to crumble. If heated to about 150°C in Aroclor®, the aggregates darken slightly and crumble into separate small birefringent crystals. The birefringence is low, and the indices are near 1.50.

records.microscopy description: It is tetragonal and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms (001001).
records.Extended description: Chlorinated trisodium phosphate is soluble in water. It is tetragonal and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms (001001). Cleavage is imperfect, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured (001000). In air, chlorinated trisodium phosphate slowly loses chlorine and water of crystallization. At 100°C, they are released rapidly and completely. The refractive indices are 1.450 (omega) and 1.455 (epsilon); (+) 0.005. Small percentages of the octahydrate (001000) and of sodium chloride (336) (000000) will be found in all samples of this compound. The octahydrate crystallizes as tetragonal dipyramids, and several well-formed crystals of this phase appear in the figure.

records.microscopy description: It is tetragonal and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms (001001).
records.Extended description: Hydrated trisodium phosphate is soluble in water and insoluble in alcohol. It is tetragonal and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms (001001). Cleavage is observed parallel to the c crystallographic axis, and the fracture is uneven (001000) . The crystals have a specific gravity of 1.62. Hydrated trisodium phosphate loses water of crystallization and decomposes slowly in air; all twelve molecules of water are lost at 100°C. The refractive indices are 1.447 (omega), 1.452 (epsilon); (+) 0.005.

records.microscopy description: It is monoclinic and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms.
records.Extended description: Tetrasodium pyrophosphate is soluble in water and insoluble inalcohol and ammonium hydroxide. It is monoclinic and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms. Cleavage is poor, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured (001000). The crystals have a specific gravity of about 1.83, and slight effiorescence is apparent in dry air. Hydrated tetrasodium pyrophosphate loses one molecule of water of crystallization at 94 °C and melts at 880°C. The refractive indices are 1.4499 (alpha), 1.4525 (beta), 1.4604 (gamma); (+) 0.0105.

records.microscopy description: It is monoclinic and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms.
records.Extended description: Tetrasodium pyrophosphate is soluble in water and insoluble inalcohol and ammonium hydroxide. It is monoclinic and crystallizes as colorless, birefringent, elongated prisms. Cleavage is poor, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured (001000). The crystals have a specific gravity of about 1.83, and slight effiorescence is apparent in dry air. Hydrated tetrasodium pyrophosphate loses one molecule of water of crystallization at 94 °C and melts at 880°C. The refractive indices are 1.4499 (alpha), 1.4525 (beta), 1.4604 (gamma); (+) 0.0105.

records.microscopy description: These glassy, amorphous particles (sometimes tabular) are a ground product of a fusion process. They are attacked by moisture in the air, and the conchoidal surfaces are usually coated with fine particles of various hydrated calcium phosphates. Sometimes square tablets of calcium pyrophosphate dot these surfaces.
records.Extended description: The common name for calcium metaphosphate is calmeta. These glassy, amorphous particles (sometimes tabular) are a ground product of a fusion process. They are attacked by moisture in the air, and the conchoidal surfaces are usually coated with fine particles of various hydrated calcium phosphates. Sometimes square tablets of calcium pyrophosphate dot these surfaces. The refractive index is about 1.48, but variable. Small anisotropic phosphate crystals more or less cover the surface.

records.microscopy description: It crystallizes as colorless, isotropic trapezohedrons (n > = 1.6426).
records.Extended description: Ammonium chloride, NH4Cl, is moderately soluble in water and ammonium hydroxide and very slightly soluble in alcohol. It crystallizes as colorless, isotropic trapezohedrons (n > = 1.6426). Cleavage is imperfect, and ground crystals are conchoidally fractured. The crystals are soft (Moh 1.5-2) with a specific gravity of 1.53. The crystals show rounding due to their significant vapor pressure at room temperature. Ammonium chloride transforms at 156 C to another cubic modification and vaporizes at 350 C. The dispersion colors observed in Aroclor are red-orange with the annular stop and blue-green with the central stop; Ao= 640 nm. The orange tint in the figure, due to dispersion staining, is apparent even with an ordinary objective because ammonium chloride shows unusually strong dispersion.

records.microscopy description: Most crystals are equant, having rounded, often blobular surface texture. The birefringence, -gamma-alpha, for the room temperature form is very high (0.224); The dust particles will be fragments showing little or no external crystal morphology. The specific gravity of crystals of the stable form is 1.619.
records.Extended description: Ammonium nitrate, NH4N03, is a colorless, transparent, hygroscopic crystal; well-formed crystals are pseudotetragonal prisms. Most crystals are equant, having rounded, often blobular surface texture. Freshly ground, the fragments show conchoidal fracture. Ammonium nitrate has five crystal phases: tetragonal below -16 C, orthorhombic (-16 C to 32 C), biaxial (32 C to 84 C), tetragonal (84 C to 125 C) and cubic (125 C to 170 C, the melting point). The birefringence, -gamma-alpha, for the room temperature form is very high (0.224); 1.413 (alpha), 1.611 (beta), 1.637 (gamma). The ammonium nitrate as used in fertilizers is usually formed into spherical "prills" about 3/4 inch in diameter for easier handling. The dust particles will be fragments showing little or no external crystal morphology. The specific gravity of crystals of the stable form is 1.619.

records.microscopy description: It is tetragonal and crystallizes from water as colorless, birefringent prisms terminated by pyramids (001000). Cleavage is poor and ground crystals are conchoidally fractured, often elongated fragments (001001).
records.Extended description: Monoammonium phosphate, NH4H2PO4, is moderately soluble in water, slightly soluble in alcohol and insoluble in acetone. It is tetragonal and crystallizes from water as colorless, birefringent prisms terminated by pyramids (001000). Cleavage is poor and ground crystals are conchoidally fractured, often elongated fragments (001001). The crystals have a specific gravity of 1.803. The refractive indices of monoammonium phosphate are 1.5246 (omega), 1.4792 (epsilon); (-) 0.0454.

records.microscopy description: Crushed crystals are equant, having sharp edges, a smooth surface texture, uneven fracture and good cleavage.
records.Extended description: Diammonium phosphate, (NH4 nHPO4, is a colorless, transparent crystal: well-formed crystals are equant or prismatic. Crushed crystals are equant, having sharp edges, a smooth surface texture, uneven fracture and good cleavage. Diammonium phosphate is monoclinic prismatic; 1.468 (alpha), 1.570 (beta), 1.582 (gamma); (+) 0.114. Crystals have a specific gravity of 1.619 and decompose at 155 C on heating.

records.microscopy description: It usually has a slightly rough surface texture. Well-formed crystals are equant to prismatic and occasionally slightly flattened;
records.Extended description: Ammonium sulfate, (NH4)2SO4, is a transparent, colorless crystal when viewed using transmitted light. It usually has a slightly rough surface texture. Well-formed crystals are equant to prismatic and occasionally slightly flattened; the fracture is uneven and the cleavage is good. Ammonium sulfate is orthorhombic; 1.5209 (alpha), 1.5209 (beta), 1.5330 (gamma); (+) 0.0121. The crystals have a specific gravity of 1.769, and they decompose at 235 C.

records.microscopy description: Fragments which break away from the brown conglomerates are colorless or shades of yellow to dark brown; even particles less than 10 m may be opaque. They are of random shape but generally rounded and equant. The surface is rough and shriveled; particles less than 2 m have a smooth surface. Most of the particles look splotchy or mottled, primarily due to less than 2 m inclusions which are opaque.
records.Extended description: Industrial tankage is made from a variety of plant and animal products, garbage and industrial by-products. Meat scraps, intestines, bones and carcasses of dead animals are cooked under steam pressure; the greases are removed and the product is dried and ground. Organic materials processed this way through heat, steam and/ or chemicals have all of their recognizable morphology completely destroyed. The result is a brown meal of rounded conglomerates containing about 9.5-11 % nitrogen as NH3 and 12-20% calcium phosphate (bone). Fragments which break away from the brown conglomerates are colorless or shades of yellow to dark brown; even particles less than 10 m may be opaque. They are of random shape but generally rounded and equant. The surface is rough and shriveled; particles less than 2 m have a smooth surface. Most of the particles look splotchy or mottled, primarily due to less than 2 m inclusions which are opaque. All of the indices are around 1.53-1.55; the particles rarely show birefringence.

records.microscopy description: Recrystallized from water, colorless orthorhombic dipyramids are formed. These are brittle and fracture into flakes and equant particles with conchoidal surfaces.
records.Extended description: Recrystallized from water, colorless orthorhombic dipyramids are formed. These are brittle and fracture into flakes and equant particles with conchoidal surfaces. The refractive indices are 1.450 (alpha), 1.461 (beta), 1.477 (gamma).

records.microscopy description: Recrystallized from water, colorless orthorhombic dipyramids are formed. These are brittle and fracture into flakes and equant particles with conchoidal surfaces.
records.Extended description: Recrystallized from water, colorless orthorhombic dipyramids are formed. These are brittle and fracture into flakes and equant particles with conchoidal surfaces. The refractive indices are 1.450 (alpha), 1.461 (beta), 1.477 (gamma).

records.microscopy description: There are many kinds of particles in this sample, but the most distinctive are: 1. Fiber bundles of vegetable matter with rounded ends (a result of digestive action) and a darker color. Very small fragments of fibers or tissues, say 10 m, do not retain their shape and appear as colorless to dark yellow, transparent, cellulosic masses with a smooth surface, irregularly rounded in outline (001001, 011001, 000000, 010000). Transparent, colorless, hollow, smooth-surfaced, short, curved cylinders that come to a point at one end: about 8 X 120 m. These are trichomes similar to those found on cereal grains (294, 295, 337, 356) (001001).
records.Extended description: Sheep manure consists of undigested feed residues, especially corn bran, frequently accompanied by wood shavings (549), quartz sand (183) and limestone (161). Litters commonly found with both sheep and cow manure include straw (69) and other roughage, e.g., cottonseed hulls (312) with attached !inters (61). The identification of animal manure is assisted by the fact that most animals in licking themselves constantly take in hair which passes through the digestive tract. There are many kinds of particles in this sample, but the most distinctive are: 1. Fiber bundles of vegetable matter with rounded ends (a result of digestive action) and a darker color. Very small fragments of fibers or tissues, say 10 m, do not retain their shape and appear as colorless to dark yellow, transparent, cellulosic masses with a smooth surface, irregularly rounded in outline (001001, 011001, 000000, 010000). 2. Transparent, colorless, hollow, smooth-surfaced, short, curved cylinders that come to a point at one end: about 8 X 120 m. These are trichomes similar to those found on cereal grains (294, 295, 337, 356) (001001).

records.microscopy description: In bulk, the product looks like gray spheres with paper fibers protruding. Transparent to translucent, colorless to yellow to brown, weakly birefringent particles with indices about 1.53; particles thinner than 10 m tend to be colorless and apparently isotropic; larger particles are almost opaque. The particles are rough in outline and have a rough surface. Most appear to be made up of a transparent, colorless or brown matrix with innumerable colorless to opaque occlusions.
records.Extended description: This is a nitrogenous material produced from activated sludge at sewage disposal plants. In bulk, the product looks like gray spheres with paper fibers protruding. 1. Transparent to translucent, colorless to yellow to brown, weakly birefringent particles with indices about 1.53; particles thinner than 10 m tend to be colorless and apparently isotropic; larger particles are almost opaque. The particles are rough in outline and have a rough surface. Most appear to be made up of a transparent, colorless or brown matrix with innumerable colorless to opaque occlusions. At 1250X, the rounded to elongated occlusions are seen to be less than 1 m, most less than 0.5 m (001000, 011000). About 95% of the sample. 2. Transparent, colorless, flat paper fibers tapering to pointed ends; the indices are about 1.53; the interference colors are low (001011). About 5% of the sample.

records.microscopy description: Well-formed crystals are prismatic. Crushed particles are equant chips having sharp edges, rough surface texture, uneven fracture and poor basal cleavage. This is a good example of the effect of reflected light on color or, perhaps better, the effect of particle size on color. A particle, appearing to be opaque because it is an aggregate of small particles, will appear white by reflected light if the individual crystals are colorless and transparent.
records.Extended description: Phosphate rock, Ca5 (PO4) 3F, fluorapatite, is a transparent to translucent, colorless to light brown crystal. Well-formed crystals are prismatic. Crushed particles are equant chips having sharp edges, rough surface texture, uneven fracture and poor basal cleavage. Phosphate rock is hexagonal dipyramidal with indices of 1.6325 (omega), 1.6300 (epsilon); (-) 0.0025. These crystals are used both as a fertilizer and as a raw material for the manufacture of fertilizer. The specific gravity is about 3.20. Figures 284A and B show phosphate rock with transmitted light only (284A and C) and both reflected and transmitted light (284B). This is a good example of the effect of reflected light on color or, perhaps better, the effect of particle size on color. A particle, appearing to be opaque because it is an aggregate of small particles, will appear white by reflected light if the individual crystals are colorless and transparent. Phosphate rock has some color due to iron impurities, but most of the dark brown observed in 284A and 284G is due to light scattering by fine crystals.

records.microscopy description: Crushed crystals are equant, having sharp edges showing uneven fracture or cubic cleavage. In this sample, the birefringent occlusions are carbonates of calcium, magnesium and sodium.
records.Extended description: Potassium chloride, sylvite, KCl, is colorless, transparent and isotropic (n_D^25 = 1.490); well-formed crystals are cubes. Crushed crystals are equant, having sharp edges showing uneven fracture or cubic cleavage. In this sample, the birefringent occlusions are carbonates of calcium, magnesium and sodium. Potassium chloride can be easily differentiated from sodium chloride (336) and other 000000 substances by refractive index (1.490). The specific gravity is 1.984; the melting point is 776 C.

records.microscopy description: These particles dissolve in water but not in alcohol. They are tetragonal and recrystallize from water as colorless, birefringent prisms terminating in pyramids (001001).
records.Extended description: These particles dissolve in water but not in alcohol. They are tetragonal and recrystallize from water as colorless, birefringent prisms terminating in pyramids (001001). Cleavage is poor, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured (001000). The specific gravity of these crystals is 2.338. The crystals melt at 252.6 C and lose one molecule of water at 400 C, forming potassium metaphosphate. The refractive indices are 1.5095 (omega) and 1.4684 (epsilon); (-) 0.0411.

records.microscopy description: well-formed crystals are equant tablets, short prismatic or dipyramidal. Crushed crystals are equant, having rounded edges, uneven fracture and good cleavage.
records.Extended description: Potassium sulfate, K2S04, is colorless and transparent; well-formed crystals are equant tablets, short prismatic or dipyramidal. Crushed crystals are equant, having rounded edges, uneven fracture and good cleavage. Potassium sulfate is orthorhombic; 1.4935 (alpha), 1.4947 (beta), 1.4973 (gamma); (+) 0.0038. The density is 2.662; it transforms at 588 C on heating and melts at 1069 C.

records.microscopy description: Translucent to opaque, orange and brown to black, decomposed organic matter (000000, 010000); these are irregular isotropic masses with a foamy surface; Transparent, colorless, rounded, irregular particles of birefringent limestone, 100 m (5-250 m) (001000); Transparent, colorless, cotton and paper fibers of low birefringence, which average 150 m (50-750 m) (001001).
records.Extended description: As might be expected, this sample contains a great variety of components: 1. Translucent to opaque, orange and brown to black, decomposed organic matter (000000, 010000); these are irregular isotropic masses with a foamy surface; the fragments average 90 m (10-190 m). About 75% of the sample. 2. Transparent, colorless, rounded, irregular particles of birefringent limestone, 100 m (5-250 m) (001000); see calcite (133). About 10% of the sample. 3. Transparent, colorless, cotton and paper fibers of low birefringence, which average 150 m (50-750 m) (001001). See individual descriptions of paper (70-74) and cotton fibers (59). Minor components include quartz (183), glass (510), plant parts, diatoms (4-7), coal (559-561), coke (496), fused ash etc.

records.microscopy description: It is made up of colorless, transparent, submicroscopic crystals forming jagged agglomerates adhering to crystals of gypsum (151).
records.Extended description: Single superphosphate, 16 to 20% P20 5, is phosphate rock that has been reacted with sulfuric acid to make the phosphorus compounds more water soluble. It is made up of colorless, transparent, submicroscopic crystals forming jagged agglomerates adhering to crystals of gypsum (151). The phosphate agglomerates are translucent with a brown color by transmitted light. The refractive indices are less than 1.66 with low birefringence. The specific gravity is approximately 3.

records.microscopy description: Obviously, both systems of illumination must be used for any apparently opaque particles by transmitted light.
records.Extended description: Triple superphosphate, 44-48% P2O5, is phosphate rock that has been reacted with orthophosphoric acid to increase both phosphate content and water solubility. This product is made up of colorless, transparent, submicroscopic crystals of, principally, monocalcium phosphate usually forming agglomerates. The agglomerates are translucent and tan to dark brown by transmitted light. The refractive indices are less than 1.66 with low birefringence. The specific gravity is about 3.1. The possible variations in appearance in changing from crossed polars (290A) to reflected light (290B) are dramatic. Obviously, both systems of illumination must be used for any apparently opaque particles by transmitted light.

records.microscopy description: Urea is colorless, transparent and tetragonal: 1.484 (omega), 1.602 (epsilon); Crushed crystals are equant (001000) with distinct cleavage and a smooth surface texture.
records.Extended description: Urea is colorless, transparent and tetragonal: 1.484 (omega), 1.602 (epsilon); (+) 0.118; well-formed crystals are thin prisms. Crushed crystals are equant (001000) with distinct cleavage and a smooth surface texture. The crystals have a specific gravity of 1.32 and melt at 133 C.

5-10-30 fertilizer is a physical mixture of potassium chloride (285) (000000), and triple superphosphate (290) (001000). The designation 5-10-30 expresses the amounts of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in the fertilizer, the so-called NPK ratio. In order to provide a 5% nitrogen content, this product has been ammoniated, as evidenced by the presence of minute birefringent crystals of ammonium phosphate (277, 278) (001000) rather evenly distributed over the surface of the particles. All three components have been described earlier in this section. Most of the samples comprise large crystals of isotropic KCl (285) (000000) with coatings of smaller crystals of the other birefringent compounds.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, pale yellow cells with wavy walls. These almost isotropic cells are 14-25 X 25-70 µm (011010). Transparent, colorless, isotropic cells from the lower epidermis. They are 20-35 µm wide, 40-100 µm long. The stomates are ovals which are 20-40 X 10-25 µm (000010). The characteristic trichomes consist of two short cells, 15-20 µm long near the point of attachment, and a linear terminal cell, 350-1120 µm long.
records.Extended description: I. Transparent, pale yellow cells with wavy walls. These almost isotropic cells are 14-25 X 25-70 µm (011010). 2. Transparent, colorless, isotropic cells from the lower epidermis. They are 20-35 µm wide, 40-100 µm long. The stomates are ovals which are 20-40 X 10-25 µm (000010). 3. The characteristic trichomes consist of two short cells, 15-20 µm long near the point of attachment, and a linear terminal cell, 350-1120 µm long. The colorless, translucent trichome has thick walls and a warty cuticle. First-order interference colors (001001). 4. Transparent, colorless, glandular trichomes of low birefringence. They are 25 µm wide, 75-100 µm long (001001). 5. Pollen grains when present are transparent, colorless, isotropic spheres 30-35 µm; they have three pores and three furrows (000000). Calcium oxalate crystals (486) are also present (001000).

records.microscopy description: alfalfa dust (lucerne) | Elongated, rectangular, lignified cells alternating with short cells arranged in parallel rows. The yellow and orange-brown lignified cells are 12-20 µm wide, 20-150 µm long; the short cells are 20 µm long. Colorless to pale yellow, transparent, serrated cells. They have wavy, scalloped outlines with oval to circular pits. These cells are 25-30 µm wide and 20-40 µm long;
records.Extended description: Several kinds of cells characterize this sample; all have refractive indices around 1.53: 1. Elongated, rectangular, lignified cells alternating with short cells arranged in parallel rows. The yellow and orange-brown lignified cells are 12-20 µm wide, 20-150 µm long; the short cells are 20 µm long. Both types have low birefringence (011011). 2. Colorless to pale yellow, transparent, serrated cells. They have wavy, scalloped outlines with oval to circular pits. These cells are 25-30 µm wide and 20-40 µm long; they show low birefringence (001000, 011000 (295B). 3. Isotropic, transparent, colorless, subrectangular cells. They are 12-25 µm wide, 50-170 µm long (000001). 4. Transparent, colorless, lignified fibers. These show low birefringence, are 10 µm wide and up to 380 µm long (001001). 5. Unicellular, conical trichomes, or plant hairs. Transparent and colorless, they are 20-30 µm wide at the point of attachment, 60-150 µm long; their birefringence is low (001001) (295B). 6. Starch. These transparent, colorless, oval grains are 10-40 µm long. They resemble wheat starch (349) but are more irregular and slightly smaller. Between crossed polars, they are gray with a black cross (001000).

records.microscopy description: bean dust | Starch: spherical to oval, 10-30 µm particles with low-order interference colors and a moderately strong extinction cross (001000). Transparent, colorless, irregular to rounded, 5 µm particles with low birefringence (001000). Clay: transparent, colorless, rounded, 1-3 µm particles with low interference colors (001000). Humus: transparent to translucent, light yellow to brown, 1-15 µm, irregular to rounded particles of decayed plant material which may be isotropic (010000) to anisotropic (011000).
records.Extended description: This dust from an electric sorting machine consists of some bean tissue but is mostly soil components and other dusts associated with the cleaning and sorting of beans. 1. Starch: spherical to oval, 10-30 µm particles with low-order interference colors and a moderately strong extinction cross (001000). 2. Transparent, colorless, irregular to rounded, 5 µm particles with low birefringence (001000). 3. Clay: transparent, colorless, rounded, 1-3 µm particles with low interference colors (001000). 4. Humus: transparent to translucent, light yellow to brown, 1-15 µm, irregular to rounded particles of decayed plant material which may be isotropic (010000) to anisotropic (011000). Other components include 1-20 µm quartz, corn starch, wheat starch, hematite, calcite, mold spores and a trace of diatoms.

records.microscopy description: At higher magnification, there is a tissue network of generally compressed, transparent, colorless, flat, polygonal cells 15-30 µm across which are isotropic (000000) or weakly birefringent (001000). There are also birefringent, spiral vascular bundles that resemble miniature tracheae.
records.Extended description: Beet pulp is a waste product of the sugar industry-the dried residue from sugar beets which have been cleaned of debris and extracted for sugar. It is used mostly in dairy feeds. Under the stereomicroscope, it shows as tough, gray, stringy, slightly curled threads (resulting from shredding the beet) which absorb water readily. At higher magnification, there is a tissue network of generally compressed, transparent, colorless, flat, polygonal cells 15-30 µm across which are isotropic (000000) or weakly birefringent (001000). The cells may also be stained brown (010000, 011000). There are also birefringent, spiral vascular bundles that resemble miniature tracheae. Some of the cells contain calcium oxalate crystals.

records.microscopy description: bone dust | Irregular, colorless to gray-brown fragments and some thin plates with rough outlines and a few smooth faces constitute this sample (001000, 011000, 001010, 011010). The particles average 50 µm in width (3-385 µm). Between crossed polars, the gray to first-order yellow particles show undulose or wavy fanlike extinction. In thin-edged fragments, some of the histological features should be discernable, viz., concentric flat plates (the lamellae) and grooves and channels (the canaliculi). The thin edges are transparent; larger particles are translucent.
records.Extended description: Irregular, colorless to gray-brown fragments and some thin plates with rough outlines and a few smooth faces constitute this sample (001000, 011000, 001010, 011010). The particles average 50 µm in width (3-385 µm). Between crossed polars, the gray to first-order yellow particles show undulose or wavy fanlike extinction. In thin-edged fragments, some of the histological features should be discernable, viz., concentric flat plates (the lamellae) and grooves and channels (the canaliculi). Bits of articular cartilage, marrow and, occasionally, blood vessel remnants may also be present. About 65% of the total weight of bone is mineral substance, especially tricalcium phosphate; the remainder is an organic matrix, chiefly collagen. The thin edges are transparent; larger particles are translucent. In reflected light, the particles are colorless to milk-white with some yellow and orange. Indices are around 1.60.

records.microscopy description: Brewer's grits is a refined form of cornstarch. The cornstarch is present here as colorless to gray, transparent to translucent agglomerates averaging 130 µm across (10-500 µm). For a description of the individual grains, see cornstarch (344).
records.Extended description: Brewer's grits is a refined form of cornstarch. After the refining process, a small portion of the protein, in the form of germ and oil, is blended back in. The cornstarch is present here as colorless to gray, transparent to translucent agglomerates averaging 130 µm across (10-500 µm). For a description of the individual grains, see cornstarch (344). The sample strongly resembles corn meal (310), but one is less apt to find bits of husks and the like in brewer's grits; also, more protein and oil are blended back into corn meal.

records.microscopy description: It dissolves quickly in hot Aroclor® 5442, then forms long needles on cooling (300A) : 1. Long, colorless, hexagonal prisms showing high birefringence (0.272) and negative elongation (001101). This may or may not form, depending on temperature conditions.
records.Extended description: Acetone, benzene or chloroform will dissolve caffeine; it is slightly soluble in water and alcohol, very slightly soluble in ether. It dissolves quickly in hot Aroclor® 5442, then forms long needles on cooling (300A) : 1. Long, colorless, hexagonal prisms showing high birefringence (0.272) and negative elongation (001101). 2. Very fine, stubby prisms and rods (300A). This may or may not form, depending on temperature conditions. Crystals mounted in a Cargille refractive index liquid without heat are characterized by high birefringence and one index, usually parallel to the long direction, higher than that of the medium (300A). Caffeine sublimes between 180 and 200°C, melts at 238°C. The refractive indices are 1.707 (omega) and 1.435 (epsilon); (-) 0.272.

records.microscopy description: Most of the particles here show the epidermis which consists of "bubble" cells that look like masses of rounded, 6-10 µm doughy balls. They are isotropic (000000) but may contain minute (<l µm) birefringent inclusions (001000). Occasional 3 X 15 µm blades (001011) and fusion droplets with first-order interference colors may be the poisonous principles of the bean.
records.Extended description: The seed of the castor bean, Ricinus communis, yields castor oil. All parts of the plant, but particularly the bean, are poisonous to humans, cattle and poultry-as few as three beans have produced death in an adult man. The poison responsible is the albumin ricin, a blood poison, and the alkaloid ricinine. Most of the particles here show the epidermis which consists of "bubble" cells that look like masses of rounded, 6-10 µm doughy balls. They are isotropic (000000) but may contain minute (<l µm) birefringent inclusions (001000). An orange to brown, non-particulate stain may color some of the tissue (010000). Occasional 3 X 15 µm blades (001011) and fusion droplets with first-order interference colors may be the poisonous principles of the bean.

records.microscopy description: The irregular fragments contain a great many air bubbles fairly uniformly 0.5 µm in diameter. The bubbles scatter light and cause the particles to appear brown to opaque black. Some particles show stratification and/ or striations. The particles disappear, showing only the air bubbles, at some point of stage rotation when that index almost matches that of Aroclor®.
records.Extended description: These particles are composed essentially of calcium carbonate and have the optical properties of calcite (133), q.v. The irregular fragments contain a great many air bubbles fairly uniformly 0.5 µm in diameter. The bubbles scatter light and cause the particles to appear brown to opaque black. A number of pieces show the air bubbles more or less aligned. Some particles show stratification and/ or striations. The particles disappear, showing only the air bubbles, at some point of stage rotation when that index almost matches that of Aroclor®.

records.microscopy description: These crystals are slightly deliquescent at room temperature but lose water on heating to give a monoclinic anhydrous form which melts at 153 °C. those of the monoclinic form are higher. The specific gravity is 1.542 for the hydrate, 1.665 for the anhydrous form.
records.Extended description: Citric acid is soluble in water and alcohol and slightly soluble in ether. The monohydrate crystallizes from water at room temperature as orthorhombic prisms and pinacoids showing good basal cleavage. These crystals are slightly deliquescent at room temperature but lose water on heating to give a monoclinic anhydrous form which melts at 153 °C. The hydrate has indices of 1.4932 (alpha), 1.4977 (beta), 1.5089 (gamma) ; (+) 0.0157; those of the monoclinic form are higher. The specific gravity is 1.542 for the hydrate, 1.665 for the anhydrous form.

records.microscopy description: citrus dust | These bits of peel and pulp were collected on an Alundum® thimble from a dryer fired with a bunker C oil burner The transparent to translucent citrus portions (000000, 010000, 011000, 001000) average 100 µm in diameter (2-700 µm). a few particles are colorless (000000). some are isotropic.
records.Extended description: These bits of peel and pulp were collected on an Alundum® thimble from a dryer fired with a bunker C oil burner The transparent to translucent citrus portions (000000, 010000, 011000, 001000) average 100 µm in diameter (2-700 µm). In addition, however, there are black, opaque spheres of oil soot (556-558), 40 µm (12-> 100 µm) in diameter (100000) and bits of birefringent aluminum oxide from the thimble, 90 µm wide (50-> 180 µm) (001100). The indices of the tissue are 1.53; the indices of the Alundum are about 1.76 (see corundum, 137). Samples of this kind contain mixtures of various cell and tissue types. The cells are generally large and pulpy; they contain calcium oxalate crystals (486) with indices of 1.49 (alpha) to 1.65 (gamma) (001000). One striking feature of this sample is that, in transmitted light, the colors seen are particularly deep and rich yellows, oranges and orange-browns (010000, 011000); a few particles are colorless (000000). The samples differ, of course, in content; they are likely to represent the waste of a variety of citrus fruits. The refractive indices are about 1.53. Most of the fragments are gray between crossed polars; some are isotropic.

records.microscopy description: citrus dust | These bits of peel and pulp were collected on an Alundum® thimble from a dryer fired with a bunker C oil burner The transparent to translucent citrus portions (000000, 010000, 011000, 001000) average 100 µm in diameter (2-700 µm). a few particles are colorless (000000). some are isotropic.

In addition, however, there are black, opaque spheres of oil soot (556-558), 40 µm (12-> 100 µm) in diameter (100000) and bits of birefringent aluminum oxide from the thimble, 90 µm wide (50-> 180 µm) (001100). The indices of the tissue are 1.53; the indices of the Alundum are about 1.76 (see corundum, 137). Samples of this kind contain mixtures of various cell and tissue types.
