records.microscopy description: Most particles are colorless to dark brown and show low birefringence but contain many birefringent rosettes and crystals of calcium oxalate (486) (001000). Long, narrow, colorless to orange-brown fibers, 8-10 µm wide and up to 250 µm long from near the outside skin of the bean (011001, 001001), have low birefringence. Elongated, flat, polygonal cells, 20-40 µm wide and 90-150 µm long (011011, 001011). They are lightly colored to colorless, with very low birefringence. Very characteristic brown, thick-walled, rectangular or polygonal cells, 10-30 µm long and 5-10 µm wide (011000). colorless and moderate birefringence (001001).
records.Extended description: Most particles are colorless to dark brown and show low birefringence but contain many birefringent rosettes and crystals of calcium oxalate (486) (001000). The refractive indices are about 1.53 for the tissue, 1.49 (alpha) to 1.65 (gamma) for the calcium oxalate. This sample includes: 1. Long, narrow, colorless to orange-brown fibers, 8-10 µm wide and up to 250 µm long from near the outside skin of the bean (011001, 001001), have low birefringence. 2. Elongated, flat, polygonal cells, 20-40 µm wide and 90-150 µm long (011011, 001011). They are lightly colored to colorless, with very low birefringence. 3. Very characteristic brown, thick-walled, rectangular or polygonal cells, 10-30 µm long and 5-10 µm wide (011000). They show low birefringence. 4. Spiral vessels, usually in parallel array; colorless and moderate birefringence (001001). 5. Starch grains, rounded to rounded-polygonal, 4-9 µm in diameter. They are gray with a black cross under crossed polars (001000).

records.microscopy description: Isotropic or low birefringent tissue is present sometimes with calcium oxalate (486) (001000). Immediate examination in immersion oil shows birefringent caffeine (300) needles which dissolve in a few minutes. The important particles are: 1. Cells with thick birefringent walls. They range in size from 24 µm to 80 µm (011000). Moderately thick-walled cells with large oval pits.
records.Extended description: Isotropic or low birefringent tissue is present sometimes with calcium oxalate (486) (001000). Immediate examination in immersion oil shows birefringent caffeine (300) needles which dissolve in a few minutes. The important particles are: 1. Cells with thick birefringent walls. The yellow to brown cells are square, rectangular or polyhedral. They range in size from 24 µm to 80 µm (011000). 2. Moderately thick-walled cells with large oval pits. These cells from the meaty portion of the bean, the endosperm, are 20-60 µm wide and 50-80 µm long. Almost isotropic, they are translucent and vary in color from shades of yellow through oranges to browns (011000). 3. Very common and characteristic, highly lignified cells with hardened walls, the sclerids. The sclerids are elongated ovals or boats with numerous oval pits arranged side by side in groups of 2 to 20 or more. The colorless, translucent cells average 20 X 150 µm (12-65 µm wide, 100-375 µm long). Between crossed polars, the birefringent sclerids themselves are bright gray but frequently appear shades of yellow and orange because lignin in the surrounding tissues masks the true gray (001001, 011001). 4. Spiral vessels of low birefringence, 5-10 µm wide. These translucent vessels, which look like tightly wound springs and originate from the seamlike union of the two halves of the bean, are not very abundant and may not be seen in all samples (001001). See coffee chaff (307).

records.microscopy description: The seed coat, or chaff, of coffee is a diaphanous, flake-like tissue characterized by the presence of lignified sclerids. the transparent, extremely thin tissue resembles a grayish brown, homogeneous film which is almost isotropic (011010).
records.Extended description: The seed coat, or chaff, of coffee is a diaphanous, flake-like tissue characterized by the presence of lignified sclerids. 1. Highly lignified sclerids. See coffee (306), component 3, for a complete description (001001, 011001). 2. The individual cells of the parenchyma are difficult to see; the transparent, extremely thin tissue resembles a grayish brown, homogeneous film which is almost isotropic (011010). Tiny fragments and rosettes of calcium oxalate (486) are scattered throughout.

records.microscopy description: Irregular fragments of translucent, yellow-brown tissue, straight and sharp to rounded, appear here (011010). Some consist of 25 µm birefringent cells shaped like honeycombs (011000); The particles in this sample average 900 µm across (320->3000 µm). Cornstarch grains (344) are present (001000) but are not as abundant as in corn meal (310) or corn powder (311);
records.Extended description: Irregular fragments of translucent, yellow-brown tissue, straight and sharp to rounded, appear here (011010). Some consist of 25 µm birefringent cells shaped like honeycombs (011000); others include long rectangular cells with serrated walls (011001). The particles in this sample average 900 µm across (320->3000 µm). These rough tissues are from the corncob and portions of the plant other than the seed. Cornstarch grains (344) are present (001000) but are not as abundant as in corn meal (310) or corn powder (311); they help to reveal the identity of this sample. The tissues are gray to orange between crossed polars; the refractive indices are about 1.53. In reflected light, the tissues are white, shades of yellow and orange-brown.

records.microscopy description: This sample consists of four kinds of particles: 1. Transparent, orange to reddish-brown, thick-walled, birefringent, square to mostly rectangular (approximately 30 X 100 µm) cells aligned like rows of brick or resembling a net (011010). Transparent, colorless, thin-walled, birefringent, approximately rectangular cells (30 X 80 µm) which form a light, filmy tissue (001010) and may contain starch grains -component 1 above. Colorless to yellow and orange, unstructured, plastic-looking masses with very low birefringence which may also contain cornstarch grains.
records.Extended description: This sample consists of four kinds of particles: 1. Corn starch (344), q.v. (001000). 2. Transparent, orange to reddish-brown, thick-walled, birefringent, square to mostly rectangular (approximately 30 X 100 µm) cells aligned like rows of brick or resembling a net (011010). 3. Transparent, colorless, thin-walled, birefringent, approximately rectangular cells (30 X 80 µm) which form a light, filmy tissue (001010) and may contain starch grains -component 1 above. 4. Colorless to yellow and orange, unstructured, plastic-looking masses with very low birefringence which may also contain cornstarch grains.

records.microscopy description: corn meal dust | These large agglomerates of transparent, colorless, birefringent, polyhedral starch grains (001000) have many jagged edges and both smooth and rough faces. The agglomerates average 200 µm across (50-1000 µm). See cornstarch (344) for a description of individual grains.This sample is essentially large clumps of starch grains;
records.Extended description: These large agglomerates of transparent, colorless, birefringent, polyhedral starch grains (001000) have many jagged edges and both smooth and rough faces. The agglomerates average 200 µm across (50-1000 µm). See cornstarch (344) for a description of individual grains.This sample is essentially large clumps of starch grains; an occasional bit of rough seed covering or husk with low birefringence may be seen (001000, 001010). The refractive indices are about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: Large sheets of cells (chaff; 001010, 011010), 10 µm to more than 7 mm long, and polyhedral grains (starch; The colorless to orange sheets of chaff are composed of large, empty, transparent, colorless, rounded, rectangular cells, 25 X 80 µm. The sheets, although large, are exceedingly light and readily airborne. The starch grains help to identify the kind of plant from which the sample came. See cornstarch (344) for a description of individual grains.
records.Extended description: Large sheets of cells (chaff; 001010, 011010), 10 µm to more than 7 mm long, and polyhedral grains (starch; 001000) are scattered throughout this sample. The colorless to orange sheets of chaff are composed of large, empty, transparent, colorless, rounded, rectangular cells, 25 X 80 µm. The sheets, although large, are exceedingly light and readily airborne. The starch grains help to identify the kind of plant from which the sample came. See cornstarch (344) for a description of individual grains. The refractive indices are about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: The tissue of this transparent to translucent cellular material is smoothly rounded or gently irregular in outline; the surface is generally smooth though tissues from the outside of the seed are quite wrinkled. The tissues range from colorless in tiny fragments to shades of yellow and orange (001000, 001010, 011000, 011010).
records.Extended description: The tissue of this transparent to translucent cellular material is smoothly rounded or gently irregular in outline; the surface is generally smooth though tissues from the outside of the seed are quite wrinkled. The tissues range from colorless in tiny fragments to shades of yellow and orange (001000, 001010, 011000, 011010). Individual cells are seldom seen. Between crossed polars, the tissues may appear yellow to orange due to scattered c alcium oxalate (486), 1.49 (alpha) to 1.65 (gamma) (001000). The most dominant feature of this sample is the presence of cotton linters (61). These (001001) are a clue to identity. All tissues have a refractive index around 1.53. Trapped air and oil droplets are common.

records.microscopy description: It forms colorless, birefringent, six-sided monoclinic tablets. flakes are common (001010).
records.Extended description: Dextrose is highly soluble in water, very slightly soluble in alcohol and insoluble in ether. It forms colorless, birefringent, six-sided monoclinic tablets. Cleavage is poor, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured (001000) ; flakes are common (001010). The crystals have a specific gravity of 1.544. Dextrose melts in its water of crystallization at about 83 °C. The refractive indices are 1.529 (alpha), 1.555 (beta), 1.566 (gamma); (-) 0.037.

records.microscopy description: Wheat and wheat grain dust (356), q.v.
records.Extended description: This is, of course, a variable product whose constituents may represent many food categories. This particular dog meal sample contains: 1. 90-95% com meal. See corn (ground) (308) and corn meal (310) (001000, 001010, 011000, 011001, 011010). 2. Wheat and wheat grain dust (356), q.v. (000001, 001000, 001001, 011000). 3. A very small amount of meat and bone scraps. See bone dust (298) (001000, 001010, 011000, 011010). Other particles include hairs, paper fibers and hematite.

records.microscopy description: The resulting particles are transparent to translucent, colorless to brown masses of pulped feathers that have a surface resembling a plate of cooked spaghetti (000000, 010000). Individually, the feather particles are colorless, transparent, straight or (usually) curved, melted plastic tubes (000001, 000011), some of which may show some strain birefringence (001001).
records.Extended description: This material results from the drying, grinding and treatment under steam pressure of poultry feathers. The resulting particles are transparent to translucent, colorless to brown masses of pulped feathers that have a surface resembling a plate of cooked spaghetti (000000, 010000). This appearance results from the incomplete breakdown of the rachis, or stem. Individually, the feather particles are colorless, transparent, straight or (usually) curved, melted plastic tubes (000001, 000011), some of which may show some strain birefringence (001001).

records.microscopy description: The cooked fish tissue is colorless to yellow and brown, isotropic, rounded amorphous masses (000000, 010000) which contain tiny, 1 µm, equant or needlelike, birefringent inclusions (001000, 001001). The bones are transparent to translucent, colorless, narrow cylinders with low birefringence (001001). The scales are transparent, colorless, flat or curved plates with low birefringence (001010) and with or without concentric surface markings.
records.Extended description: Fish meal is the result of cleaning undecomposed whole fish or fish cuttings, cooking under steam pressure, pressing for removal of oils, drying and grinding. I. The cooked fish tissue is colorless to yellow and brown, isotropic, rounded amorphous masses (000000, 010000) which contain tiny, 1 µm, equant or needlelike, birefringent inclusions (001000, 001001). 2. The bones are transparent to translucent, colorless, narrow cylinders with low birefringence (001001). 3. The scales are transparent, colorless, flat or curved plates with low birefringence (001010) and with or without concentric surface markings. Small, conical teeth and glass-beadlike eyes may also be seen.

records.microscopy description: Most of the sample consists of colorless, transparent, isotropic, 15-50 µm, polygonal, thin-walled cells of the endosperm and embryo tissue, without the starch grains and without the oil globules (000000).
records.Extended description: This sample is histologically the same as linseed meal (324), q.v. Here, however, the seeds have had all of the starch and linseed oil removed so that now the sample shows essentially only three components: 1. Most of the sample consists of colorless, transparent, isotropic, 15-50 µm, polygonal, thin-walled cells of the endosperm and embryo tissue, without the starch grains and without the oil globules (000000). 2. Some thin, orange-red, translucent, isotropic, rounded parallelograms (usually square or diamond shaped) of pigment cells averaging 15 µm (010010). 3. Transparent, colorless, rounded, isotropic particles (5-15 µm) of protein material-the aleurone grains (000000).

records.microscopy description: This product, however, is prepared from the smaller, imperfect flaxseeds, weed seeds and other foreign material separated in the cleaning of flaxseed, and will show these particles.
records.Extended description: This sample is like linseed meal (324), q.v., and has all of the same kinds of tissues. This product, however, is prepared from the smaller, imperfect flaxseeds, weed seeds and other foreign material separated in the cleaning of flaxseed, and will show these particles. This sample is the dust from a batch which has not yet been pressed for removal of the linseed oil. Cf. (317) and (324).

records.microscopy description: These colorless (000000) to gray and gray-brown (010000), transparent, isotropic, spherical and approximately spherical particles strongly tend to form groups, depending largely on the amount of moisture present. The spherical nature indicates that the sample is a spray-dried product. The spheres are water-soluble and soften or melt on heating. They average 25 µm (5-90 µm) in diameter in this sample.
records.Extended description: These colorless (000000) to gray and gray-brown (010000), transparent, isotropic, spherical and approximately spherical particles strongly tend to form groups, depending largely on the amount of moisture present. The spherical nature indicates that the sample is a spray-dried product. The spheres are water-soluble and soften or melt on heating. They average 25 µm (5-90 µm) in diameter in this sample. records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless starch grains (90+% of the sample) are round to oval, about 24 X 45 µm; They resemble potato starch (345), but differ in having a protuberance at one end and showing fewer grains with an air bubble (001000). These are columns (to 35 µm diameter) of birefringent rings that resemble tracheae. Transparent, orange, amorphous masses of the oleo-resin, gingerin (011000). Other particles include the partially lignified but birefringent fibers of the fibrovascular bundle with their moderately thick walls and wide lumen, and transparent, colorless, filmy, cellular tissue that enclosed the starch grains.
records.Extended description: This sample of ground ginger, the prepared root of the perennial herb Zingiber o-fficinale, is characterized by three major components: 1. Transparent, colorless starch grains (90+% of the sample) are round to oval, about 24 X 45 µm; some have a stellate to tiny dot internal air bubble and show a moderately dark cross between crossed polars. They resemble potato starch (345), but differ in having a protuberance at one end and showing fewer grains with an air bubble (001000). 2. Vessels. These are columns (to 35 µm diameter) of birefringent rings that resemble tracheae. If split, they look like backbones with ribs attached (001000, 001001). 3. Transparent, orange, amorphous masses of the oleo-resin, gingerin (011000). Other particles include the partially lignified but birefringent fibers of the fibrovascular bundle with their moderately thick walls and wide lumen, and transparent, colorless, filmy, cellular tissue that enclosed the starch grains.

records.microscopy description: Because their preparation involves drying and crushing, the resulting flakes have no characteristic outline and resemble the larger irregular shapes one obtains by crushing a dried leaf. The fragment sizes will also vary from less than 10 µm to more than 5 mm; The surface is slightly rough and covered in many places with opaque splotches 5 µm in diameter.
records.Extended description: This is a marine alga, a seaweed. Because their preparation involves drying and crushing, the resulting flakes have no characteristic outline and resemble the larger irregular shapes one obtains by crushing a dried leaf. The fragment sizes will also vary from less than 10 µm to more than 5 mm; the microscopist is not likely to encounter larger pieces although the plant itself may grow to several meters. High magnification reveals olive-green to olive-brown pigment bodies although there is a yellow-brown color throughout. The surface is slightly rough and covered in many places with opaque splotches 5 µm in diameter. The translucent fragments are yellow, orange and dark brown in transmitted light and shades of yellow to olive-brown in reflected light. Birefringence is very weak gray to first-order yellow. Indices are about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: It is monoclinic and forms colorless, transparent, birefringent wedges.
records.Extended description: alpha-Lactose dissolves slowly in water, is very slightly soluble in alcohol and is insoluble in ether and chloroform. It is monoclinic and forms colorless, transparent, birefringent wedges. Cleavage is distinct, but ground crystals also show considerable conchoidal fracture. The specific gravity is 1.525. a-Lactose loses its water of crystallization at 120°C and melts at 201.6°C. The refractive indices are 1.517 (alpha), 1.542 (beta), 1.555 (gamma); (-) 0.038.

records.microscopy description: Some of these expanded, collapsed and distorted hollow spheres and subspheres are actually shaped like lemons. The spheres, typical of a spray-dried product, are transparent and isotropic with a refractive index below 1.66. They are colorless with smoothly undulose surfaces and an average diameter of 15 µm (5-65 µm) diameter.
records.Extended description: Some of these expanded, collapsed and distorted hollow spheres and subspheres are actually shaped like lemons. The spheres, typical of a spray-dried product, are transparent and isotropic with a refractive index below 1.66. They are colorless with smoothly undulose surfaces and an average diameter of 15 µm (5-65 µm) diameter.

records.microscopy description: Closely packed cells, loose polygonal grains, some fibers and agglomerates of all of these appear in this sample. The particles average 80 µm (10-650 µm) in length and have a refractive index of about 1.53. Polygonal, tabular, epidermal cells. These are colorless to yellow, translucent, isotropic, 30-45 µm across; many contain starch grains (000000, 010000). Orange-red, thin, translucent, isotropic, rounded parallelograms (averaging 15 µm wide).
records.Extended description: Closely packed cells, loose polygonal grains, some fibers and agglomerates of all of these appear in this sample. The particles average 80 µm (10-650 µm) in length and have a refractive index of about 1.53. The individual components are: 1. Polygonal, tabular, epidermal cells. These are colorless to yellow, translucent, isotropic, 30-45 µm across; many contain starch grains (000000, 010000). 2. Orange-red, thin, translucent, isotropic, rounded parallelograms (averaging 15 µm wide). They are bits of the cuticle (010010). 3. Lignified cells with hard walls-the sclerids. They are 8-14 µm wide, 120-190 µm long. The translucent, colorless to yellow cells are weakly birefringent, gray in aggregates (001001, 011001). 4. Isotropic, colorless, transparent, polygonal, tabular cells from the inner epidermis. These are 20-50 µm in diameter (000000). 5. Colorless, transparent, isotropic grains containing protein matter. They are aleurone grains, 5-15 µm across (000000). 6. Transparent, colorless, rounded-polygonal starch grains. They average 8 µm wide and under crossed polars are gray with a black cross (001000). 7. Conical, birefringent, hollow trichomes or plant hairs. Not very common, they are about 10 µm wide and 200 µm long (001001).

records.microscopy description: Most of these whole and distorted, colorless, transparent to translucent, isotropic spheres and other rounded particles contain one or more air bubbles, indicating that the sample has been spray-dried. The particles agglomerate into rounded groups (000000). The isotropic matrix usually contains gray, birefringent specks throughout. A few separate crystals of birefringent material (pastels) may also be present (001000). The surface is generally smooth. The particles in this sample average 10 µm (3-90 µm) in diameter.
records.Extended description: Most of these whole and distorted, colorless, transparent to translucent, isotropic spheres and other rounded particles contain one or more air bubbles, indicating that the sample has been spray-dried. The particles agglomerate into rounded groups (000000). The isotropic matrix usually contains gray, birefringent specks throughout. A few separate crystals of birefringent material (pastels) may also be present (001000). The surface is generally smooth. The particles in this sample average 10 µm (3-90 µm) in diameter. The refractive index is about 1.50. In reflected light, the particles are colorless to milk-white.

records.microscopy description: The triclinic crystals made from water solution at 130°C are colorless, transparent, birefringent rods (001001) or tablets (001010) with oblique extinction. Dark traces of hydration mark the surfaces of these crystals.
records.Extended description: Monocalcium phosphate dissolves in water. The triclinic crystals made from water solution at 130°C are colorless, transparent, birefringent rods (001001) or tablets (001010) with oblique extinction. Cleavage is absent, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured (001000). Their specific gravity is 2.546. Monocalcium phosphate decomposes at 268 °C. The refractive indices are 1.548 (alpha), 1.572 (beta), 1.602 (gamma); (+) 0.054. Dark traces of hydration mark the surfaces of these crystals.

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless, birefringent, sharp-edged fragments (001000) of lactose (322), 1.517 (alpha) to 1.555 (gamma), are intimately associated here with isotropic casein (000000). Lactose particles are 8-12 µm in diameter and form agglomerates about 50 µm wide, "cemented" by the casein. In reflected light, individual particles are colorless; occasional large particles of lactose show first- and second-order colors.
records.Extended description: Transparent, colorless, birefringent, sharp-edged fragments (001000) of lactose (322), 1.517 (alpha) to 1.555 (gamma), are intimately associated here with isotropic casein (000000). The casein is almost impossible to discern; its presence is indicated largely by the loose agglomerates of lactose. Lactose particles are 8-12 µm in diameter and form agglomerates about 50 µm wide, "cemented" by the casein. In reflected light, individual particles are colorless; the agglomerates appear milky white. Interference colors are mostly gray, with some white to pale first-order yellow; occasional large particles of lactose show first- and second-order colors.

records.microscopy description: This sample of powdered yellow mustard consists of transparent, colorless, isotropic, 6-10 µm, rounded, partially collapsed, thin-walled cells (000000), frequently found in compact, pale yellow masses (010000). Throughout the masses there are numerous, tiny (3 X 4 µm) birefringent plates or rhombs (001010) and needles (001001) or fragments thereof (001000).
records.Extended description: This sample of powdered yellow mustard consists of transparent, colorless, isotropic, 6-10 µm, rounded, partially collapsed, thin-walled cells (000000), frequently found in compact, pale yellow masses (010000). Throughout the masses there are numerous, tiny (3 X 4 µm) birefringent plates or rhombs (001010) and needles (001001) or fragments thereof (001000). Interference colors of the crystals are first-order grays and white.

records.microscopy description: The hull consists of layers of 10-15 µm diameter, birefringent fibers (001001, 001011) crisscrossing each other at all angles; Transparent, colorless, weakly birefringent, thin-walled parenchyma cells, about 40-60 µm across, forming a very thin, light tissue (001010). Mostly 6 µm (to 15 µm), round to slightly oval;
records.Extended description: This material consists of the ground hulls with a bit of the meal and possibly some of the skin (331) ; it is used as a diluent or carrier in animal feed products. Several tissues can be seen: 1. The hull consists of layers of 10-15 µm diameter, birefringent fibers (001001, 001011) crisscrossing each other at all angles; the separated fibers adhere to each other in tight bundles. In heated chloral hydrate (8:5), the fibers appear greenishgammaellow. 2. Transparent, colorless, weakly birefringent, thin-walled parenchyma cells, about 40-60 µm across, forming a very thin, light tissue (001010). A small amount of similar tissue is brownish-orange (011010). 5. Starch. Mostly 6 µm (to 15 µm), round to slightly oval; occasional tiny internal air bubble; dark cross between crossed polars, in common with other starches (001000).

records.microscopy description: Most of this sample is composed of transparent, pale pink to salmon pink and orange tissue made up of mostly 4- or 5-sided, 10-50 µm, birefringent cells with thick walls. The inner walls of the cells have birefringent, pointed (mostly) or rounded, 5-15 µm long projections growing toward the center of the cell (011010).
records.Extended description: This consists of the outer covering of the kernel, exclusive of hulls; it is obtained from the milling process and is used in animal feeds. Most of this sample is composed of transparent, pale pink to salmon pink and orange tissue made up of mostly 4- or 5-sided, 10-50 µm, birefringent cells with thick walls. The inner walls of the cells have birefringent, pointed (mostly) or rounded, 5-15 µm long projections growing toward the center of the cell (011010). This sample also contains some of the meaty portion of the peanut (001000) and a considerable amount of starch (001000). See peanut hulls (330).

records.microscopy description: The translucent, yellow to red-orange cells are about 15 X 25 X 60 µm and have thick walls (011000). These translucent, yellowish to red-orange, rounded cells have low birefringence, are 30-85 µm long, 15-20 µm wide and 15-20 µm thick. Thin-walled, almost isotropic, transparent cells, 1000 X 300 X 150 µm. Despite their size, these colorless cells are very light after drying (001010). Very characteristic cells with heavy, wavy, birefringent walls; the yellowish cells are 30-90 µm long, 15-60 µm wide and 30 µm thick (011000).
records.Extended description: Several kinds of tissue characterize cayenne pepper; all have low birefringence with indices around 1.53. Calcium oxalate crystals (486) (001000) are scattered throughout the tissues; indices are 1.49 (alpha) to 1.65 (gamma). The cells and tissues include: 1. Subrectangular cells, usually in rows of six. The translucent, yellow to red-orange cells are about 15 X 25 X 60 µm and have thick walls (011000). 2. Parenchyma. These translucent, yellowish to red-orange, rounded cells have low birefringence, are 30-85 µm long, 15-20 µm wide and 15-20 µm thick. These cells contain "sandy" calcium oxalate (001000), oil droplets and yellow-red pigment bodies (011000). 3. Thin-walled, almost isotropic, transparent cells, 1000 X 300 X 150 µm. Despite their size, these colorless cells are very light after drying (001010). 4. Very characteristic cells with heavy, wavy, birefringent walls; the yellowish cells are 30-90 µm long, 15-60 µm wide and 30 µm thick (011000). 5. Thin-walled, polygonal-tabular cells. Yellowish with low birefringence, these extremely characteristic cells show 15-30 µm diameters. These are the cells which secrete capsaicin, the pungent principle of cayenne pepper. Among the oil droplets usually associated with these cells, one may see crystalline plates of capsaicin (m.p. 65°C) (011000). 6. Seed fragments. The outer layer is very characteristic, consisting of coarsely wrinkled cells with wavy, heavy walls. The yellow, birefringent cells are rounded and irregular in outline (011000).

records.microscopy description: Transparent to translucent, mostly colorless (to yellowish) sheets of tissue with large, rounded (30-50 µm) to approximately rectangular (15 X 50 µm) cells (001010, 011010). The surface has a knobby appearance, the knobs being 1-3 µm in diameter. Broken fragments are equant (001000, 011000). Transparent to translucent, colorless, highly birefringent fragments of undeveloped egg shell. This sample does, in fact, show individual grains and agglomerates of starch (001000).
records.Extended description: This feed consists of the wholesome parts of slaughtered poultry which have been cleaned, dry-rendered and ground. The parts include heads, feet, undeveloped eggs, intestines and gizzards; feathers and intestinal tract contents are not included. There are two major components in this sample: 1. Transparent to translucent, mostly colorless (to yellowish) sheets of tissue with large, rounded (30-50 µm) to approximately rectangular (15 X 50 µm) cells (001010, 011010). The surface has a knobby appearance, the knobs being 1-3 µm in diameter. Broken fragments are equant (001000, 011000). 2. Transparent to translucent, colorless, highly birefringent fragments of undeveloped egg shell. See chicken egg-shell (302) (001000). This component appears intimately mixed with the other tissues. Good factory practice dictates that only a trace of in testinal contents be included in this product. This sample does, in fact, show individual grains and agglomerates of starch (001000).

records.microscopy description: Large, thin, transparent and colorless, somewhat elongated plates averaging 120 µm in length (20-350 µm). They are moderately birefringent; Transparent, colorless, isotropic cubes averaging 100 µm across (50-215 µm).
records.Extended description: This pudding mix has five components: I. Cornstarch (344). About 55% of the sample (001000). 2. Sucrose (351). About 20% of the sample (001000). 3. Dextrose (313). Large, thin, transparent and colorless, somewhat elongated plates averaging 120 µm in length (20-350 µm). They are moderately birefringent; the indices are 1.529 (alpha) to 1.566 (gamma). About 20% of the sample (001010). 4. Sodium chloride (336). Transparent, colorless, isotropic cubes averaging 100 µm across (50-215 µm). About 3% of the sample (000000). 5. Colorless, translucent, spherical particles of mono-calcium phosphate monohydrate. This "spray-dried phosphate," averaging 50 µm in width (10-148 µm), has indices of about 1.50. About 2% of the sample (000000).

records.microscopy description: rice hull dust | Rice hulls yield a variety of characteristic particles: I. Individual cells are translucent, colorless to brownish gray (due to light scatter) with first-order interference colors. Individual "strings" of the woven bamboolike structure are about 3 µm wide and have low birefringence. Flat, rectangular, serrated, epidermal cells of low bi-refringence. They are transparent and colorless (001010). These are hollow, slightly curved, birefringent cones, 32 µm wide at the base and 400 µm long;
records.Extended description: Rice hulls yield a variety of characteristic particles: I. Square and rectangular fragments of tissue which tend to be "stringy" like celery or broken bamboo. They have a woven appearance. Individual cells are translucent, colorless to brownish gray (due to light scatter) with first-order interference colors. Individual "strings" of the woven bamboolike structure are about 3 µm wide and have low birefringence. 2. Flat, rectangular, serrated, epidermal cells of low bi-refringence. They are transparent and colorless (001010). 3. Trichomes, or plant hairs. These are hollow, slightly curved, birefringent cones, 32 µm wide at the base and 400 µm long; the surfaces are smooth (001001). 4. Rice starch grains (346) (001000) occur both individually and in small agglomerates.

records.microscopy description: salt dust | Their yellowish color is then due to light scattering by the optical discontinuities within the particle.
records.Extended description: Pure salt fragments are whole and broken, transparent, colorless, isotropic cubes of sodium chloride (n = 1.544). This is table salt, distinguished from pure, reagent grade sodium chloride by the presence of other components. The birefringent rhombs are calcium sulfate, gypsum (151), a natural impurity commonly associated with salt when it is mined. The gypsum crystals often dehydrate during heating of the Aroclor® preparation and become anhydrite (116) or plaster of Paris (532), pseudomorphs of gypsum. Their yellowish color is then due to light scattering by the optical discontinuities within the particle. These effects are best shown with slightly uncrossed polars. Manufacturers may add small amounts of sodium carbonate (339) or trisodium phosphate (271, 272) to combine with hygroscopic impurities such as calcium and magnesium chloride. Other compounds sometimes added are sodium silicoaluminate and, in the case of "iodized" table salt, potassium iodide.

records.microscopy description: seed-cleaning dust | Most of the particles in this sample are colorless to yellow, irregular bits of torn tissue (011000); these transparent, almost isotropic fragments average 10 µm across (1-25 µm). Polygonal starch grains are also present (001000), as well as cells, some of which have serrated walls. Smooth, birefringent trichomes, both straight and curved, usually appear; these are 3 µm wide (1-5 µm) and 30 µm long (10-100 µm) (001001). The presence of trichomes, starch grains, spiral cells and cells with serrated edges indicates that a cereal grain was being cleaned.

records.microscopy description: It is monoclinic, crystallizing as colorless, birefringent prisms (001001), tablets (001010) or equant crystals (001000).
records.Extended description: Sodium bicarbonate is moderately soluble in water and slightly soluble in alcohol. It is monoclinic, crystallizing as colorless, birefringent prisms (001001), tablets (001010) or equant crystals (001000). Cleavage is good along some directions, but ground crystals show considerable conchoidal fracture. The crystals are soft (Moh 2.5) with a specific gravity of 2.21. Sodium bicarbonate loses CO2 and is converted to sodium carbonate (339) at 270°C. The refractive indices are 1.380 (alpha), 1.500 (beta), 1.586 (gamma); (-) 0.206. X- and Y-shaped twins, common in these crystals, may easily be identified by the unexpected property that all portions go to extinction simultaneously.

records.microscopy description: It forms colorless, transparent, birefringent, equant crystals, sometimes showing lamellar twinning.
records.Extended description: Sodium carbonate is moderately soluble in water, slightly soluble in absolute alcohol and insoluble in acetone. It forms colorless, transparent, birefringent, equant crystals, sometimes showing lamellar twinning. Cleavage is poor, and ground crystals are unevenly fractured. The crystals are hygroscopic; specific gravity is 2.532. Sodium carbonate begins to lose CO2 at 400°C. The refractive indices are 1.415 (alpha), 1.535 (beta), 1.546 (gamma); (-) 0.131.

records.microscopy description: It is orthorhombic and forms colorless, birefringent, slightly flattened or elongated, equant crystals.
records.Extended description: Hydrated sodium carbonate crystallizes from water above 32 °C. It is soluble in water and slightly soluble in glycerin but insoluble in other organic solvents. It is orthorhombic and forms colorless, birefringent, slightly flattened or elongated, equant crystals. Cleavage is not pronounced, and ground crystals are irregularly fractured. The crystals are soft (Moh 1.5) and deliquescent with a specific gravity of 2.25. The monohydrate dehydrates at about 100°C or higher to give an anhydrous pseudomorph which breaks up into a fine powder in Aroclor®, especially if the cover slip is used to shear the prep. The refractive indices of the monohydrate are 1.420 (alpha), 1.506 (beta), 1.524 (gamma); (-) 0.104.

records.microscopy description: This ground grain sorghum feed consists of several distinguishing particles: 1. The 3-15 µm diameter starch grains bear a very strong resemblance to cornstarch (344), but they are not quite so polygonal and the internal air bubble is more dotlike, less stellate (001000). The individual grains and agglomerates of this component make up 90% of the sample. The outer coat consists of brown, reddish-brown, deep red, yellow or mottled tissue made up of 15-20 µm wide elongated cells with low birefringence (011010); fragments are equant and highly colored (011000). Starch grains are embedded in this tissue.
records.Extended description: This ground grain sorghum feed consists of several distinguishing particles: 1. Starch. The 3-15 µm diameter starch grains bear a very strong resemblance to cornstarch (344), but they are not quite so polygonal and the internal air bubble is more dotlike, less stellate (001000). The individual grains and agglomerates of this component make up 90% of the sample. 2. The outer coat consists of brown, reddish-brown, deep red, yellow or mottled tissue made up of 15-20 µm wide elongated cells with low birefringence (011010); fragments are equant and highly colored (011000). Starch grains are embedded in this tissue. 3. Transparent, colorless, weakly birefringent tissue made up of generally rounded, 15 µm cells (001010). Under a stereomicroscope, the color of the outer coat may be seen to leach down into the starchy endosperm. The red color will leach out into a chloral hydrate mount.

records.microscopy description: soybean dust | The particles in this sample average 190 µm across (less than 5 to more than 2000 µm). They include cells, tissues and starch grains, all with low birefringence and refractive indices of about 1.53. Transparent to translucent, colorless, polygonal, prismatic cells, 7-20 µm wide and 45-60 µm high. Colorless, transparent, I-shaped cells. Almost isotropic, these are 40-120 µm high, 18-30 µm wide in the middle and 30-40 µm wide at top and bottom (001001). Flattened, isotropic, baggy cells.
records.Extended description: The particles in this sample average 190 µm across (less than 5 to more than 2000 µm). They include cells, tissues and starch grains, all with low birefringence and refractive indices of about 1.53. Calcium oxalate crystals (486) (001000) are found throughout the tissues; their indices are 1.49 (alpha) to 1.65 (gamma). The four main components are: 1. Transparent to translucent, colorless, polygonal, prismatic cells, 7-20 µm wide and 45-60 µm high. The walls are thick and pitted. Birefringence is low (001001). 2. Colorless, transparent, I-shaped cells. Almost isotropic, these are 40-120 µm high, 18-30 µm wide in the middle and 30-40 µm wide at top and bottom (001001). 3. Flattened, isotropic, baggy cells. They are colorless and transparent (000010). 4. Starch grains. These rounded particles are about 8 µm in diameter. Between crossed polars, they are gray with a well-marked black cross. records.microscopy description: These are transparent, colorless, ovoid to ellipsoid bodies with one or more small tuberosities on the surface of each. The grains are 7-75 µm long, but the average length is more commonly 30-45 µm. The usual internal air bubble is present as a cleft, often resembling the wings of a bat in flight and usually at the broader end of the grain. Very faint striations may be apparent on the surfaces. Between crossed polars, each grain appears gray with a well-marked black cross. Arrowroot starch grains do not usually form agglomerates, but, when they do, the agglomerates are simple.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless, polyhedral or subspherical grains are 5-15 µm in diameter (though they may be as wide as 25 µm). An air bubble is usually observed in each starch grain as a central triangular or two- to five-pointed split. The surface is smooth. Between crossed polars, the grains appear gray with well-marked black crosses.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless, polyhedral or subspherical grains are 5-15 µm in diameter (though they may be as wide as 25 µm). An air bubble is usually observed in each starch grain as a central triangular or two- to five-pointed split. The surface is smooth. There is usually no agglomeration, but some simple agglomerates may be found in commercial cornstarch. Between crossed polars, the grains appear gray with well-marked black crosses. Cornstarch is obtained from Zea mays. The refractive index is about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless grains look like potatoes -ovoid, irregularly ovoid or subspherical and somewhat flattened. They average 25 µm in length (15-65 µm) although ovoid grains may be 30-100 µm long; rounded grains are 10-35 µm across. A dark, triangular air bubble usually appears at one end of the grain, generally one-third to one-fourth eccentric. Striations on the smooth surface, when seen, are concentric and well marked; Between crossed polars, the grain is gray to white with a well-marked black cross.

There is little tendency to agglomeration; when it does occur, each group has only two to three components. The refractive index is about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: These smooth, transparent, colorless, polyhedral grains are 3-12 µm in diameter though the most common size range is 5-8 µm. A very tiny air bubble appears in most of the grains. The starch grains tend to form ovate, compound agglomerates of 2 to more than 150 components; these groups are 7-20 X 12-30 µm. Between crossed polars, the grains appear gray with a well-marked black cross (346B).

The cross is not seen in plane polarized light (346A). In actual practice, of course, one changes from plane polarized light to crossed polars frequently, or one may scan the preparation between slightly uncrossed polars.

records.microscopy description: The transparent, colorless, subspherical grains of tapioca starch are usually nearly spherical but sometimes resemble mullers or pestles and round-bottomed cups or kettles. The air bubble characteristic of starch grains is round, stellate or linear, and either centered or as much as one-half eccentric. Striations on the smooth surface, if seen, are concentric. These grains fall into two size groups: large, 25-35 µm; small, 5-12 µm (or even 5-25 µm). Between crossed polars, the grain appears gray with a well-marked black cross.

Striations on the smooth surface, if seen, are concentric. These grains fall into two size groups: large, 25-35 µm; small, 5-12 µm (or even 5-25 µm). Between crossed polars, the grain appears gray with a well-marked black cross. The refractive index is about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: These are transparent, colorless particles of cornstarch (344). In this sample, the transparent to translucent clumps average 90 µm across (20-200 µm); they are colorless to milk-white in reflected light.
records.Extended description: These are transparent, colorless particles of cornstarch (344). Tortilla flour differs from ordinary cornstarch in the presence of agglomerates. In this sample, the transparent to translucent clumps average 90 µm across (20-200 µm); they are colorless to milk-white in reflected light. The sample is essentially corn meal (310).

records.microscopy description: Wheat starch grains are transparent, colorless and lenticular; they are oval, circular or subreniform in outline. The grains in this sample average 10 µm in length (3-25 µm), but larger grains may be as long as 50 µm. The grains tend, to form agglomerates averaging 40 µm across (25-100 µm). The air bubble characteristic of most starch grains is a central point which looks like a line when the grain is on edge. When striations can be seen on the smooth surface, they are faintly concentric.
records.Extended description: Wheat starch grains are transparent, colorless and lenticular; they are oval, circular or subreniform in outline. The grains in this sample average 10 µm in length (3-25 µm), but larger grains may be as long as 50 µm. The grains tend, to form agglomerates averaging 40 µm across (25-100 µm). The air bubble characteristic of most starch grains is a central point which looks like a line when the grain is on edge. When striations can be seen on the smooth surface, they are faintly concentric. Between crossed polars, the grain appears gray with a faint black cross; grains on edge show a cross shaped like two Y's joined in line at the tails, a phenomenon peculiar to wheat starch. The refractive index is about 1.53. In wheat flour, small agglomerates as well as bits of tissue which originally held the starch grains in place are common. These wall segments resemble, of all things, perlite (350).

records.microscopy description: The particles in this sample, however, are less rounded, and there are fewer starch grains. In reflected light, the sample is colorless to milk-white, yellow in large fragments. The particle size range here is 10-250+ µm.
records.Extended description: This sample consists of the same kinds of cells and tissues described under soybean (342), q.v. The particles in this sample, however, are less rounded, and there are fewer starch grains. In reflected light, the sample is colorless to milk-white, yellow in large fragments. Oil droplets can be seen in many of the cells. The particle size range here is 10-250+ µm. Unlike the animal feed described earlier (342), this is an air filter sample taken in a soybean processing area.

records.microscopy description: It is monoclinic and crystallizes from water as colorless, transparent, birefringent, thick tablets. The crystals, which may be equant (001000) or flakelike (001010), have a specific gravity of 1.588.
records.Extended description: Sucrose is highly soluble in water, slightly soluble in methanol, very slightly soluble in ethanol and insoluble in ether or chloroform. It is monoclinic and crystallizes from water as colorless, transparent, birefringent, thick tablets. Some cleavage is evident, but the ground crystals are conchoidally fractured. The crystals, which may be equant (001000) or flakelike (001010), have a specific gravity of 1.588. Sucrose melts with decomposition at 160-190°C, depending on the heating rate. The refractive indices are 1.540 (alpha), 1.567 (beta), 1.572 (gamma); (-) 0.028.

records.microscopy description: This air filter sample from a sugar company contains three principle kinds of particles: 1. Transparent to translucent, colorless tissue made up of thin-walled, weakly birefringent cells which are irregular in outline and of variable size (001010). They are composed of birefringent rings about 20 µm in diameter (001001).
records.Extended description: This air filter sample from a sugar company contains three principle kinds of particles: 1. Transparent to translucent, colorless tissue made up of thin-walled, weakly birefringent cells which are irregular in outline and of variable size (001010). 2. As above but dark yellow to orange-brown, light and dark brown (011010)-about 50% of the sample. 3. Spiral vessels that look like windpipes. They are composed of birefringent rings about 20 µm in diameter (001001). Cf. beet pulp (297). This sample contains some combustion products.

records.microscopy description: tea dust | Leaf fragments, roughly rounded, in which cell structure and vessels are evident. The translucent yellow to dark reddish brown particles are isotropic but appear birefringent due to well-defined, scattered calcium oxalate (486) rosettes (a= 1.49, gamma = 1.65) (001000). If the fragments are 8 µm or less in diameter, they look like transparent, colorless, smooth, rounded flakes (010010). These are transparent, colorless to very pale yellow, unicellular, thick-walled, conical to linear hairs with a clubfootlike base and a rounded point; They are 9-13 µm wide at the base and 200-300 µm long. These highly irregular cylindrical bodies have many rounded protuberances at angles to the main body.
records.Extended description: Tea dust has four identifying components: 1. Leaf fragments, roughly rounded, in which cell structure and vessels are evident. The translucent yellow to dark reddish brown particles are isotropic but appear birefringent due to well-defined, scattered calcium oxalate (486) rosettes (a= 1.49, gamma = 1.65) (001000). Individual cells are difficult to discern; cell boundaries are not distinct. If the fragments are 8 µm or less in diameter, they look like transparent, colorless, smooth, rounded flakes (010010). 2. Trichomes. These are transparent, colorless to very pale yellow, unicellular, thick-walled, conical to linear hairs with a clubfootlike base and a rounded point; they are hollow and may trap air. They are 9-13 µm wide at the base and 200-300 µm long. Between crossed polars, the hairs are gray, white and first-order yellow (001001, 011001). 3. Idioblasts. These highly irregular cylindrical bodies have many rounded protuberances at angles to the main body. Some idioblasts are suggestive of dendritic structures or of pieces of jigsaw puzzle; others resemble spiked horns. The wide lumen extends through the body and protuberances; the wall of the idioblast has uniform thickness. The transparent, colorless to pale yellow structures are about 25 X 200 µm and birefringent (gray, white, first-order yellow). They are found free and embedded in leaf tissue (001001, 011001). and are birefringent (001001). The trichomes and idioblasts are by far the most characteristic features of this sample. The indices of all tissues are about 1.53.

records.microscopy description: Under high magnification, the skins are yellow to yellow-green, polygonal, thick-walled cells of low bire-fringence (0ll010).
records.Extended description: This sample consists of the stems, seeds, trim, skins and pulp waste from the tomato juice and canning industries. It is used primarily in dog food. Under the stereomicroscope, the skins are a vivid yellow and curled like a manu-script roll. Under high magnification, the skins are yellow to yellow-green, polygonal, thick-walled cells of low bire-fringence (0ll010). If air is entrapped in the cells, the appearance is that of leopard skin. This sample also contains shredded bits of woody stems (001001) and pulp fragments (001000), but the skins are the identifying

records.microscopy description: walnut shell dust | These are irregular, rounded fragments of colorless (000000) to yellow, orange and brown cells and tissue (010000, 0ll000). Most of the cells are equant; The transparent, almost isotropic particles are 40 µm across (5-90 µm).
records.Extended description: These are irregular, rounded fragments of colorless (000000) to yellow, orange and brown cells and tissue (010000, 0ll000). Most of the cells are equant; some have rather thin walls which are slightly concave. The transparent, almost isotropic particles are 40 µm across (5-90 µm). The refractive indices are about 1.53. Tiny fragments of calcium oxalate (486) are scattered throughout this sample (001000).

records.microscopy description: wheat grain dust | This sample consists of several kinds of particles: 1. Birefringent, rectangular epidermal cells 12-35 µm wide and 40- 180 µm long resemble the sclerids of coffee chaff (307). They are thick walled, colorless to yellow, slightly and unevenly lignified and usually parallel to each other on a thin outer skin; Fairly thick walled, pitted and beaded, these almost isotropic cells are 10-15 µm wide, 80-95 µm long; they are colorless and transparent (001000). Transparent, colorless, tubular, isotropic cells.
records.Extended description: This sample consists of several kinds of particles: 1. Birefringent, rectangular epidermal cells 12-35 µm wide and 40- 180 µm long resemble the sclerids of coffee chaff (307). They are thick walled, colorless to yellow, slightly and unevenly lignified and usually parallel to each other on a thin outer skin; Pits make them appear beaded (001000, 0ll000). 2. Transverse or cross cells. Fairly thick walled, pitted and beaded, these almost isotropic cells are 10-15 µm wide, 80-95 µm long; they are colorless and transparent (001000). 3. Transparent, colorless, tubular, isotropic cells. They are 10-15 µm wide, 175-250 µm long (000001). 4. Trichomes or hairs. These smooth, elongated, hollow, transparent, colorless cones taper to a point at the free end. They average 15 µm wide (10-20 µm) and 200 µm long (25-500 µm). The hairs may, however, average as long as 250 µm (25-1000 µm). They show gray to white birefringence (001001).

records.microscopy description: calcined alumina dust
records.Extended description: Precipitated hydrated aluminum oxide is calcined to drive off water and obtain the anhydrous oxide. This sample shows at least three solid phases: one, the oxide corundum with indices higher than Aroclor® (1.66) (001100); two, a hydrous oxide showing indices almost the same as Aroclor® (yellow to orange dispersion staining colors in all orientations with the annular stop (001000) ; and three, an oxide with even more water is indicated by a refractive index considerably less than 1.66 (about 1.58)(001000).

records.microscopy description: aluminum manufacturing dust | This sample, collected from the scrubber of a plant that produces aluminum by the Harvey process, shows a large quantity of graphite (389) (100000, 100010) from the anodes and collection cells, some cryolite (139) (000000) which is used as a flux in this process, alumina (corundum, 137), (001100), and transparent, colorless, equant, tri-clinic fragments of anhydrous aluminum fluoride (001000).
records.Extended description: This sample, collected from the scrubber of a plant that produces aluminum by the Harvey process, shows a large quantity of graphite (389) (100000, 100010) from the anodes and collection cells, some cryolite (139) (000000) which is used as a flux in this process, alumina (corundum, 137), (001100), and transparent, colorless, equant, tri-clinic fragments of anhydrous aluminum fluoride (001000). The indices of AlF 3 are about 1.45; the density has been reported as 3.07 and as 2.882. The substance sublimes at about 1260°C without melting; it is slightly soluble in water and insoluble in most organic solvents. It is used in the aluminum production process to lower the melting point of the electrolyte and increase its conductivity.

records.microscopy description: These opaque, silvery ribbons (100011), slivers (100001) and equant pieces (100000) of metal are sawtoothed to irregularly jagged. The surfaces of the sheared metal fragments show numerous, close parallel lines. Bits of the white metal less than 8 µm across lack the high reflectivity of the larger pieces; they appear black and may be mistaken for other kinds of particles. The electron or ion microprobe is required to determine the exact composition when only a single particle is available.
records.Extended description: These opaque, silvery ribbons (100011), slivers (100001) and equant pieces (100000) of metal are sawtoothed to irregularly jagged. The surfaces of the sheared metal fragments show numerous, close parallel lines. Bits of the white metal less than 8 µm across lack the high reflectivity of the larger pieces; they appear black and may be mistaken for other kinds of particles. Top light and rotation of the stage are essential with metal samples of this kind. The electron or ion microprobe is required to determine the exact composition when only a single particle is available. The specific gravity is 2.702, and the melting point is 659.7°C.

records.microscopy description: Carbon graphite (389) (100000) in apparent flakes and agglomerates of tiny, opaque, black, rounded grains. A second component appears to be agglomerates of tiny, transparent grains with indices sometimes higher than Aroclor®, sometimes lower, and sometimes both; the grains sometimes seem moderately birefringent, sometimes almost isotropic. Transparent, colorless, rounded grains (less than 2 µm wide) of synthetic cryolite (139) (000000). Transparent, colorless, rounded chips and equant fragments of alumina (00ll00).
records.Extended description: This is a representative sample of the slag-actually the electrolyte-from the collecting vessel of an aluminum-producing cell. 1. Carbon graphite (389) (100000) in apparent flakes and agglomerates of tiny, opaque, black, rounded grains. These make up about 45% of the sample. A second component appears to be agglomerates of tiny, transparent grains with indices sometimes higher than Aroclor®, sometimes lower, and sometimes both; the grains sometimes seem moderately birefringent, sometimes almost isotropic. Actually, these are alumina chips thoroughly cov- 2. Transparent, colorless, rounded grains (less than 2 µm wide) of synthetic cryolite (139) (000000). The indices are 1.337 (alpha) to 1.338 (gamma); (+) 0.00ll. 3. Transparent, colorless, rounded chips and equant fragments of alumina (00ll00). The indices are 1.768 (omega) to 1.760 (epsilon); (-) 0.008. See corundum (137).

records.microscopy description: About 80% of this sample, a smelting fume, consists of mostly 1 µm (<0.5-3 µm), transparent to opaque, yellowish to dark orange-brown, round to almost rounded, isotropic particles with an index greater than 1.66 (010100, ll0000). These form frequent agglomerates to 10+ µm. Transparent, colorless, well-formed, isotropic octahedra, with an index greater than 1.66, these are mostly 4 µm (000100) and comprise 15% of the sample. Transparent, yellowish, 0.8 µm wide needles up to 15+ µm long, with an index greater than 1.66 (010101), comprise another 5% of the sample.
records.Extended description: About 80% of this sample, a smelting fume, consists of mostly 1 µm (<0.5-3 µm), transparent to opaque, yellowish to dark orange-brown, round to almost rounded, isotropic particles with an index greater than 1.66 (010100, ll0000). These form frequent agglomerates to 10+ µm. Transparent, colorless, well-formed, isotropic octahedra, with an index greater than 1.66, these are mostly 4 µm (000100) and comprise 15% of the sample. Transparent, yellowish, 0.8 µm wide needles up to 15+ µm long, with an index greater than 1.66 (010101), comprise another 5% of the sample.

records.microscopy description: About 70% of this sample consists of 25 µm (5-65 µm), opaque, black, magnetic, relatively smooth metallic spheres (100000).
records.Extended description: About 70% of this sample consists of 25 µm (5-65 µm), opaque, black, magnetic, relatively smooth metallic spheres (100000). The remaining particles are transparent, red, rounded fragments (most are less than 1 µm in diameter) of red iron oxide (223,390,391)(0lllO0).

records.microscopy description: The smaller particles are shiny silvery alloy spheres. The larger particles appear to be sintered small spheres with a corresponding pebbly surface and major protuberances. Reflectivity is high even though the surfaces are softly granular.
records.Extended description: The smaller particles are shiny silvery alloy spheres. The larger particles appear to be sintered small spheres with a corresponding pebbly surface and major protuberances. Reflectivity is high even though the surfaces are softly granular. This sample, collected from a cyclone collector exit, is about 60% Bi, 40% Cd.

records.microscopy description: blast furnace dust | Opaque, black, sharp fragments of pig iron. They are magnetic with finely granular surfaces (100000). Transparent, colorless, rhombohedra and rounded equant particles of limestone (161) (001000).
records.Extended description: An electrical precipitator yielded this sample. Its components are: 1. Opaque, black, sharp fragments of pig iron. They are magnetic with finely granular surfaces (100000). These fragments make up about 15% of the sample. 2. Transparent, red, rounded grains (less than 2 µm across) of red iron oxide (223,390,391) (011100). They are about 40% of the sample. 3. Opaque, black, rough fragments of magnetic iron oxide (165, 407) (100000). Most are partially or completely covered with component 2. These also make up about 40% of the sample. 4. Transparent, colorless, rhombohedra and rounded equant particles of limestone (161) (001000). Many of these are also covered with component 2. They comprise about 5% of the sample. Quartz particles (183) are present (001000) in a trace quantity.

records.microscopy description: Their outlines are rough and sharp to relatively smooth; the surfaces are finely granular to coarse and pitted (100000). It occurs here in both transparent, deep red, rounded particles (011100) and larger, black, opaque, equant particles with granular surfaces (100000). Transparent, colorless rhombohedra, rounded equant fragments and microcrystalline aggregates of limestone (161) (001000). Transparent, colorless, vitreous, rounded, smooth, equant particles of slag (418). The isotropic particles have a lower index than Aroclor® but show considerable strain birefringence (000000).
records.Extended description: The four components of this sample are: 1. Opaque, black, equant fragments of magnetic iron oxide, Fe30 4 (165, 407). Their outlines are rough and sharp to relatively smooth; the surfaces are finely granular to coarse and pitted (100000). 2. Red iron oxide (223, 390, 391). It occurs here in both transparent, deep red, rounded particles (011100) and larger, black, opaque, equant particles with granular surfaces (100000). 3. Transparent, colorless rhombohedra, rounded equant fragments and microcrystalline aggregates of limestone (161) (001000). 4. Transparent, colorless, vitreous, rounded, smooth, equant particles of slag (418). The isotropic particles have a lower index than Aroclor® but show considerable strain birefringence (000000).

records.microscopy description: Transparent, colorless to yellow and brown, rounded and sharply angular particles of vitreous slag (see also 418) with indices slightly less than Aroclor®. Most of the particles are isotropic, but many have strain birefringence. Opaque, black, rough, magnetic fragments of iron (392) (100000).
records.Extended description: The principal constituents are: 1. Transparent, colorless to yellow and brown, rounded and sharply angular particles of vitreous slag (see also 418) with indices slightly less than Aroclor®. Most of the particles are isotropic, but many have strain birefringence. Most also show dispersion staining colors (orange). Many include air bubbles, some in parallel rows. These silicates of variable composition are about 90% of the sample (000000, 010000). 2. Opaque, black, rough, magnetic fragments of iron (392) (100000). They comprise about 2% of the sample. 3. Transparent, deep red, equant fragments of iron oxide (223, 390, 391) (011100). These make up about 1 % of the sample.

records.microscopy description: This common furnace product, collected from a brass melting induction furnace, consists of transparent, colorless, rounded grains less than 1 µm in diameter; These particles are so small, however, that they appear virtually opaque. In precise focus, they appear black because of the high contrast and small size; A particular particle will change from white to black to white as the microscope passes through the position of best focus. In spite of their small size, they are birefringent enough to show low-order white polarization colors.
records.Extended description: This common furnace product, collected from a brass melting induction furnace, consists of transparent, colorless, rounded grains less than 1 µm in diameter; agglomerates, when they occur, are simple. X-ray diffraction data indicate the major component is ZnO (zincite, 211). The indices are 2.013 (omega) to 2.029 (epsilon); (+) 0.016. These particles are so small, however, that they appear virtually opaque. In precise focus, they appear black because of the high contrast and small size; slightly out of focus, they appear white. A particular particle will change from white to black to white as the microscope passes through the position of best focus. In spite of their small size, they are birefringent enough to show low-order white polarization colors.

records.microscopy description: These opaque, shiny yellow metal flakes (110010) and clumps (110000) have irregular and rounded jagged outlines; the surfaces are rough to coarsely granular. if a bit of metal less than 10 µm wide appears opaque black even with top light and complete rotation of the stage, "rolling" the particle in the medium by sliding the cover slip will usually bring it to a position where it will show a pinpoint of reflected light. The electron or ion microprobe is required to determine the exact composition when only a single particle is available.
records.Extended description: These opaque, shiny yellow metal flakes (110010) and clumps (110000) have irregular and rounded jagged outlines; the surfaces are rough to coarsely granular. Reflectivity is moderately high; if a bit of metal less than 10 µm wide appears opaque black even with top light and complete rotation of the stage, "rolling" the particle in the medium by sliding the cover slip will usually bring it to a position where it will show a pinpoint of reflected light. The electron or ion microprobe is required to determine the exact composition when only a single particle is available.

records.microscopy description: The opaque, elongated globules of shiny yellow metal which make up this sample have generally smooth, rounded outlines with some sharp points and jagged edges. Surfaces are smooth to softly granular; Bits of the metal less than 1 µm across are easily overlooked, but many may be spotted by tilting the mirror to get a modified darkfield through extreme oblique illumination.
records.Extended description: The opaque, elongated globules of shiny yellow metal which make up this sample have generally smooth, rounded outlines with some sharp points and jagged edges. Surfaces are smooth to softly granular; reflectivity is moderately high. Bits of the metal less than 1 µm across are easily overlooked, but many may be spotted by tilting the mirror to get a modified darkfield through extreme oblique illumination. Tilting the mirror in this way produced pinpoints of reflected yellowish light on a dark field. Bronzes, i.e., Cu-Sn alloys, usually have densities of about 8.8.

records.microscopy description: In this sample, individual carbon particles are <0.5-10 µm, mostly 0.5-4 µm. Only particles less than 0.5 µm are rounded. Most of the particles are sharply angular (100000);
records.Extended description: Carbon black is produced by the vapor-phase decomposition of, for example, an oil feedstock composed of a mixture of substituted aromatic hydrocarbons. The refractory conditions are controlled to produce different kinds of carbon black. In this sample, individual carbon particles are <0.5-10 µm, mostly 0.5-4 µm. Only particles less than 0.5 µm are rounded. Most of the particles are sharply angular (100000); many are sliver like (100001); some are platelike (100010). There are no apparent agglomerates (cf. 371, 372).

records.microscopy description: This sample, apparently a furnace carbon, consists of individual, opaque, black, rounded particles, <0.5-80 µm.
records.Extended description: This sample, apparently a furnace carbon, consists of individual, opaque, black, rounded particles, <0.5-80 µm. They are soft and easily broken (cf. 370, 372). The specific gravity is 1.8-2.1.

records.microscopy description: Channel (or impingement) carbon is produced by burning natural gas or natural gas containing oil vapors in a multitude of small flames whose tops impinge on the surface of the channel. High volatile content is accompanied by high surface area. This sample consists of individual, opaque, black, generally rounded aggregates <0.5-100 1.tm.
records.Extended description: Channel (or impingement) carbon is produced by burning natural gas or natural gas containing oil vapors in a multitude of small flames whose tops impinge on the surface of the channel. The resulting sooty product normally has a volatile content of about 5% but may be as much as 17%. High volatile content is accompanied by high surface area. This sample consists of individual, opaque, black, generally rounded aggregates <0.5-100 1.tm. They are soft and easily broken and smeared (due to oil) (cf. 370, 371).

records.microscopy description: calcined clay dust | Transparent, colorless to gray, rounded grains and agglomerates of grains which look like snowballs under top light. The grains are isotropic or have very low birefringence; Colorless, transparent, isotropic, glassy spheres with an index of about 1.57.
records.Extended description: The major constituents of this sample are: 1. Transparent, colorless to gray, rounded grains and agglomerates of grains which look like snowballs under top light. The grains are isotropic or have very low birefringence; their indices are about 1.57 (000000, 001000). 2. Colorless, transparent, isotropic, glassy spheres with an index of about 1.57. Many include debris and gas bubbles (000000).

records.microscopy description: Chamotte, or ceramic grog, consists of transparent, colorless (000000) (and colored, 010000), isotropic, generally rounded particles with an index of about 1.56. The largest particles here are about 3 µm across; most are less than 1 µm in diameter.
records.Extended description: Chamotte, or ceramic grog, consists of transparent, colorless (000000) (and colored, 010000), isotropic, generally rounded particles with an index of about 1.56. The largest particles here are about 3 µm across; most are less than 1 µm in diameter. Magnifications around 1000X are necessary for this sample.

records.microscopy description: The particles are much less than 1 µm in diameter and show no indication of shape. Both single particles and agglomerates are black and opaque. This is typical of foundry fumes which may be recognizable as such by the small individual sizes of the particles making up large homogeneous agglomerates. To determine the kind of foundry usually requires the electron microprobe when only a few small particles are available.
records.Extended description: This sample (copper oxide, CuO) is from a copper foundry. The particles are much less than 1 µm in diameter and show no indication of shape. Agglomerates are common. Both single particles and agglomerates are black and opaque. This is typical of foundry fumes which may be recognizable as such by the small individual sizes of the particles making up large homogeneous agglomerates. To determine the kind of foundry usually requires the electron microprobe when only a few small particles are available.

records.microscopy description: A shiny, brownish gold characterizes these opaque, sharply jagged bits of metal. Their surfaces are sharply rough; Particles less than 10 µm across do not reveal their metallic luster or top light color unless vertical illuminators or darkfield techniques are used. What appears to be a colorless, transparent substance in the photomicrograph is simply specular reflections from small areas of the metal particles.
records.Extended description: A shiny, brownish gold characterizes these opaque, sharply jagged bits of metal. Their surfaces are sharply rough; reflectivity is good. Particles less than 10 µm across do not reveal their metallic luster or top light color unless vertical illuminators or darkfield techniques are used. What appears to be a colorless, transparent substance in the photomicrograph is simply specular reflections from small areas of the metal particles. The specific gravity of copper is 8.92, and the melting point is 1083°C.

records.microscopy description: The crystals are rounded equant and less than 2 µm wide;
records.Extended description: Composition varies in these transparent, colorless, apparently isotropic crystal fragments of Na3AlF 6. The crystals are rounded equant and less than 2 µm wide; very few look like cubes (compare with natural cryolite, 139), and those that do are best seen at 800-lO00X. The indices are 1.337 (alpha) to 1.338 (gamma); exceedingly low birefringence, (+) 0.0011. Hardness is 2.5; density is 2.97; melting point is about 1000°C. Cryolite is slightly soluble in water and insoluble in hydrochloric acid; it decomposes in alkali. Synthetic cryolite is put to the same uses as the natural product, viz., as a flux in aluminum production, in ceramics and insecticides and as a binder for abrasives. records.microscopy description: This stack sample from a silica reduction process consists of colorless, transparent, less than I µm, isotropic, apparently rounded particles of silica which may form flattened agglomerates to 20+ µm.
records.Extended description: This stack sample from a silica reduction process consists of colorless, transparent, less than I µm, isotropic, apparently rounded particles of silica which may form flattened agglomerates to 20+ µm. This sample also contains a few small bits of coal.

records.microscopy description: Opaque, rounded grains, these are peach to reddish in top light. All particles are less than 3 µm across, most less than I µm. A few of the particles are magnetic.
records.Extended description: Opaque, rounded grains, these are peach to reddish in top light. All particles are less than 3 µm across, most less than I µm. Small agglomerates are present, but they are not common. A few of the particles are magnetic. X-ray diffraction data indicate that the sample is composed of Fe3O4 and Mg2Fe2O4.

records.microscopy description: These transparent, colorless, rounded grains are less than 2 µm in diameter. The grains are creamy peach in top light, grayish brown in bulk with indices much greater than Aroclor®. One can see with high magnification nearly spherical colorless crystals and other more angular opaque crystals (100000). Both are very tiny (less than 2-3 µm) and show no interference colors.
records.Extended description: These transparent, colorless, rounded grains are less than 2 µm in diameter. The grains are creamy peach in top light, grayish brown in bulk with indices much greater than Aroclor®. One can see with high magnification nearly spherical colorless crystals and other more angular opaque crystals (100000). Both are very tiny (less than 2-3 µm) and show no interference colors. X-ray diffraction data indicate that the constituents are ZnO (432) (001100) and Fe3O4. The sample was collected from an electrostatic precipitator at a galvanizing plant.

records.microscopy description: electric furnace dust | Fine, opaque, gray-black powder in spheres less than 2 µm across, often coating other particles (100000). Besides the free particles, agglomerates seem to be trapped in a translucent, colorless to grayish yellow, isotropic, rounded, irregular matrix. The particle indices are about 1.66 (000100, 010100). Many are so densely packed that they appear completely opaque; their outlines are granular, and the surfaces are foamy to slightly rough (100000). Transparent, colorless and brown to gray, isotropic spheres of fused ash averaging 5 µm in diameter (3-50 µm).
records.Extended description: This sample has several major components: 1. Fine, opaque, gray-black powder in spheres less than 2 µm across, often coating other particles (100000). Besides the free particles, agglomerates seem to be trapped in a translucent, colorless to grayish yellow, isotropic, rounded, irregular matrix. The particle indices are about 1.66 (000100, 010100). Many are so densely packed that they appear completely opaque; their outlines are granular, and the surfaces are foamy to slightly rough (100000). 2. Transparent, colorless and brown to gray, isotropic spheres of fused ash averaging 5 µm in diameter (3-50 µm). The index is about 1.58. Many contain trapped gases (000000, 010000).

records.microscopy description: electric furnace dust (from glass melting) | Four materials commonly used in making plate glass are evident here: 1. The compound was originally anhydrous, but it has absorbed water vapor from the air to form the monohydrate. The "snow-balls" are made up of 1-3 µm, transparent, colorless, rounded, equant particles; In top light, the "snowballs" and snowlike particles are white (001000); in transmitted light, the aggregates are translucent and brownish (due to light scatter from individual particles). Transparent, colorless, isotropic, equant fragments with sharp edges, smooth faces and conchoidal fracture (000000).
records.Extended description: Four materials commonly used in making plate glass are evident here: 1. Transparent, colorless, sharp-edged, equant particles of quartz (183). The indices are 1.544 (omega) to 1.553(epsilon) ; 2. Fragments, less than 4 µm across, of birefringent calcite (133) (001000). This material is originally added as calcium oxide, but it picks up carbon dioxide from the air to form the carbonate. 3. "Snowballs" of sodium carbonate (339). The compound was originally anhydrous, but it has absorbed water vapor from the air to form the monohydrate. The "snow-balls" are made up of 1-3 µm, transparent, colorless, rounded, equant particles; these also cover the quartz in the sample like "snow." The indices are 1.420 (alpha) to 1.524 (gamma); (+) 0.104. In top light, the "snowballs" and snowlike particles are white (001000); in transmitted light, the aggregates are translucent and brownish (due to light scatter from individual particles). 4. Transparent, colorless, isotropic, equant fragments with sharp edges, smooth faces and conchoidal fracture (000000). The index is near 1.57. These are glass particles from the cullet-a small amount of broken bits always present during glass manufacture.
